title: Desktop: write log records to standard error and a rotating log file
author: switch87
body:
## Why

The desktop app never installs a logger (only the web build does, via `WebLogger`), so every `log::warn!` / `log::error!` is discarded, and start-up problems only reach `eprintln!`. A launch from a desktop menu or the Dock has no terminal, so an ordinary user has nothing to attach to an issue, and `RUST_LOG` can't help them.

We ran into this in the sister project PhotoCraft (storytold/photocraft#1143): a window that stayed empty on Linux took an hour of `WAYLAND_DEBUG` and `gdb` to understand, while the app had already logged the relevant decision to nowhere.

## What

`apps/gridcraft/src/logging.rs`, no new dependency (`log` was already a dependency of the app):

- **Two sinks:** standard error and `logs/gridcraft.log` next to `ui.json` / `prefs.json` (Linux/BSD `~/.config/gridcraft/logs`, macOS `~/Library/Application Support/GridCraft/logs`, Windows `%APPDATA%\GridCraft\logs`).
- **Rotation:** each launch moves the previous log to `gridcraft.1.log` (and that one to `.2`), so the log of a run that crashed survives the next start.
- **Bounded:** the file stops at 16 MiB with one note; records logged before the file is attached are buffered (max 512); without a file the buffer is released.
- **Levels:** `info` for `gridcraft*` targets, `warn` for everything else. `RUST_LOG` replaces this with env_logger-style directives; a trailing `*` matches a prefix.
- **`GRIDCRAFT_NO_PREFS`:** such runs log to standard error only, so test and agent runs don't rotate away the user's logs.
- **Never crash:** no `unwrap`/`expect`/indexing; an unusable directory or a failed write keeps standard error only; lock poisoning is handled.

`main.rs`: the logger is installed first, followed by a small panic hook that reports through `log::error!` (GridCraft had none, so panics caught by `Session::execute` never reached a file); the log file is attached after argument parsing so `--version` creates nothing; the three `eprintln!`s become `log::warn!` / `log::error!`. `control_server.…

title: Fix: list and render installed system fonts (#4)
author: justinjohn0306
body:
## Summary

Fixes #4. The font dropdown listed a hardcoded 17 names and cells always rendered in the built-in role font, so a font installed on the machine could not be listed or chosen. Opening an XLSX that used an installed font showed the text correctly (the file's font resolved), but the user could not pick any installed font from the UI.

## Root cause

Two defects in `crates/ui-egui`, both from one constraint:

1. The font combo iterated `ribbon::FONTS`, a fixed array of 17 names. Nothing enumerated the machine's fonts.
2. `theme::cell_family` reduced any name to one of 8 pre-bound roles, so a chosen name would have rendered as the Calibri fallback regardless.

The reason it was hardcoded: **egui panics when asked for a `FontFamily::Name` that was never bound to font data** (`epaint` `text/fonts.rs:1025`). Only the 8 built-in roles were ever bound. So a fix must both *list* installed families and *register their bytes*.

## Changes

- **New `crates/ui-egui/src/fonts.rs`** — scans the platform font folders, reads each file's `name` table with **skrifa** to catalog families/weights/styles. skrifa is already compiled transitively through epaint at the same `0.44` version, so it adds no new build. Damaged or non-font files and symlink loops yield nothing, never a panic. The scan runs on a background thread; `families()` (non-blocking) feeds the combos: the standard names first, then installed families A–Z.
- **Binding** — `theme::font_definitions(used)` binds the workbook's *installed* fonts as egui families keyed `fnt:{family}:{b|n}{i|n}`, each chained to egui's default proportional fonts so emoji/odd glyphs still render. A global bound-family registry is the safety gate; `cell_family` returns the installed family only when it is bound, else the previous bucketing, so it never names an unbound family.
- **Wiring** (`lib.rs`) — `setup_context` starts the scan; `logic()` rebinds when the workbook's `(uid, revision)` changes, with a one-frame skip-paint gate (egui a…

title: AppImage: show the app icon on Wayland (install launcher entry + icon) (#3)
author: justinjohn0306
body:
Fixes #3.

## Problem

A directly-run AppImage showed the generic Wayland placeholder in the dock/taskbar instead of the GridCraft icon.

## Why

Under Wayland the compositor **ignores the window icon a client sets** (winit's Wayland backend makes `set_window_icon` a no-op), and instead picks the dock icon by matching the window's app id — `ai.storyteller.gridcraft` — against an **installed** desktop entry whose `Icon=` resolves in the icon theme.

A directly-run AppImage exposes its `.desktop` and icons only *inside* the mounted image, so that lookup finds nothing and GNOME/KDE fall back to the generic placeholder. The deb/rpm/Flatpak packages don't have this problem because `postinst.sh` installs under `/usr/share` and refreshes the caches.

The AppImage build itself was byte-for-byte identical to the working sibling craft apps, so this is a runtime-integration gap, not a packaging-script divergence.

## Fix

Replace the bare `AppRun` symlink with a script, `packaging/linux/apprun.sh`. On launch it installs the launcher entry and the hicolor icon into the user's `$XDG_DATA_HOME` (or `~/.local/share`), then `exec`s the binary:

- rewrites `Exec`/`TryExec` to the AppImage's **absolute path** (the packaged `Exec=gridcraft %F` only works for a system install where `gridcraft` is on `PATH`), with proper desktop-entry quoting and `%`→`%%` field-code escaping;
- copies the whole hicolor icon tree so a bare `Icon=ai.storyteller.gridcraft` resolves;
- refreshes the desktop and icon caches **only when something changed**, so repeat launches are no-ops;
- is best effort (any failure still launches the app) and can be disabled with `GRIDCRAFT_SKIP_DESKTOP_INTEGRATION=1`; it skips itself under Flatpak.

## Tests

`packaging/linux/apprun-selftest.sh` exercises AppRun against a throwaway AppDir and `HOME`: the entry and icon install, `Exec`/`TryExec` point at the AppImage (including a path with a space and a literal `%`), `Icon=` stays the bare app id, a second run is idempotent…

title: Objects: anchor modes — images/charts/shapes follow cells on sort (#5)
author: justinjohn0306
body:
## Summary

Fixes #5.

Excel pins a floating object (picture, chart, shape) to the grid in one of three ways, stored in the drawing anchor's `editAs` attribute:

| Excel option | File representation |
| --- | --- |
| Move and size with cells (default) | `<xdr:twoCellAnchor>` |
| Move but don't size with cells | `<xdr:oneCellAnchor>` / `editAs="oneCell"` |
| Don't move or size with cells | `editAs="absolute"` / `<xdr:absoluteAnchor>` |

GridCraft had no such concept. On import it discarded `editAs` (and flattened every anchor kind to a plain two-cell anchor), on export it always wrote a plain `<xdr:twoCellAnchor>`, and sorting/filtering never touched an object at all — so a picture stayed where it was drawn when its row was reordered. This change makes objects honour their anchor mode, so imported workbooks sort the way Excel sorts them.

## Changes

**Model** (`crates/model/src/features.rs`)
- New `AnchorMode` enum (`MoveAndSize` / `MoveOnly` / `Absolute`) on `Anchor`, with `#[serde(default)]` so existing documents and JSON round-trip unchanged.

**XLSX** (`crates/xlsx/src/drawing.rs`)
- Read the anchor element kind and the `editAs` attribute into the mode (`oneCellAnchor` → move only, `absoluteAnchor` / `editAs="absolute"` → absolute, plain `twoCellAnchor` → move and size).
- Write the mode back out as Excel does it: a plain `twoCellAnchor`, `editAs="oneCell"`, or `editAs="absolute"`.

**Engine**
- `data.sort*` now moves objects anchored inside the sorted body along with their lines. "Move and size" objects are re-fitted to the rows/columns they land on; "move but don't size" keeps its size; "don't move or size" (absolute) stays exactly where it was.
- Structural insert/delete rows/columns honours the same rule via `shift_sheet_features` (which previously moved every object's cell unconditionally and ignored shapes entirely).
- New `object.setAnchorMode` command (`{kind, id, mode}`), matching Excel's Format ▸ Size and Properties ▸ Properties wording. `arrange.selec…

title: macOS DMG: branded window background and icon layout
author: XusBadia
body:
## What

The macOS DMG opened as a plain white Finder window. It now opens like this:

![GridCraft DMG window in Finder](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/XusBadia/gridcraft/dmg-preview/finder.png)

The icon's figure as a cover on the GridCraft colour field, GridCraft.app and the `Applications` link side by side on Paper, and a small GridCraft-specific touch: the arrow and the mono line under the title come from the app's craft. Ink, Paper and the app colour only; Inter and JetBrains Mono.

## How

Same approach as PhotoCraft's and VectorCraft's, which have landed (storytold/photocraft#1201, storytold/vectorcraft#493):

- `packaging/macos/dmg/background.svg`: the source. Its text is outlined, so rendering it needs no fonts, and the figure is an `<image>` of the existing icon in `assets/app-icon/`.
- `background.tiff`: 1x 660×400 + 2x 1320×800 in one HiDPI TIFF (16-colour palette, Deflate, sRGB; 26 KB). No paper grain: noise doesn't compress, and this keeps the binary small.
- `dmg-layout.DS_Store`: Finder's view settings (window 660×400 content, icon size 128, GridCraft.app at (326, 205), Applications at (574, 205), the background). It's named so it isn't mistaken for, or ignored like, a Finder-generated `.DS_Store`.
- `generate.py`: writes both from the SVG on any OS (`pip install 'pillow>=12' ds_store==1.3.3 mac_alias==2.2.3`, resvg on PATH). The output is byte-for-byte reproducible and carries nothing from the machine that ran it: no paths, users, disk names or volume UUIDs.
- `package.sh` copies the TIFF and the layout into the staging folder. The image is still built with `hdiutil makehybrid`, and nothing extra runs in the signing job.

## One behaviour change: the volume name drops the version

`.DS_Store` points at the background through an alias that includes the volume name. With `GridCraft <version>` Finder kept the window and icon positions but lost the background (tested). So the mounted volume is now called `GridCraft`; the DMG file name still carries t…

title: File open: report password-protected (encrypted) files clearly (#11)
author: justinjohn0306
body:
Fixes #11.

## What was happening

Excel password-protected files are not zip packages: they are CFB/OLE2 compound files (magic `D0 CF 11 E0 A1 B1 1A E1`) holding `EncryptionInfo` + `EncryptedPackage` streams. GridCraft's `sniff()` classified them as `Unknown`, but `open_bytes` still routed `.xlsx`-named bytes to the zip reader (by extension), so the user got the cryptic:

> We can't open 'secret.xlsx': the file is not a valid zip package: invalid Zip archive: Could not find EOCD

No crash and no data loss (the workbook is never modified), but no hint that the file is simply encrypted.

## The fix

- `sniff()` now recognises the CFB/OLE2 magic and returns a new `Format::Encrypted`.
- `open_bytes` short-circuits on it with a clear message: *"'…' is password-protected. GridCraft can't open encrypted workbooks yet; remove the password in Excel and try again."*

This is the detective half of the issue: the file is now identified as protected and the message says so, rather than failing as a mystery zip error.

## Tests

- `sniffing_formats` (xlsx): the full 8-byte CFB magic → `Encrypted`; a truncated CFB prefix still → `Unknown`.
- `encrypted_workbook_is_reported_not_misread` (engine): `open_bytes` on CFB bytes errors with "password-protected" and never leaks the word "zip".

## Gates

`cargo fmt`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets` (with the three lints that already fail on `main` allowed — see below), `cargo test --workspace` (all pass), `cargo xtask assets`, `cargo xtask layers`, `cargo xtask wasm`, `cargo xtask parity` all pass.

Note: `cargo xtask ci`'s clippy step fails on `main` itself under clippy 1.96 (`manual_range_contains` in `core/src/date.rs`, plus `nonminimal_bool` / `overly_complex_bool_expr` elsewhere). Those are pre-existing and unrelated to this change; verified clean with those three lints allowed.

## Scope

Full decryption (ECMA-376 agile/standard encryption: AES + SHA + HMAC, plus CFB parsing) is deliberately out of scope here — it needs new…

title: macOS: open files from Finder and `open -a` via application:openURLs:
author: smkly
body:
Same fix as the WordCraft PR: https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/pull/33

## Problem
On macOS, Finder "Open With" and double-click on a `.xlsx` show "GridCraft cannot open files in the … format". `open -a GridCraft file.xlsx` also opens nothing. File > Open and drag-and-drop work.

## Cause
GridCraft reads files to open only from argv. Finder and `open` send files through the `application:openURLs:` Apple Event on the NSApplicationDelegate. Nothing handled that method.

## Approach
- New crate `crates/macos-open` (`gridcraft-macos-open`). It adds `application:openURLs:` to the class of winit's own delegate with `class_addMethod`. It does this at `NSApplicationWillFinishLaunchingNotification`: the delegate exists, and AppKit has not yet delivered the launch documents.
- Why not a replacement delegate: winit 0.30.13 registers its own delegate in `EventLoop::new` and panics if it is replaced: `tried to get a delegate that was not the one Winit has registered`. Its doc comment that says otherwise is stale.
- `apps/gridcraft` installs the handler before `eframe::run_native`. The handler queues the paths and requests a repaint. `raw_input_hook` drains the queue through `open_path`, the same path as argv and drag-and-drop.
- No new external crates. `objc2`, `block2`, `objc2-foundation` and `objc2-app-kit` were already in `Cargo.lock`. The lockfile diff adds only the new workspace package and one dependency edge.
- `xtask/src/layers.rs` classifies `macos-open` as L6.

## Testing
- `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo xtask layers`, `cargo build --release -p gridcraft`: pass.
- `cargo xtask ci`: fmt, clippy, test, assets and layers pass. The wasm step did not run locally (no `wasm32` target installed). The new crate has only macOS-target dependencies and is not a wasm crate.
- Cold open: with the app not running, `open -a` on an `.xlsx` launched the app with that workbook open. Confirmed through the JSON control chann…

title: Preserve VBA macros + Excel-style macros UX (issue #6)
author: justinjohn0306
body:
## What

Opening a macro-enabled workbook (`.xlsm`) and saving it **silently stripped `xl/vbaProject.bin`**, turning it into a macro-free file. For anyone whose work depends on macros, that is data loss — the same class of failure as a crash, which this project ranks above feature work.

GridCraft still does **not run VBA** (its own recorded/editable scripts remain the automation path). It now **carries the project through unchanged**, so a macro-enabled workbook survives open → edit → save, and the **UI tells the user so** in an Excel-shaped surface rather than dropping the warning on the floor.

## Changes

**Engine — preserve, don't destroy**
- **model** — `Workbook.vba_project: Option<Vec<u8>>` (base64 in JSON via a new `b64::opt` helper). `None` = no macros.
- **xlsx read** — capture the `vbaProject` relationship's bytes instead of warning and dropping them; warn that macros are kept but not executed.
- **xlsx write** — when present, emit `xl/vbaProject.bin` byte-identical, add the `.../relationships/vbaProject` relationship, switch the main part to the macro-enabled content type (`...sheet.macroEnabled.main+xml`), and add the `application/vnd.ms-office.vbaProject` override.
- **engine** — `view.macros` lists the preserved project alongside GridCraft's own scripts (`{"kind":"vba","executed":false}`).
- **ROADMAP** — scope changed from "out of scope" to "preserve, don't execute" (per @echelon).

**UI — Excel-style surfaces, honest about what GridCraft does** (the open-time warning used to be discarded)
- **Info bar** under the ribbon (Excel's message-bar slot). A VBA project gets an amber bar: *"This workbook contains VBA macros. GridCraft keeps them intact when you save, but does not run them."* with a **What this means** button; any other open-time warning becomes a blue informational bar. Dismissable, and a clean open clears a stale notice.
- **Macros dialog** (Automate ▸ Macros, **Alt+F8**) — lists GridCraft's own scripts and the preserved VBA project (prese…

title: Default Windows startup to DirectX 12
author: DWAA1660
body:
No GridCraft issue reports this yet. This is a preventive fix for the same Windows startup crash.

Same fix as storytold/designcraft#168, applied to GridCraft. FilmCraft has the same change for storytold/filmcraft#179.

## Problem

GridCraft's desktop app uses eframe's default wgpu instance, which enables `PRIMARY | GL` on Windows. Creating the OpenGL backend can crash inside AMD's OpenGL driver (`atio6axx.dll`) before adapter selection or any Rust error handling runs. The app then flashes in Task Manager and exits with no window and no error (storytold/designcraft#167, storytold/filmcraft#179, storytold/filmcraft#268). `WGPU_BACKEND=dx12` was the verified workaround.

## Change

- New `apps/gridcraft/src/graphics.rs`: when no `WGPU_BACKEND` is set, the Windows wgpu instance enables only DirectX 12 before it is created, so OpenGL is never initialized as a fallback. Picking an adapter afterwards would be too late.
- `main.rs` applies it on Windows only. An explicit `WGPU_BACKEND` is still honoured, and the process environment is not changed.
- macOS, Linux and the web build are unchanged.
- README: a short Windows troubleshooting note on the default and the `WGPU_BACKEND` override.

## Validation

- `cargo test -p gridcraft graphics`: 2 passed. `windows_default_initializes_only_dx12` asserts that eframe's default includes GL and that the configured instance is DX12 only. `explicit_backend_override_is_preserved` covers overrides.
- `cargo clippy -p gridcraft --no-deps --all-targets -- -D warnings` (Linux): clean. `rustfmt --check` on the changed files: clean.
- `cargo clippy -p gridcraft --no-deps --target x86_64-pc-windows-gnu -- -D warnings`: clean, so the Windows-only call site compiles. (`--no-deps` because clippy 1.97 reports an existing `manual_range_contains` lint in `crates/core/src/date.rs:100`, which this change does not touch.)
- Limitation: no Windows/AMD hardware here, so the driver crash itself was not reproduced. The DX12 workaround comes from the desig…

title: Render CJK text (Japanese/Chinese/Korean) instead of tofu
author: justinjohn0306
body:
## What

Open a Japanese (or Chinese/Korean) workbook and every kanji and kana draws as a `.notdef` box (tofu) — while Excel shows it correctly. The engine reads the strings fine (`sheet.read` returns `カテゴリ`, `シート名`, `説明`); the failure is purely the render path: **egui's bundled fonts carry no CJK coverage**, and GridCraft never adds a CJK face to the fallback chain.

## Fix

Append a system CJK face to **every** font family (UI, cell, serif, mono):

- a **Japanese** face first (`YuGothR` → `msgothic` / Hiragino), so kana and JIS kanji get Japanese glyph shapes;
- a **Chinese** face next (`msyh` / PingFang), for breadth;
- a **Hangul** face (`malgun` / AppleSDGothicNeo), for Korean.

epaint renders each glyph from the first face in a family that has it, so Latin text still comes from the Latin fonts and only Han/Kana/Hangul reach the CJK fonts. No font bytes are bundled (per AGENTS.md): families are loaded from the OS at runtime, and a machine with no CJK font simply keeps today's behaviour. On wasm the loader no-ops.

## Tests

- Structural: the CJK keys sit at the **end** of every family chain (Latin stays first).
- Real render: the proportional family resolves `カテゴリ` to actual glyphs, not the replacement character — confirmed to **fail without the fix** (tofu → replacement char) and pass with it.

Verified by offscreen render of the reported file: cells and sheet tabs now show Japanese.

## Notes

Standalone and independent of the VBA work in #19. Snapshot below is the same `excel_sample.xlsm` that showed boxes before.

title: i18n: switch the interface language, defaulting to the system language (#20)
author: justinjohn0306
body:
Fixes #20.

Adds an **interface-language** preference. It defaults to the system's language on first run and can be switched by hand. The interface chrome — ribbon tabs, every button/menu label, status bar, number-format list — is translated; command ids, file names and document text are not.

## What the issue asked for

> The software's default language is English; is it possible to switch to another language — for example, by manually changing the setting or having it automatically match the device's default language?

Both: an automatic system-language default **and** a manual switch.

## How it works

- **`Language` enum** (`En`, `Ja`) with `tr(text) -> &str` and English fallback, matching the [filmcraft house convention](https://github.com/storytold/filmcraft). A single `JAPANESE` table holds the English→Japanese strings, so coverage grows incrementally and an unknown string is never a bug — it just renders in English.
- **Automatic default**: `UiState.language` is `#[serde(default = "i18n::Language::system")]`, and `Language::system()` reads the desktop locale via [`sys-locale`](https://crates.io/crates/sys-locale) (native only; the wasm build falls back to English — no system locale to read). A `ja`/`ja-JP` system means the app opens in Japanese; anything else opens in English.
- **Manual switch**: a **View ▸ Interface language** combo box next to Dark Mode. It persists in `ui.json` like every other UI preference.
- **Everything is a command**: `app.language.english` / `app.language.japanese` / `app.language.set={"code":"ja"}` reach it over the control channel, CLI and MCP, like the UI.
- **One place per surface**: all ribbon chrome goes through the `big_button` / `small_button` / `toggle_button` / `split_button` / `icon_button` helpers (`widgets.rs`) and `menu_items` (`ribbon.rs`), so translating there localises ~180 labels from a handful of edits. The frame's language is carried in egui context data (`i18n::current`) so helpers that only get a `Ui` can rea…

title: Fix: inserting or deleting rows, columns or cells cancels copy/cut mode (#21)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Part of #21. This fixes the second problem in the issue, the stale copy source. It does not add the "Insert Copied Cells" menu item, which is a separate feature.

**What the user saw:** copy or cut a row, then insert a row above it. The dotted copy border stayed on the old row number, which now holds different cells. After a cut, Paste moved whatever was at the old position (for example the new blank row) and left the real data where it was. It also rewrote formulas as if that old range had moved.

**Cause:** the clipboard stores its source as a fixed sheet range (`Clipboard::range`). Inserting or deleting rows, columns or cells never updates or clears it. A cut-paste then takes the cells at that range from the current sheet (`paste_special`, `take_range(src)`).

**What changed:** in `crates/engine/src/cmd/sheet.rs`, `insert_lines`, `delete_lines`, `insert_cells` and `delete_cells` now clear the clipboard after a successful edit when the clipboard came from the same workbook. Excel does the same: inserting or deleting cancels copy mode. A clipboard from another workbook is left alone.

**Tests:** `inserting_or_deleting_cells_cancels_copy_mode` in `crates/engine/src/tests.rs`. It cuts row 3, inserts a row at 3, and checks that the clipboard is cleared, that a paste does nothing and that the data is still in row 4. It then checks that Delete Columns, Insert Cells and Delete Cells also clear a copy. Without the fix, the first assertion fails.

title: Fix missing dropdown arrows on large ribbon buttons (#26)
author: harrisonoconnorhover
body:
Large ribbon dropdown buttons append `▾` to their labels. If the UI font has no glyph for it, the button shows a missing-character box, as reported on Linux Mint in #26.

Draw the existing `Icon::Chevron` beside the final label line, matching the small and split ribbon buttons. Include the arrow and gap in the measured width and center the label/arrow together, so both one-line and two-line buttons fit.

Fixes #26.

Validation:
- Regression test fails on the original widget; the plain-button control passes.
- `cargo +1.95.0 test --locked --workspace`: 339 passed, 0 failed, 0 ignored (including both new widget tests).
- Formatting, diff check, asset attribution, dependency layers, WebAssembly build, and parity check passed.
- Before/after light-mode and fixed dark-mode offscreen renders inspected on macOS; arrows fit and remain aligned.
- `cargo xtask ci` stops at strict Clippy on unchanged `crates/core/src/date.rs:100` (`manual_range_contains`). A separate strict UI check with `--no-deps` stops on existing findings in `formula_bar.rs:169` and `grid.rs:580,1541,1657`. Those files are unchanged; no lints were suppressed. The remaining CI steps were run individually as listed above.

The change adds no fonts, assets or dependencies. The Linux Mint AppImage itself was not run; the regression uses egui's bundled fonts, and visual checks run on macOS.

title: Fix copying selected cells as rich HTML tables
author: harrisonoconnorhover
body:
Copying cells into Writer or another rich-text editor currently offers only tab-separated text, so the selection loses its table structure. This adds an HTML table alongside the existing text clipboard format on desktop and web.

Fixes #23.

- Render the selected, visible rows with displayed values, escaped text, line breaks, clipped merges, and basic font/color/fill/alignment styling.
- Route keyboard, ribbon, context-menu, and native-menu Copy/Cut through one host clipboard callback. Native uses arboard (retaining its owner); web writes HTML and text in one ClipboardItem during the copy gesture. Existing internal copy/cut/paste remains unchanged.
- Keep the existing text path when rich clipboard support is absent or fails. Copies above 10,000 cells or 4 MiB of HTML use text only; HTML is never partially emitted.

Validation: 344 workspace tests passed, including seven new engine/UI regressions. Formatting, diff, assets, layering, parity, native build, WASM build and WASM check passed. On macOS, an actual GridCraft → LibreOffice Writer paste produced a table; Chrome → contenteditable paste also preserved header styling, currency display, multiline text and a merged row. Windows and Linux runtime testing remains outstanding.

`cargo xtask ci` was attempted but stops at the existing `core/date.rs:100` Clippy finding. Separate targeted strict lint also encounters existing expressions in `engine/cmd/file.rs`, `ui-egui/formula_bar.rs` and `ui-egui/grid.rs`; this patch does not suppress them. Browser testing opened a synthetic XLSX fixture because sample creation hits the existing `std::time::Instant::now()` WASM panic in `engine/cmd/mod.rs`.

This provides table interoperability and basic styling, not full workbook formatting fidelity.

title: feat(functions): add BAHTTEXT worksheet function
author: tukimtk-design
body: Adds the standard Microsoft Excel worksheet function =BAHTTEXT() to convert numbers into Thai currency words (e.g. 1234.50 -> 'หนึ่งพันสองร้อยสามสิบสี่บาทห้าสิบสตางค์'). Fully covered with comprehensive unit tests for zero, negative values, and fractional satang precision to enhance Excel parity.

title: Fonts: render Thai and Hebrew (and other non-Latin scripts) instead of tofu (#32)
author: justinjohn0306
body:
Fixes #32.

Thai (and other non-Latin) text rendered as tofu boxes even though the text was read correctly and the user had Thai-capable fonts installed. Same class of bug as #25: egui bundles only Latin glyphs, and the fallback chain appended only the Han/Kana and Hangul faces, so Thai and Hebrew had no face to fall through to.

## What the issue reported

> Thai text shows as square boxes or wrong characters, even when using fonts that support Thai … switching to Tahoma, Arial, or Segoe UI does not fix it … copying the cell into Windows Notepad displays the Thai correctly.

The reporter is right that the underlying Unicode is preserved — this is purely the render path. A commenter confirmed the same for **Hebrew** on Linux.

## Fix

Generalise the CJK fallback (from #25) into a **per-script fallback**. Every font family now also carries:

- a **Thai** face — Leelawadee UI / Tahoma / Microsoft Sans Serif (Windows), Thonburi / Sukhumvit Set (macOS), Noto Sans Thai / Garuda (Linux);
- a **Hebrew** face — David / FrankRuehl / Tahoma (Windows), Arial Hebrew / David (macOS), Noto Sans Hebrew / DejaVu Sans (Linux).

The faces stay at the **end** of each chain, so Latin still wins for Latin text and each fallback face only catches its own script. No font bytes are bundled (per `AGENTS.md`): every family loads from the OS at runtime, machines without the face keep current behaviour, and the wasm loader no-ops.

The key enabler is that epaint 0.36 shapes complex scripts itself (it depends on `harfrust`, a HarfBuzz-lineage shaper) — Thai reordering and per-run shaping are handled. It only needed a face that has the glyphs.

## Verified

Offscreen render (`snapshot --cmd 'cell.set={…}'`): Thai `ทดสอบภาษาไทย 1234`, pure Hebrew `שלום`, `אבג`, and Korean/Japanese all render as real glyphs — no tofu. Verified visually against the crop, and by the tests below.

## Tests

`fallback_covers_its_script` (`crates/ui-egui/src/theme.rs`): a per-script render check that a sample string re…

title: Add initial Alt ribbon keytips and legacy shortcuts (#33)
author: harrisonoconnorhover
body:
Typing the sequential shortcuts from #33 currently starts a cell edit. This adds a transient keytip mode that consumes those keystrokes before any editor sees them and runs the existing commands.

Part of #33. This is initial support for the issue's concrete examples; the broader mouse-free navigation request should remain open.

- Press/release left Alt on Windows/Linux/BSD, or F10 on any platform. Show keytips on Home and the supported controls. Mac Option, right Alt/AltGr, text editing, dialogs and modified shortcuts retain their existing input paths.
- Implement H A L/C/R for alignment, H V S / legacy E S for Paste Special, and H O I / legacy O C A for AutoFit columns. Keyboard paths open the existing Paste/Format menus. Escape backs up one level; another Alt/F10, a click, scrolling or focus loss exits.
- In Paste Special, T/V/F/C select formats/values/formulas/comments and E toggles transpose; Enter applies. These mnemonics work with or without Alt outside macOS, and without Option on macOS.
- Handle both Key-before-Text and Text-before-Key backend ordering, plus held-key repeats, without leaking shortcut letters into cells. No engine commands, assets, persisted preferences or dependencies are added.

Validation:
- 348 workspace tests pass, including 11 new input/state regressions. These cover both event orders, Alt/F10 activation, cancellation, repeat keys, editor/Option/AltGr isolation, command effects, and clicking a keyboard-opened menu.
- Native macOS: F10 H A R right-aligns without changing text; F10 H V S, V, E, Enter pastes formula results as transposed values. Light/dark keytips and menu renders visually inspected.
- Native build, WASM check, formatting, assets, layers, and parity check pass. Windows/Linux activation is tested through egui input simulation; browser runtime was not qualified.
- `cargo xtask ci` stops on the pre-existing `core/date.rs:100` Clippy finding. Targeted UI Clippy reports six existing findings in `formula_bar.rs` and `grid.rs`;…

title: Fix disappearing text when editing merged cells (#40)
author: harrisonoconnorhover
body:
Editing a covered cell inside a merged range currently stores text in that hidden cell, while the sheet displays the top-left cell. Text therefore appears to disappear after committing the edit and can reappear when a different part of the merged area is edited.

Fixes #40.

Resolve the merged range's top-left cell when beginning an edit and reading the formula bar. Typing, F2, double-click and formula-bar editing now use the same cell the grid displays. Existing engine commands, navigation and explicit programmatic cell addresses are unchanged.

Validation:
- All three focused UI regressions fail on main and pass with this fix: typing then clicking away, F2/double-click editing of existing text, and formula-bar display/editing from a covered cell.
- 340 workspace tests pass. Native build, formatting, WASM check, asset attribution, dependency layering and parity check pass.
- Reproduced on native macOS before the fix: selecting B11 in merged A10:B11 and typing `x` writes to hidden B11 while A10 stays empty. After the fix, the same native keys write to A10, B11 remains empty, and the text stays visible. Re-selecting B11 and editing via the formula bar also updates A10.
- `cargo xtask ci` stops on the pre-existing `core/date.rs:100` Clippy finding. Targeted UI Clippy reports six unchanged findings in `formula_bar.rs`/`grid.rs`; no suppressions or unrelated changes included.
- The reported Windows runtime was not available; pointer/keyboard behavior is covered through egui integration tests and the native macOS check.

This corrects subsequent UI edits; it does not migrate text already stored in covered cells.

title: Fix header double-click AutoFit for selected columns and rows (#42)
author: harrisonoconnorhover
body:
Double-clicking a column or row boundary currently enters the ordinary resize path and returns before AutoFit runs. Handle boundary double-clicks first, clear the pending resize gesture, and invoke the existing AutoFit command.

Fixes #42.

If the boundary belongs to selected whole columns/rows, fit all selected areas, including discontiguous selections. Otherwise fit only the clicked column/row. Preserve the selection and keep ordinary drag resizing and fill-handle behavior.

Validation:
- 339 workspace tests pass. New pointer regressions fail on the original code and pass with this fix, covering single/adjacent/discontiguous selections, boundaries outside the selection, row AutoFit, selection preservation, single-step undo and ordinary row/column dragging.
- Native macOS: reproduced a no-op double-click before the fix; afterward the same gesture expands both selected columns to display their labels, retains A:B selection, and records exactly one AutoFit command.
- Native build, formatting, WASM check, assets, layers and parity pass.
- Required `cargo xtask ci` stops at the existing `core/date.rs:100` Clippy finding. Targeted UI Clippy reports the same six existing findings; no suppressions or unrelated changes included.
- Windows/Linux native runtime was not available; shared pointer behavior is covered by egui integration tests. Existing AutoFit sizing calculations are unchanged.

title: Fix worksheet popups staying open after outside clicks (#41)
author: harrisonoconnorhover
body:
Header context menus and filter dropdowns currently stay open when clicking elsewhere in GridCraft because dismissal checks whether the pointer is outside all application UI. Check clicks against the individual popup instead.

Fixes #41.

Apply the same correction to validation-list dropdowns, which use the same broken check. Ignore the opening click, keep interactions inside each popup, and dismiss on outside clicks, Escape or window focus loss. Discard unapplied filter checkbox edits when closing so they do not leak into a reopened dropdown.

Validation:
- 341 workspace tests pass. Four grouped pointer regressions cover grid/ribbon clicks, another table/sheet, opening press/release in one frame, checkbox interactions, menu actions, Escape and focus loss. The original implementation fails the dismissal cases; cancellation/reopening also has a confirmed failing baseline before its correction.
- Native macOS: reproduced both stuck header and filter menus before the fix. Afterward outside clicks dismiss them, inside checkbox clicks retain the filter, cancellation resets the draft on reopening, and Apply still hides the excluded row and closes the popup.
- Native build, formatting, WASM check, assets, layers and parity pass.
- Required `cargo xtask ci` stops at the pre-existing `core/date.rs:100` Clippy finding. Targeted UI Clippy reports six unchanged findings; no suppressions or unrelated changes included.
- Windows/Linux native runtime was not available; shared pointer behavior is covered through egui integration tests.

title: Issue #48: rotated text with Wrap Text draws upright (grid and print)
author: LloydNicholson
body:
Fixes #48.

Cells with both a text rotation and Wrap Text (upright headers over narrow columns, common in mark sheets and schedules) were drawn flat: the wrap path drew the galley and `continue`d before the rotation was applied, so headers came out as 3–4 character fragments. Printing had the same gap (`rot != 0 && rot != 255 && !wrap`).

**Changes** (`ui-egui/src/grid.rs`, `engine/src/cmd/print.rs`)
- Rotated text no longer takes the flat wrap path. Upright (±90°) text wraps to the **row height**, its lines stacking across the column; other angles keep a single line, as before.
- Downward (−90°) text was anchored at the bottom-left, so it ran out of the cell (over the row headers in the grid). It now starts at the top, one block-height in, so the block sits inside the cell.
- Upright text no longer "overflows" into empty neighbours: overflow used the flat text width, widening the clip and repainting the neighbours' gridlines.
- Print/PDF gets the same three fixes (wrapped lines stack right for up, left for down).
- Also drops a redundant `|| text.contains('\n') && wrap` clause (implied by `wrap`).

**Tests**
- `ui-egui/tests/interaction.rs::rotated_wrapped_text_is_drawn_rotated_inside_its_cell`: up and down headers are each one text shape at ±90°, upright, ≤3 lines, inside a one-column clip. Verified it fails on `main` (angle 0), and separately fails if either the downward anchor or the overflow change is reverted.
- `print.rs::rotated_wrapped_text_prints_rotated`: every text block on the page uses a ±90° `Tm`, a few long lines each. Fails on `main` (flat `1 0 0 1` fragments).
- `cargo xtask ci` locally: fmt, clippy `-D warnings`, test (339 passed, 0 failed), assets, layers and `parity --check` all pass. **Not run locally:** the wasm step (my toolchain lacks the `wasm32-unknown-unknown` target); the change adds no dependencies or platform code, and this PR's CI covers it.
- Checked by eye on a real school mark sheet (not attached; it holds pupils' data): all row-6 …

title: Issue #51: General numbers fit by the cell's own font, not 11pt
author: LloydNicholson
body:
Fixes #51.

`grid.rs` measured the digit width once per frame for an 11pt cell font (`char_w`), and `display_text` decided how many General digits fit from that, whatever the cell's own font size. So 9pt marks like `100` in columns with a stored width of 4 (28px, common in mark sheets) showed `##`, although they fit; printing already got this right because `print.rs` measures with the cell's font and size.

**Change** (`crates/ui-egui/src/grid.rs`): the digit width is measured per cell with its own `FontId` (a cached one-glyph layout), and used both for the General fit and for the `####` fill count. The shared 11pt measurement and the `char_w` parameter of `paint_quadrant` are removed.

**Tests**
- `ui-egui/tests/interaction.rs::general_numbers_fit_by_the_cells_own_font`: a 9pt `100` in a 28px column draws in full, and `123456789` next to it still shows `####`. Fails on `main`, passes with the change.
- `cargo xtask ci` locally: fmt, clippy `-D warnings`, test (338 passed, 0 failed), assets, layers and `parity --check` pass. **Not run locally:** the wasm step (my toolchain lacks the `wasm32-unknown-unknown` target); the change uses only egui's text layout (no new dependencies or platform code), and this PR's CI covers it.
- Checked on a real school mark sheet (not attached; it holds pupils' data): all 18 `100` marks that showed `##` now draw in full.

Independent of #50 (different code in the same file; no overlap).

**How this was made:** this fix was written with Claude Code (AI coding assistant) at my direction; I reviewed it, and it was tested as described above. The commit carries a Co-Authored-By trailer.

title: ROUND: keep 15 significant digits when asked for 15+ digits, so ROUND(0.1+0.2,15) is 0.3 (#58)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #58.

`round_half_away` returned `x` unchanged when the requested digits reached past the 15 significant digits it works with, so `ROUND(0.1+0.2,15)` kept the binary noise and showed `0.30000000000000004`. That branch now returns the value cut to 15 significant digits through the existing `to_sig_digits` helper, as Excel does. Rounding to fewer digits is unchanged.

title: Line charts: smooth (spline) curves (issue #52)
author: justinjohn0306
body:
Closes #52.

Adds support for Excel's **smoothed line** chart style. The `smooth` flag flows model → resolve → chart render, persists through XLSX, and is toggleable via the `chart.addElement` `"smooth"` element.

## Behaviour

Rendering interpolates each gap-free run with a **uniform Catmull-Rom spline** (0.5 tangent scale, 100 sub-segments per data segment). The curve passes through every data point and rounds the vertices — matching Excel's observed behaviour (`<c:smooth val="1"/>`). Long runs are still decimated before smoothing, and runs are still split at gaps (`None` values), so the `draw_runs` smoothing happens per-run.

I verified this by authoring a straight+smooth side-by-side workbook, rendering it offscreen in GridCraft, and comparing against Excel's own render of the same file (black-box observation, per `AGENTS.md`). The curves match. Note that with gently-trending data the curvature is inherently subtle in **both** apps — Excel looks nearly the same as its straight version on a near-monotonic series.

## Changes

- **model** — `Series.smooth` with `#[serde(default)]`, so existing workbooks load unchanged.
- **chart** — `SeriesData.smooth`; `smooth_run` + `catmull` in `render.rs`; wired through `resolve` and the `sanitize()` copy; `draw_runs` takes the flag (line and scatter paths).
- **engine** — `chart.addElement` `"smooth"` handler.
- **xlsx** — read and write `<c:smooth val>` instead of hard-coding `val="0"`.
- **tests** — `smooth_line_adds_interpolated_points_and_keeps_endpoints`, `smooth_line_splits_at_gaps` (chart), `smooth_line_setting_round_trips` (xlsx).
- **examples** — `smooth_demo.rs` generates a straight+smooth side-by-side workbook (not committed as a file; regenerated on demand).

## Verification

`cargo xtask ci` — all 7 steps pass (fmt, clippy `-D warnings`, test, assets, layers, wasm, parity). Run locally; GitHub CI doesn't run these on a code PR (the build/test workflows gate on the release branch).

Constructor/serde call sites up…

title: XLSX: write _xlpm. prefix on LET/LAMBDA parameter names, strip it on read (#63)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #63.

Excel stores LET and LAMBDA parameter names with the `_xlpm.` prefix, and it does not open a workbook whose formulas use bare names. GridCraft wrote `_xlfn.LET(x,1,x+1)` where Excel expects `_xlfn.LET(_xlpm.x,1,_xlpm.x+1)`.

Changes in `crates/xlsx/src/fmla.rs`:

- Writing: `prefix_params` adds `_xlpm.` to each LET/LAMBDA parameter where it is declared and everywhere it is used in scope. This includes a LET-bound LAMBDA called by name (`f(3)` becomes `_xlpm.F(3)`). It handles nesting. A LET name enters scope only after its value expression. A name with the same spelling outside the LET/LAMBDA stays a plain defined name.
- Reading: `from_file` removes a leading `_xlpm.` (in any case) from names and from called names, so files from Excel load with clean formula text.

Test: `let_lambda_params` covers LET with one and two names, an invoked LAMBDA, a LET-bound LAMBDA called by name, a same-named reference outside the LET, and reading Excel's form back.

title: Issue #122: Recalc: linear in the number of range formulas
author: LloydNicholson
body:
Fixes #122.

Opening a workbook with `=SUM(E{r}:J{r})` on each of 50,000 rows took 9 s (1.5 s at 25k, 0.4 s at 12.5k), and a 50k×20 sheet took over a minute to open in the app. Editing a cell that 50,000 formulas read froze the app for 30–50 s. All the computed values were correct; only the time grew quadratically.

### Cause (profiled)
1. `Evaluator::trim` calls `Sheet::used_range` on every range read, and that walks every stored row, so a full recalc cost rows × range formulas. This was 99% of the time on open.
2. Each column's range precedents were kept in a Vec. Finding a cell's dependents scanned all of them, and re-entering a formula ran a `retain` over each of its columns, so paste, fill-down and sort were quadratic.

### Change (`crates/calc/src/recalc.rs`, `eval.rs`)
- The recalc pass works out each sheet's used range once (`Host::used_range`). Other hosts keep the old behaviour.
- Per-column and per-sheet "wide range" interval indexes (sorted by start, with a max-end segment tree) answer a lookup in O(log n + k). Removals are tombstones, insertions wait in a small pending set, and `Graph::settle` merges them after each batch.
- Single-cell dependents are a set, and `dependents_of_range` queries each column once.
- Semantics are unchanged: whole rows and columns, other sheets, names, tables, spills and volatile functions all use the same paths.

### Numbers (release build, before → after; values identical)
| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Headless open + recalc, 12.5k rows | 0.38 s | 0.09 s |
| Headless open + recalc, 25k rows | 1.46 s | 0.16 s |
| Headless open + recalc, 50k rows | 8.6 s | 0.31 s |
| 50k-row VLOOKUP column | 9.8 s | 1.05 s |
| App: open 50k×20 file | 65 s | 3.7 s |
| App: edit a cell with 100k dependents | 31.6 s | 1.25 s |
| App: fill 50k formulas down | >60 s | 0.36 s |
| Sort 50k rows (headless) | 9.0 s | 0.14 s |

### Tests
- The interval index checked against a linear scan over 20k random steps, plus a deterministic bound on how m…

title: Issue #123: SUMIF/AVERAGEIF size the sum range like the criteria range
author: LloydNicholson
body:
Fixes #123.

With A1:B3 = a,1 / b,2 / a,3, `=SUMIF(A1:A3,"a",B1)` should be 4. Excel adds up the range that starts at sum_range's top-left cell and has the criteria range's size. GridCraft gave 1, and AVERAGEIF had the same problem. `if_numbers` only saw sum_range's values, so it couldn't resize, although its comment said it did.

### Change (`crates/calc/src/eval.rs`)
- For SUMIF/AVERAGEIF with three arguments, the evaluator resizes a single-area sum-range reference to the criteria range's height × width, cut off at the sheet edge. This is done the way OFFSET/INDEX handle references, so it works across sheets and through names.
- `precedents()` records the resized range, so editing a cell inside it recalculates. If the criteria range isn't a plain reference, the formula recalculates every time instead.
- SUMIFS/AVERAGEIFS still return #VALUE! for ranges of different sizes (checked, unchanged).

| Formula (A1:B3 = a,1 / b,2 / a,3) | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `SUMIF(A1:A3,"a",B1)` | 1 | 4 |
| `AVERAGEIF(A1:A3,"a",B1)` | 1 | 2 |
| `SUMIF(A1:A3,"a",B1:B2)` | 1 | 4 |
| `SUMIF(A1:A3,"a",Data!B1)` | 10 | 40 |
| `SUMIF(…,B1)` after setting B3 to 5 | 1 | 6 |

### Tests (fail on `main`)
`calc/src/tests.rs` covers:
- single-cell, shorter, wider, longer and horizontal sum ranges, and whole-column criteria;
- recalculation after an edit inside the resized range;
- the sheet edge (B1048575/B1048576);
- another sheet and a defined name;
- SUMIFS/AVERAGEIFS size mismatches giving #VALUE!.

### Verified
`cargo xtask ci` (fmt, clippy `-D warnings`, test, assets, layers, wasm, parity) passes on macOS arm64, as do the FreeBSD workflow's `cargo build --workspace --all-targets --locked` and craft-fonts `cargo test --workspace --locked --no-fail-fast`. Untouched `main` also passes, so there are no pre-existing failures. The values above were checked in the release app over the control channel.

title: Issue #124: DATE(1900,2,29) is serial 60, as in Excel
author: LloydNicholson
body:
Fixes #124.

Excel's 1900 date system keeps Lotus's 29 February 1900 as serial 60, and `DAY(60)` already returned 29. But `DATE(1900,2,29)` and `DATEVALUE("2/29/1900")` returned 61, and `DATE(1900,3,0)` returned 59. `serial_from_ymd` worked out the real calendar date and shifted it afterwards, so it never reached serial 60.

### Change (`crates/core/src/date.rs`, `parse.rs`, `functions/src/date.rs`)
- The serial of the first of the month is taken in Excel's calendar, and the day (with any overflow) counts on from there, so overflow passes through serial 60 in both directions. Month and day arithmetic is checked, so hostile values return None instead of overflowing.
- `days_in_month_in` gives February 1900 29 days in the 1900 system. EDATE, EOMONTH and the text parser use it, so typing `2/29/1900` also gives 60.
- The 1904 system is unchanged.

| Formula | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `DATE(1900,2,29)`, `DATEVALUE("1900-02-29")`, `DATEVALUE("2/29/1900")`, `DATE(1900,1,60)` | 61 | 60 |
| `DATE(1900,3,0)`, `EOMONTH(60,0)`, `EDATE(DATE(1900,1,31),1)` | 59 | 60 |
| `DAY(60)` / `DATE(1900,3,1)` | 29 / 61 | unchanged |

Note for review: EDATE/EOMONTH in February 1900 now treat 1900-02-29 as the end of February, so they agree with `DAY(60)`. On `main`, `EOMONTH(60,0)` returned 59, the day before its input. This wasn't compared against Excel directly. DATEDIF, DAYS360 and YEARFRAC still use the real calendar for February 1900 and are left for a follow-up.

### Tests
- Serials around the leap day, and a round-trip of serials 0–366 through year/month/day.
- Hostile months and days.
- Parsing `2/29/1900`, `1900-02-29` and `29-Feb-1900`.

title: Preserve whole-sheet formatting when entering empty cells (#70)
author: DWAA1660
body:

Resolve the destination's effective cell/row/column style before parsing input. This preserves formatting for regular and array entry, text paste, and bulk values, and lets inherited Text formats keep leading zeros and formula-looking text. Update the other callers of the shared input helper to supply the destination.

Fixes #70.

title: Preserve array evaluation for non-spilling XLSX formulas
author: harrisonoconnorhover
body:
Addresses #64 (XLSX export).

`SUM(Data!A1:A20*Data!B1:B20)` can return a different value after export if Excel reads it with legacy implicit intersection. This preserves array evaluation for formulas that need it without converting every ordinary formula into a single-cell array.

The export-only classifier follows range/array operands, scalar function arguments, scoped names, structured references and indirect references. `SUM(A1:A20)`, `A1*2`, ordinary table-row formulas and legacy array-aware `SUMPRODUCT` expressions remain ordinary formulas. Array-sensitive expressions receive `cm="1"` and an array reference; actual spills and legacy CSE arrays keep their respective representations. Explicit `@` scalarizes its result while retaining any array-sensitive operations inside it. Analysis is bounded and conservative for unresolved reference dimensions; it does not evaluate formulas or change import behavior.

Rebased onto main at `1ded850`, including #85. Its `#SPILL!`/`#CALC!` → `#VALUE!` cached-error behavior and regression coverage remain intact.

Validation:
- All 52 XLSX tests pass, including eight focused export groups. Six updated groups failed under the original blanket-metadata policy before the classifier was added.
- An original CLI workbook preserves live/reopened results for range arithmetic, scalar functions over ranges, names, INDIRECT, SUMPRODUCT and scalar controls. Saved XML confirms only affected formulas carry array metadata, while scalar table formulas do not.
- Formatting, asset attribution, layering, WASM compilation, parity and diff checks pass. No dependency or layering changes.
- Required `cargo xtask ci` stops at the existing `core/src/date.rs:108` Clippy error. Scoped XLSX Clippy stops only at the existing `sheet_read.rs:146` diagnostic; no suppressions added.

Excel-native recalculation was not run for this revision, and exact metadata parity for every function is not claimed. The reading-side legacy semantics in #64 remain separate. Poli…

title: XLSX: cache #SPILL! and #CALC! as #VALUE! so Excel can open the file
author: nihilist-narwhal
body:
A formula whose value is `#SPILL!` (a blocked spill) or `#CALC!` is written with that error as its cached value. Neither is an error code of the XLSX file format, and Excel refuses to open such a file: on Excel for Mac 16.113, opening it fails with "Parameter error (-50)". So any workbook containing a blocked spill could not be opened in Excel.

Excel itself caches these errors as `#VALUE!` when it saves, so the writer now does the same. `#SPILL!`/`#CALC!` inside a cached array value are mapped too. Other errors (`#N/A`, `#DIV/0!`…) are unchanged, and GridCraft still shows the real error in its own UI, since it recalculates on open.

- Test `spill_and_calc_errors_are_cached_as_value_errors` fails before the change and passes after it. The 42 `gridcraft-xlsx` tests pass, and fmt passes.
- `cargo clippy -p gridcraft-xlsx --all-targets -D warnings` is clean apart from the existing `manual_range_contains` at `crates/core/src/date.rs:100`, which this PR doesn't touch.
- Separate from #64 and #83 (dynamic-array metadata); it applies on its own.

The second commit adds my entry to `contributors/people.toml`.

body:

Use `clicked_by(Primary)` for the grid's pointer paths so keyboard navigation operates on the active selection. Actual pointer selection, dragging, double-clicks and secondary clicks keep their existing paths. This also prevents Space from acting on an old hovered checkbox instead of the active checkbox.

author: harrisonoconnorhover
body:

title: Import worksheet data and cached results from XLSB workbooks
author: harrisonoconnorhover
body:

Charts, images, macros and other workbook features are not imported. These limits appear in an app warning, returned warnings and CLI stderr. title: Fix keyboard selection snap-back on Enter navigation
author: onemannoplan
body:
Prevent the selection indicator from reverting to stale mouse coordinates after pressing Enter by clearing active mouse drag flags and re-anchoring the selection.

**Context & Cause**

When navigating the grid using the keyboard after a mouse interaction, app.grid.drag remained stuck in Drag::Select state. Because interact() runs every frame, it continuously recalculated the active selection range from sel.anchor to the resting mouse position, causing the selection indicator to "snap back" to the cursor location during keyboard movement.

**Changes**

    crates/ui-egui/src/grid.rs:

        Reset app.grid.drag to Drag::None and app.grid.drag_select to false in the Key::Enter handler.

        Re-anchor the active selection via Selection::at(d.selection.active) when Enter is pressed without Shift.

        Refactored keyboard() control flow to properly handle bool returns across match arms.

**Validation**

    Clicked a cell to initiate a mouse selection.

    Moved cursor over non-selected grid cells without clicking.

    Tapped Enter sequentially and verified cell selection moves downwards without jumping or range-selecting towards the cursor position.

title: ui-egui: fall back to system CJK fonts
author: eyouhi
body:
Cells and chrome render CJK text as tofu boxes: `theme::font_definitions` picks at most one
system font per role from a list of Latin faces (Calibri/Carlito, Arial/Liberation, DejaVu, …)
and falls back to egui's bundled fonts, none of which carry Han glyphs.

This appends a system CJK face to every family chain — Noto Sans CJK SC (regular and bold) on
Linux, PingFang SC on macOS, Microsoft YaHei then SimSun on Windows, WenQuanYi Micro Hei as the
last Linux resort — so Han text falls through to it while every other glyph keeps its current
font. Bold roles use the bold face when one is installed.

Nothing is bundled: still system fonts only, in the spirit of the fonts standard. On a machine
with no CJK font installed the chains are exactly as before.

Tests: two unit tests in `theme.rs` cover the fallback ordering and the bold face; both skip
cleanly when no CJK font is installed (as on bare CI images).

Verified locally on Arch with Noto Sans CJK SC: an .xlsx with Chinese column headers, values and
sheet names renders correctly, and `cargo test -p gridcraft-ui-egui` plus
`cargo clippy -p gridcraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings` pass.

title: Add static pictures inside cells with XLSX roundtrip
author: harrisonoconnorhover
body:

Optional XLSX picture-data failures now warn and preserve scalar fallbacks instead of preventing the workbook from opening, including oversized metadata, excessive rich records and relationship read errors. XLSX export keeps picture value metadata and dynamic-array metadata independent in the same package. The UI cache preserves more than 128 visible small pictures across frames, with bounded texture memory and admission before decoding under pressure.

Rebased onto main `c5bf34d`. ODS/XLSB import changes are not merged there yet; `Package::read_limited` now matches the incoming XLSB implementation so the two features can share it.

Addresses #61 as an initial static-picture implementation. OS clipboard images, conversion between floating/cell pictures, `IMAGE()` and rich-value formula propagation remain follow-up work. Scalar references and text exports use `#VALUE!`; please keep the issue open for the remaining scope.
