title: Preview border presets and fix shared-edge removal
author: harrisonoconnorhover
body:
Border presets now show original two-by-two diagrams alongside their existing labels, and Format Cells → Border previews the draft before applying it. The preview uses the worksheet line painter for widths, double/dashed/dotted strokes, diagonals, and workbook colors.

Also fixes a reproduced No Border failure: after applying All Borders to A1:B2, removing A1’s borders left the right and bottom lines visible because B1/A2 still stored their facing edges. No Border now clears those facing edges in the same undo transaction, preserves unrelated formatting and values, respects worksheet limits, and honors sheet formatting protection.

Addresses #30. Keeping the issue open because the report also mentions unspecified border errors; this change covers the previews and the reproduced shared-edge removal case.

Validation: 58 engine tests and 16 UI tests passed, including actual preset clicks, draft/Cancel/OK behavior, undo, worksheet corners, and protection. Inspected light/dark menu and dialog renders. Native check, WASM, formatting, assets, layers, parity, and diff checks passed. Full `cargo xtask ci` stops at the existing `core/src/date.rs:100` Clippy diagnostic; scoped checks also report existing engine/UI diagnostics. Native OS pointer interaction was not exercised for this patch.

title: ui-egui: dismiss menus and pickers on any outside click
author: eyouhi
body:
The data-validation list picker, the filter menu and the header menu close only when a click
lands **outside the window** (`!ctx.is_pointer_over_egui()`), so clicking anywhere inside the
app — another cell, the ribbon, a sheet tab — leaves them open; only Escape or picking an entry
dismisses them.

This switches all three to: close on a press outside the popup's rectangle, on any later frame
than the one that opened it (so the opening click does not immediately dismiss it). The
validation arrow now toggles the list like Excel — pressing it again closes the list.

`context_menu` already did the rect-based check; this makes the other three consistent with it.

Verified through the real UI (control-channel driver): open the list on a validated cell, click
another cell → the list closes; press the arrow twice → it opens then closes; Escape and picking
an entry behave as before. A new `interaction.rs` test opens a picker on a validated cell and
asserts it closes on a click elsewhere in the window.

title: Offer an optional desktop shortcut in the Windows installer
author: harrisonoconnorhover
body:
Adds an optional desktop-shortcut checkbox to the per-machine Windows MSI. Fresh installations default to off; unattended installs can set `DESKTOPSHORTCUT=1` or `0`. The choice persists across major upgrades, and repair/removal is managed by Windows Installer. Addresses #24 for Windows MSI.

The shortcut component now uses `HKMU`: for this `Scope="perMachine"` package, its key path is written under HKLM and can be removed by a different account. MSI root -1 also satisfies ICE43, so no validation suppression is needed. The lifecycle test asserts there is no installing-user marker and exercises uninstall as SYSTEM after install by the runner account.

The Packaging lint Windows job builds the actual WiX source using original no-op executable fixtures, then checks default off, opt-in, shortcut target/icon, repair, upgrade persistence, explicit opt-out and cross-account cleanup. It also renders the six authored dialogs with Windows Installer's native preview API and uploads PNGs plus logs as `desktop-shortcut-msi-evidence`. These are native layout previews; they do not prove interactive checkbox behavior or a complete full-UI install sequence. Normal UI is the choice dialog followed by completion; the other dialogs support cancel/failure/files-in-use paths.

Rebased onto main at `1ded850`, including current action pins.

Local validation:
- WiX XML parses; per-machine scope, HKMU key path and absence of HKCU authoring asserted.
- All Windows PowerShell scripts parse, and the preview helper's C# interop compiles.
- actionlint, formatting and diff checks pass.
- Required `cargo xtask ci` stops at the existing `core/src/date.rs:108` Clippy diagnostic. No Rust runtime code changed.

[Windows Packaging lint run 38068335687](https://github.com/storytold/gridcraft/actions/runs/38068335687) is **green** at `811cb11`. Both packaging lint and Windows smoke jobs pass: WiX/ICE validation, default-off and opt-in installs, repair, upgrade persistence, explicit opt-out, uninstall, cr…

title: Preserve quick selection drags and clarify the fill handle
author: harrisonoconnorhover
body:
Quick pointer drags can currently leave only the starting cell selected: press C3, move to F7 in one frame, then release. The drag-start path returns before consuming its first endpoint, and the release path clears the drag without applying the final position.

This applies the first, intermediate, and release positions through the same selection update, reading the newly established anchor rather than a stale selection. Formula point-mode ranges use the same path and retain cross-sheet qualification. Ordinary clicks, cell contents, and AutoFill behavior stay intact.

Related to #28: inspection of the attached recording shows the bottom-right fill handle and its expected single-axis AutoFill preview. The fast-drag defect above was reproduced separately. A brief fill-handle hint now explains filling versus dragging from inside a cell to select a rectangle. Please keep the issue open for reporter confirmation; this PR does not claim the recording demonstrates the fast-drag defect.

Validation: all 20 UI tests pass (including six new selection tests; the baseline fails five of those six). The regressions cover first movement, reverse selection, release-only movement, multiple frames, ordinary click/hover, formula point mode, cross-sheet references, and unchanged cell values/formulas. Inspected the hint and resulting rectangular selection renders. Native compilation, WASM, formatting, assets, layers, parity, and diff checks pass. `cargo xtask ci` stops at the existing `core/src/date.rs:100` Clippy diagnostic; scoped UI Clippy also reports existing formula-bar/grid diagnostics. Real OS pointer interaction is not qualified by the offscreen input harness.

title: Protection: enforce locked cells for every command, keep hidden formulas hidden
author: nihilist-narwhal
body:
On a protected sheet only `cell.set` checked protection. `edit.clearContents`, `range.setValues`, `edit.paste`, the fills, `home.deleteRows`/`deleteColumns`, `edit.replace` and `data.goalSeek` all changed locked cells. For example, after `review.protectSheet {}`, `edit.clearContents {"range":"A1"}` cleared A1.

The check now runs in `commit`, which every edit passes through. An edit that changes the value or formula of a locked cell on a protected sheet is refused with Excel's message, whichever command made it. To keep the check cheap, `CellStore::diff` compares only the 64-row bands the edit copied. Inserting and deleting rows and columns follow the protection's options, and deleted lines must not hold locked cells.

Hidden formulas no longer show on a protected sheet: not with Show Formulas on, not in Find (`lookIn: formulas`), and not in the formula bar when a cell of their spill range is selected.

- Tests cover each command, refused on locked cells and allowed on unlocked ones, the row/column options, and each of the hidden-formula paths. Each test fails before the change.
- fmt, the workspace tests, assets, layers and parity pass. `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings` is clean apart from the existing `manual_range_contains` at `crates/core/src/date.rs:100`, which this PR doesn't touch.

title: Insert/Delete Cells: adjust references like Excel
author: nihilist-narwhal
body:
`home.deleteCells` with a shift left formulas alone: it built the reference edit and then discarded it, so `=A4*10` still read A4 after A3 was deleted upward. `home.insertCells` treated the shift as a move of everything below the cells, so `=SUM(A1:A5)` stayed `SUM(A1:A5)` after inserting at A3 with shift down. Excel gives `SUM(A1:A6)`.

Two new edits, `Edit::InsertCells` and `Edit::DeleteCells`, adjust a reference the way inserting or deleting rows (or columns) does when the reference lies within the shifted columns (or rows), and leave it alone otherwise, as Excel does. They go through the same `rewrite` as whole-row edits, so formulas, defined names, chart series and sparkline sources follow. Conditional-format, validation, table, filter and print-area ranges, notes, links and sparkline cells follow too.

- New tests in `formula` (adjustment rules) and `engine` (both commands, both directions, with a name, a rule, a validation and a chart) fail before the change.
- fmt, clippy (apart from the existing `date.rs` lint), the workspace tests, assets, layers and parity pass. The copy/cut-mode behaviour (#34) is untouched.

title: Names: keep sheet-level names with their sheet on move, copy and delete
author: nihilist-narwhal
body:
Name scopes are sheet indices, and sheet operations didn't keep them in step:

- `sheet.move` left a sheet-level name on whichever sheet took its old index.
- `sheet.move {copy: true}` didn't shift scopes, and the copy got none of the sheet's names.
- `home.deleteSheet` left names that referred to the deleted sheet pointing at nothing.
- `formulas.deleteName` ignored `scope` and deleted the name from every scope.

Moving now re-indexes scopes. A copy gets copies of the sheet's own names, referring to the copy, as in Excel. Names that refer to a deleted sheet become `#REF!`. `deleteName` honours `scope` ("Workbook" or a sheet name), and the Name Manager's Delete button passes it.

- `sheet_operations_keep_names_on_their_sheets` fails before the change.
- fmt, clippy (apart from the existing `date.rs` lint), the workspace tests, assets, layers and parity pass.

title: Names: R1C1-style names, Create from Selection bottom/right, LAMBDA name case
author: nihilist-narwhal
body:
Three small fixes to defined names:

- `valid_name` accepted `R1C1`, `R2`, `C3` and `RC`, which Excel refuses because they read as R1C1 references. They are now refused, like `R` and `C`.
- `formulas.createFromSelection` ignored `bottom` and `right`, and silently replaced an existing workbook name with the same label. Bottom-row and right-column labels now name the cells above them and to their left. Excel asks before replacing a name; a command can't ask, so an existing name is kept and reported in `skipped`, unless `replace: true` is passed.
- The parser upper-cases function names, so `=Double(4)` (a LAMBDA name) showed as `=DOUBLE(4)`. Calls of LAMBDA names are now spelled like the name when a formula is entered and when an XLSX file is read. Formulas then keep that spelling through edits and saves.

- Tests for each fail before the change. The LAMBDA test includes an XLSX round trip.
- fmt, clippy (apart from the existing `date.rs` lint), the workspace tests, assets, layers and parity pass.

title: Formulas: the spill range operator (A1#)
author: nihilist-narwhal
body:
`formula::parse("Sheet1!$D$1#")` failed with "unknown error literal", so formulas and names using a spill reference couldn't be entered or opened.

A `#` right after a cell reference is now the spill range operator (`UnOp::Spill`). It evaluates to the anchor's current spill range, or `#REF!` when the cell doesn't spill or its spill is blocked. Formulas that use it depend on the anchor, so they recalculate when the spill grows or shrinks. Defined names can use it. Excel's files have no `#` operator: they store `A1#` as `_xlfn.ANCHORARRAY(A1)`. The writer now does the same, and the parser reads that back as `A1#`.

- Tests cover parse/print, evaluation, recalculation as the spill grows, shrinks and is blocked, use through a name, and an XLSX round trip.
- fmt, clippy (apart from the existing `date.rs` lint), the workspace tests, assets, layers and parity pass.

title: Charts: Switch Row/Column on charts read from a file; scatter with text X values
author: nihilist-narwhal
body:
Two chart fixes:

- `chart.switchRowColumn` did nothing on a chart read from a file, because only charts made by `insert.chart` keep their source range. When a chart has no source range, the command now takes the block that the series' names, categories and values span (when they're all on one sheet), and keeps it.
- A scatter or bubble chart whose X values are text, such as a first column of labels, drew no points. Like Excel, such X values are now ignored and the points numbered 1..n (in `chart::resolve`).

- `switch_row_column_on_a_chart_read_from_a_file` and `scatter_with_text_x_values_numbers_the_points` fail before the change.
- fmt, clippy (apart from the existing `date.rs` lint), the workspace tests, assets, layers and parity pass. The branch merges cleanly with #62.

title: Preserve doubled text qualifiers in Text to Columns
author: agammann
body:
## Summary

Text to Columns currently drops a doubled quote inside a quoted field. For example, splitting `"a""b",c` on commas produces `ab` and `c`, losing the quote in the first cell.

When a text qualifier is doubled inside a quoted field, consume the pair and keep one literal qualifier. A single qualifier still opens or closes the quoted field.

## Reproduction

On `13664fe66b952e7abcd68e2371c1d4f34f990dac`, set A1 to `"a""b",c` and run `data.textToColumns` with `range: "A1"` and `delimiters: [","]`. Before the change, A1 is `ab`; after the change, A1 is `a"b`. B1 is `c` in both cases.

The new CLI regression invokes `cell.set` and `data.textToColumns` through the actual `gridcraft-cli` binary. It fails on the unmodified commit (`ab,c` instead of `"a""b",c` in CSV output) and passes with this change.

## Validation

- `cargo test -p gridcraft-cli --locked` — 10 passed.
- `cargo test -p gridcraft-engine --locked split` — 2 passed.
- `cargo clippy -p gridcraft-engine -p gridcraft-cli --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` — passed.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `git diff --check` — passed.
- `cargo xtask ci` — all 7 gates passed: formatting, workspace Clippy, workspace tests, assets, layering, WebAssembly check, and parity check.

title: Issue #118: committing a cell in the web app no longer traps on the clock
author: LloydNicholson
body:
Fixes #118.

In the web app, typing `1` into A1 and pressing Enter raised `Uncaught RuntimeError: unreachable`. Every edit goes through `cmd::commit` in the engine, which called `std::time::Instant::now()` on every call for `GRIDCRAFT_PROFILE` timing, even with profiling off. `wasm32-unknown-unknown` has no clock, so `Instant::now` panics there, and a panic on that target aborts as an `unreachable` trap. Native builds have a clock, which is why the CLI controls in the issue worked.

### Change (`crates/engine/src/cmd/mod.rs`, `clippy.toml`)
- `commit` reads the clock only when `GRIDCRAFT_PROFILE` is set, and never on wasm. Profiling output on native is unchanged.
- The other clock reads (`now_serial` for NOW()/TODAY(), `current_year` for typed dates, the UI's `now_ms`, the calc profiler) were already gated with `cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))` and are unchanged.
- Regression guard: `clippy.toml` now disallows `std::time::Instant::now` and `std::time::SystemTime::now`, with a note on why. Each clock read has to skip wasm and allow the lint at the call. The four existing gated functions and the native-only `examples/perf.rs` get an `#[allow(clippy::disallowed_methods)]`. On `main`'s `commit`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` fails with `use of a disallowed method std::time::Instant::now` at `crates/engine/src/cmd/mod.rs:221`.

### Tests
Native tests can't see a trap that happens only on wasm, so the clippy lint above is the regression guard. To reproduce, the engine at this branch and on `main` was built for `wasm32-unknown-unknown` into a small throwaway cdylib (not committed). It creates a `Session`, calls `new_workbook()` and runs `cell.set {"cell":"A1","input":"1"}`, and the module was run in Node:

| Engine | Result |
|---|---|
| `main` (13664fe) | `RuntimeError: unreachable` |
| this branch | `cell.set` returns `Ok` |

### Verified
`cargo xtask ci` (fmt, clippy `-D warnings`, test, assets, layers, wasm, parity) passes on macOS arm64. The…

title: web: print straight to the system print dialog, not just export
author: Dejan-Port
body:
## What

\`file.print\` already builds a PDF and returns it as base64, per its own doc comment: *"the PDF the UI hands to the system print dialog"* — but nothing actually did that. On the web build, Ctrl+P (Cmd+P is declared as the command's shortcut, but there's no keyboard dispatch wired to it anywhere) did nothing, and the ribbon's "Print…" menu item ran \`file.print\` via \`run_or_alert\`, which just discards the result on success.

This wires it up: a dedicated **Print** action that runs \`file.print\`, decodes the returned PDF, and (on the web build) opens it in a hidden iframe and calls the iframe's own \`print()\` once it's loaded — the standard way to drive the browser's native print dialog on a PDF without a download or a popup window the browser might block.

## How

- \`ui-egui\`: new \`Services::print\` hook (\`Option<Box<dyn Fn(&[u8])>>\`).
- \`ui-egui\`: \`SheetApp::print_now()\` — runs \`file.print\`, decodes the \`base64\` field of the result with the engine's own \`base64_decode\`, hands the bytes to \`services.print\`. Falls back to the existing alert-on-error behavior on failure (same as \`run_or_alert\`), and is a silent no-op on success when there's no \`services.print\` (desktop today — nothing regresses, \`file.print\` still runs, there's just no UI action on success, same as before this change).
- \`ui-egui\` \`ribbon.rs\`: \`Key::P\` now dispatches to \`print_now\` (previously no \`Key::P\` arm existed in the shortcut \`match\` at all); the "More commands" menu's "Print…" item calls \`print_now\` instead of \`run_or_alert("file.print", …)\`.
- \`gridcraft-web\`: implements the hook — \`Blob\` → object URL → hidden \`<iframe>\` → \`iframe.contentWindow.print()\` on \`onload\`. Added \`HtmlIFrameElement\` to the \`web-sys\` feature list.

## Testing

- \`cargo check --target wasm32-unknown-unknown -p gridcraft-web\` — clean (one pre-existing unrelated warning in \`crates/engine/src/cmd/spelling.rs\`, not from this change).
- \`cargo fmt --che…

title: Preserve formula references when cutting cells across sheets
author: harrisonoconnorhover
body:
Cutting `Sheet1!A1:A2` containing 10 and 20 into `Sheet2!C1:C2` leaves dependent formulas pointing at the emptied source, changing a total from 30 to 0 even after saving and reopening. This retargets the moved references to the destination sheet so the total remains 30.

Fixes #128.

The cross-sheet adjustment uses the existing fully-contained-range move policy and preserves absolute anchors. Formulas moved with the block retain source-sheet references to cells left behind; references to cells inside the block follow them once. Qualified defined names participate in the same rewrite. Same-sheet moves and ordinary copy behavior are covered by controls.

Validation: 59 engine tests and 12 formula tests pass. Three of the four new engine regressions fail on the baseline and pass with this change; they cover dependencies across source/destination/third sheets, quoted names, moved formulas, undo/redo, XLSX reopening, and later edits to the moved inputs. A separate CLI reproduction verifies live and reopened totals and independently reads the saved XLSX formula/cache. Native/WASM compilation, formatting, assets, layers, parity, and diff checks pass.

Full `cargo xtask ci` stops at the pre-existing `crates/core/src/date.rs:100` Clippy error. Scoped engine/formula Clippy reports the existing `crates/engine/src/cmd/file.rs:51` diagnostic. No lint suppressions are added. Validation uses original workbooks through the shared engine/CLI; native clipboard interaction and Excel were not exercised.

title: Fix/macos cjk fonts
author: musicism-tai
body:
# Add installed system fonts, CJK rendering fixes, and font picker improvements

## Summary

This PR improves system font support in GridCraft, with a focus on macOS and CJK text rendering.

### Changes

- Discover and load installed system fonts using `fontdb`.
- Add CJK font fallback to improve Chinese text rendering.
- Fix DFKai-SB glyph rendering using Mono TrueType hinting.
- Group font families and related variants in the font picker.
- Deduplicate localized font family aliases.
- Add favorite fonts with a pinned section in the font picker.
- Persist font favorites in UI preferences and save changes immediately.

### Testing

- `cargo check -p gridcraft` — passed
- `cargo clippy -p gridcraft --all-targets -- -D warnings` — passed
- WebAssembly target compilation — passed
- Manually tested on macOS:
  - Traditional Chinese input and rendering
  - MingLiU, PMingLiU, PingFang TC, and DFKai-SB
  - Font family grouping and selection
  - Favorite fonts persistence across application restarts

### Notes

Font preview rendering was explored but excluded due to performance concerns when dynamically loading large font collections.

The font picker preserves the original family names used for font selection while providing a more organized interface.

title: Recalc: stale spills and values after edits (fixes #133, #139)
author: nihilist-narwhal
body:
Two cases where a cell kept a value that a full recalculation (Calculate Now, or reopening the file) changes.

Typing a value over a dynamic array formula, or clearing it, left the values it had spilled:

```sh
gridcraft-cli run --cmd 'cell.set={"cell":"E1","input":"=SEQUENCE(3)"}' \
  --cmd 'cell.set={"cell":"E1","input":"2"}' --print E1:E3
```

prints 2, 2, 3 (Excel: 2 and two empty cells), and `=SUM(E1:E3)` gives 7. The same happens with text or `edit.clearContents`; replacing it with another formula (`=5`) was fine. Only formulas are evaluated again, so the old spill of a cell that no longer holds a formula was never written back. `Calc::cells_changed` now removes it when the formula goes and recalculates the formulas reading its area. (Different from #133, where a structural edit leaves the old spill behind.)

Second commit: `=SUM(C3:INDEX(B9:C11,2,2))` adds C3:C10, but only C3 and B9:C11 were recorded as its precedents, so typing 2 into C5 left the total at 0. A range whose ends are function results (`INDEX`, `CHOOSE`, `IF`, `XLOOKUP`…) now depends on the box spanned by the references inside it, which contains any cell those functions can return. This keeps the common `A1:INDEX(A:A,COUNTA(A:A))` pattern non-volatile.

Third commit (#133): inserting or deleting rows and columns moved formula cells but not the values they had spilled, and the full recalculation that follows reconciled spills only at the formulas' new positions. With `=SEQUENCE(3)` in A5 and row 1 deleted, A4 showed `#SPILL!`, blocked by its own old values; deleting the anchor's row left 2 and 3 behind. `recalc_all` now drops all spills and lays them out again from the formulas.

Fourth commit (#139): clearing a cell re-evaluated `#SPILL!` anchors only within 64 rows and columns above and to the left of it, so `=SEQUENCE(100)` in A1 stayed `#SPILL!` after its blocker in A90 was cleared. Emptied cells now look for blocked anchors any distance above or to the left, with one pass over the formulas p…

title: Tables: typing in the header row renames the column; Go To a table selects its data
author: nihilist-narwhal
body:
Editing a table's header cell changed only the cell. The column kept its old name, so after typing `zz` over header `a`, `=SUM(Table1[a])` still worked and the header read `zz`. Saving then wrote the old names back into the header row, so the edit was gone after reopening:

```sh
gridcraft-cli run --cmd 'range.setValues={"range":"A1","values":[["a","b","c"],[1,2,3]]}' \
  --cmd 'insert.table={"range":"A1:C2","header":true}' \
  --cmd 'cell.set={"cell":"A1","input":"zz"}' --cmd 'edit.clearContents={"range":"B1"}' --out t.xlsx
gridcraft-cli cat t.xlsx --range A1:C1   # a  b  c
```

As in Excel, the column now takes the new header. An emptied header becomes `ColumnN` and a repeated one gets a number (`a2`), written back into the cell; a number typed there is stored as text; and structured references follow the new name (`=SUM(Table1[zz])`, including `[@col]` inside the table). The check runs after every edit (`cmd::edit`) and looks only at edited header cells (every header cell after a structural edit, which can shift other cells into a header row), so sheets without tables pay nothing.

Second commit: Go To (and the Name Box) with a table's name selected the whole table, header and totals included. In Excel a table's name stands for its data rows, as in formulas (`=SUM(Table1)` adds only the data), so `edit.goTo {"reference":"Table1"}` now selects A2:B3 for a table on A1:B3. (`Table1[col]` and `Table1[#All]` still aren't accepted by Go To.)

- New tests `tables::tests::editing_a_header_renames_the_column` and `go_to_a_table_selects_its_data` fail before their changes.
- fmt, clippy (apart from the existing `date.rs` lint) and the engine tests pass.

title: Paste Special operations: keep text, errors and formulas
author: nihilist-narwhal
body:
Paste Special with Add, Subtract, Multiply or Divide only combined cells holding a plain number; every other cell was overwritten with the pasted value. Copying a cell holding 1 and pasting it with Values + Multiply over `'123`, `Total`, `=NA()` and `=B3*2` gave 1, 1, 1 and the constant 8.

Excel's behaviour, now followed:
- numbers stored as text take part, so they become numbers (`'123` × 1 = 123; this is the usual way to convert them);
- other text and error values are left as they are;
- a formula is kept and combined with the pasted number: `=(B3*2)*1`.

- New test `paste_special_operations_keep_text_errors_and_formulas` fails before the change (each of its four cases).
- fmt, clippy (apart from the existing `date.rs` lint) and the engine tests pass.

title: Current region: grow past 10,000 rows, in linear time
author: nihilist-narwhal
body:
`selection::current_region` is the range Ctrl+A, sort, filter, AutoSum, tables and Get Data use when one cell is selected. It grew the region by one ring of cells per step, rescanning every stored cell inside the ring each time, and gave up after 10,000 steps. With 20,000 rows of data in A1:B20001 and A2 selected, `data.sortDescending` sorted only rows 2–10,002 and left the rest as they were (A2 became 10001, not 20000). A 100,000-row region took 30 s and was cut at row 10,001.

It now grows one side at a time while the line next to that side has data (diagonals included), checking only the cells of that line, with no step limit. The same 100,000 × 100 region takes well under a second.

- The new assertion in `selection::tests::regions` (20,000 rows) fails before the change (`A1:B10006`).
- fmt, clippy (apart from the existing `date.rs` lint), the workspace tests, assets, layers and parity pass.

title: Whole-sheet selection: Fill and Remove Duplicates no longer run out of memory or time
author: nihilist-narwhal
body:
With the whole sheet selected, these commands worked on all 17 billion cells:

- `gridcraft-cli run --cmd edit.selectAll --cmd edit.fillLeft` on a new workbook ran for 20 s, reached a 50–70 GB memory footprint and was killed. Fill Down, Right and Up did the same. On a sheet with data, Fill Up and Fill Left took their source row or column before narrowing the selection to the data, and filled up to row 1,048,576.
- `data.removeDuplicates` and `table.removeDuplicates` didn't finish within 8 s on an empty sheet.

Whole rows and columns now narrow to the used range before anything else, and the fills do nothing on an empty sheet. A fill of more than 5,000,000 cells is refused, as `edit.autoFill` already does. Remove Duplicates works on the active cell of an empty sheet. (AutoSum had the same problem; it is fixed in `fix-autosum`.)

Second commit: given whole columns (`{"range":"D:D"}`), Remove Duplicates compared a million blank rows and reported 1,048,573 removed duplicates; given the whole sheet, or on a table resized to the whole sheet, it ran for minutes. Rows and columns past the used range are blank, so they are now left out: the result is the same and the counts match the data.

Third commit: `edit.autoFill` capped its target at 5,000,000 cells but not its source. With `{"source":"A1:XFD1048576","target":"A1"}` it read the whole sheet one column at a time and didn't finish (killed after 60 s). The source now has the same cap.

- `whole_sheet_selection_stays_within_the_data` covers each command. Every command was also run after selecting `A1:XFD1048576`, on an empty sheet and on one with data: none takes over 3 s or 2 GB now.
- fmt, clippy (apart from the existing `date.rs` lint), the workspace tests, assets, layers and parity pass.

title: selection.move: Ctrl+arrow without a direction no longer loops forever
author: nihilist-narwhal
body:
`selection.jump()` looks for the next filled cell by stepping `(dr, dc)`. With neither set, as in `selection.move {"jump": true}` from an agent call that leaves out `dr` and `dc`, the step never moved, so from a blank cell of a sheet with content the command never returned. Repro: `gridcraft-cli run --cmd home.decreaseDecimal --cmd 'selection.move={"jump":true}'`. It now returns the cell it started from.

- The new assertion in `selection::tests::jumps` hangs before the change.
- fmt, clippy (apart from the existing `date.rs` lint), the workspace tests, assets, layers and parity pass.

title: Repeated headers: number pivot fields and table columns in linear time
author: nihilist-narwhal
body:
Making repeated headers unique (`x`, `x2`, `x3`…) checked each candidate against every name before it, once per suffix tried, which is cubic when headers repeat. Recommended PivotTables over 4,000 equal headers took 28 s, and a row of check boxes across a selected row (16,384 `FALSE` headers) hung the app, in PivotTables, in Insert Table and in Get Data from Table/Range. Repro: `selection.set {"range":"1:1"}`, `insert.checkbox`, then `insert.recommendedPivotTables` or `data.fromTableRange`. Taken names and the next suffix of each header now live in a hash set and map, in `pivot::read_source`, in table creation and in the XLSX writer's pivot cache; the names are the same as before.

- `repeated_headers_get_numbered_names` checks the names (`a`, `A2`, `a3`, `a22`, …, `x3000`) for the pivot source and the table, and that each takes under 2 s; the pivot part takes 6 s before the change.
- fmt, clippy (apart from the existing `date.rs` lint), the workspace tests, assets, layers and parity pass.

title: Ranges keep their size past the used range; spilled blanks show 0
author: nihilist-narwhal
body:
A multi-cell reference was read only up to the sheet's used range. With 5 and 6 in A1:A2, `=ROWS(A1:A10*1)` gave 2 (Excel: 10), and `COUNTBLANK(A1:A10)`, `COUNTIF(A1:A10,"")` and `SUMPRODUCT(--(A1:A10=""))` counted only the blanks inside the used range. The results also depended on unrelated cells, and went stale: entering a value further down grew the used range without recalculating the formula.

References of up to 16,384 cells now keep their size. Larger ones (`A:A`, ranges reserved for data to come such as `$A$2:$A$50000`) still stop at the used range, so formulas over them stay as fast as before. The limit is a trade-off: with a 65,536-cell limit, 1,000 `SUMPRODUCT`/`COUNTIFS` formulas over `$A$2:$B$50000` holding 1,000 rows of data took 1.4 s instead of 0.13 s.

Second commit: a blank cell in a formula's result shows 0, but blanks inside an array result spilled as blank cells. `=A1:A3`, or `FILTER`/`SORT`/`TAKE` of a range with blanks, left cells that `ISBLANK` saw as blank and `COUNT` skipped; Excel shows 0 in each. Array results now show 0 for blank cells too. GROUPBY and PIVOTBY keep the blank cells of their own layout.

Fixes #137 (its COUNTBLANK repros give 6, 5, 4 and 4 with this branch).

- `references_keep_their_size_past_the_used_range` and `spilled_blank_cells_show_zero` fail before the change.
- fmt, clippy (apart from the existing `date.rs` lint), the workspace tests, assets, layers and parity pass.

title: Legacy array formulas: fill the range they were entered in
author: nihilist-narwhal
body:
A Ctrl+Shift+Enter array formula was evaluated like a dynamic array:

- Read from a file, the cached values in its range were kept as constants, so the formula showed `#SPILL!`. Any multi-cell array formula in a file saved by Excel or LibreOffice opened this way. Repro: an xlsx with `<f t="array" ref="C2:C4">B2:B3*2</f>` and cached values in C3:C4.
- Entered with `cell.set {cell:"C2", input:"=B2:B3*2", array:true}` over C2:C4, C4 stayed blank where Excel shows `#N/A`. A single-cell array formula spilled.
- On save, the values of its other cells weren't cached.

The result is now fitted to the range, as Excel does: a single row or column repeats across it, cells past the result show `#N/A`, and a larger result is cut off. A range of more than 16 million cells gives `#NUM!` rather than allocating every cell. Reading drops the cached values inside the range, entering clears the range, and saving caches its values. The formula bar shows the formula in braces, `{=B2:B3*2}`.

- `legacy_array_formulas_fill_their_range` (calc), `legacy_array_entry` (engine) and the extended `shared_formulas_and_value_types` fixture (xlsx) fail before the change.
- fmt, clippy (apart from the existing `date.rs` lint), the workspace tests, assets, layers and parity pass.

title: Recalc: formulas over a blocked spill see #SPILL!; no spilling in tables
author: nihilist-narwhal
body:
A dynamic array that couldn't spill was only rejected when results were written back, after formulas evaluated later in the same pass had read the array as if it had spilled:

1. Fill A1:C3 with 1, then set B2 to `=SEQUENCE(2,2,9)` (blocked: `#SPILL!`) and E1 to `=SUM(A1:C3)` (`#SPILL!`, as in Excel).
2. `formulas.calculateNow`, or save and reopen: B2 still shows `#SPILL!`, but E1 becomes 47.

A reader whose reference is only known while evaluating isn't in the dependency graph, so it went wrong even cell by cell: with 5 in E4, `=SUM(OFFSET(E2,0,0,2,2))` in E8 and then `=SEQUENCE(2,2,3)` in E3 (blocked), E8 showed 7.

The spill area is now checked as soon as the array is computed (the same test as at write-back: off the sheet, merged cells, other cells, other formulas' spills), so the anchor is `#SPILL!` for everything evaluated after it. Another formula's old spill doesn't count when that formula is recalculated in the same pass, as at write-back (so `=SEQUENCE(2,2)` in C8 still takes over the old area of C7's array that it blocks). The check walks only the cells of the area, so 20,000 spilling formulas recalculate as fast as before.

Found by checking, after random edits, that values equal those of a full recalculation.

Second commit: Excel doesn't support spilled arrays in tables ("Spill range in table"): `=SEQUENCE(2)` entered in a table cell shows `#SPILL!`. GridCraft spilled it over the table's cells. An array whose formula is in a table is now blocked, both when it is computed and at write-back. (Arrays from outside spilling into a table's empty cells are left as they were: I'm not sure what Excel does there.)

- New tests `blocked_spill_reads_as_spill_error`, `blocked_spill_read_through_offset` and `arrays_do_not_spill_in_tables` fail before their changes (47, 3 and a spilled 1); `spill_into_the_old_area_of_a_blocked_neighbour` guards the same-pass case.
- fmt, clippy (apart from the existing `date.rs` lint) and the calc, engine and xlsx tests pass.

title: Charts: combo and stock charts keep their kind in XLSX
author: nihilist-narwhal
body:
Combo and stock charts reopened as clustered columns. Repro: `insert.chart {"type":"combo","range":"A1:E7"}` (or `"stock"`), save, reopen.

A combo chart whose series have no kind of their own (as `insert.chart` makes them) was written as a single column group. Its series are now written as they're drawn: the first as columns, the others as lines. A stock chart was written as clustered columns; it is now a `stockChart` group, or lines when it doesn't have the 3 or 4 series a stock chart needs.

- `every_chart_kind_survives_xlsx` fails before the change. The written files open in Excel for Mac and show the right chart kinds.
- fmt, clippy (apart from the existing `date.rs` lint), the workspace tests, assets, layers and parity pass. The branch merges cleanly with #62.

title: functions: MIN() accepts zero arguments
author: itrycodinganditsbad
body:
MIN() returned #VALUE! instead of 0.

MIN was registered with a minimum of one argument, so the dispatcher rejected the empty call before the aggregate ran. Microsoft's MIN documentation makes the first argument optional and says MIN returns 0 when there are no numbers. The aggregate already returned 0 for an empty list, so only the registered arity was wrong.

The fix lowers MIN's minimum argument count from 1 to 0. I followed Microsoft's MIN documentation here; I did not run Excel.

MAX is unchanged. Its documented first argument is required, so =MAX() is not covered by this fix. MINA and MAXA are also unchanged.

Tested with a new assertion in `min_max_order` in `crates/functions/src/stat.rs` that checks `MIN()` returns 0. It failed before the change (`expected number 0, got Error(Value)`) and passes after. `gridcraft-cli eval '=MIN()'` now prints 0, and the non-empty controls (`=MIN(A1:A10)`, `=MIN(2,3)`) are unchanged. `cargo xtask ci` passes.

Fixes #138

title: fill: clamp month and year date series to the month's last day
author: itrycodinganditsbad
body:
Filling a monthly date series from Jan 31 skipped February: the next value was Mar 3, then Apr 3. The month and year steps passed the previous cell's day straight into a DATE-style helper, which rolls an out-of-range day into the following month. Feb 29 stepped by year had the same problem, and so did the autofill month pattern (for example Jan 31 and Mar 31 dragged on).

Each filled value is now the start date plus n months, with the day clamped to the last day of the target month. The clamp is not carried forward, so 2026-01-31 gives Jan 31, Feb 28, Mar 31, Apr 30, and 2028-01-31 gives Feb 29. This follows Microsoft's documented month-end example for Range.DataSeries (Jan 31, 1996 gives the last day of every month), which the issue cites. I didn't run Excel. A year step from Feb 29 lands on Feb 28 in non-leap years and returns to Feb 29 in leap years. Mid-month seeds are unchanged.

One helper in the fill module does the arithmetic and is used by the series command and the autofill month pattern.

New engine tests cover the Jan 31 series, the leap-year case, the 1996 example, Feb 29 by year, a mid-month control, and the autofill month pattern. They failed before the change and pass now. I also ran the CLI repro from the issue and it prints Jan 31, Feb 28, Mar 31, Apr 30, including after reopening the saved workbook. `cargo xtask ci` passes.

Fixes #132

title: Charts: histogram, box & whisker, waterfall, funnel, treemap and sunburst keep their kind through XLSX
author: nihilist-narwhal
body:
Combo, stock, histogram, box & whisker, waterfall, funnel, treemap and sunburst charts reopened as clustered columns. Repro: `insert.chart {"type":"waterfall","range":"A1:E7"}`, save, reopen.

- **Combo:** series with no kind of their own (as `insert.chart` makes them) were all written as columns. They are now written as they're drawn: the first as columns, the others as lines.
- **Stock:** written as a `stockChart` group. A chart without the 3 or 4 series a stock chart needs is written as lines.
- **Histogram, box & whisker, waterfall, funnel, treemap, sunburst:** Excel keeps these in `cx:chartSpace` ("chartex") parts. They are now written as Excel lays them out. Each is an `xl/charts/chartExN.xml` part whose data goes through hidden `_xlchart.v1.N` workbook names, with chart style and colour parts beside it, framed in the drawing by `mc:AlternateContent` with a text-box fallback. Fills are written out (series in theme accents, waterfall decreases and treemap/sunburst boxes in their own colours, a white chart area), so the chart doesn't depend on the style part to be painted. The reader reads chartex parts back, resolving the `_xlchart` names (which aren't kept as workbook names), along with data, title, axis titles, legend, labels and colours. It also follows `mc:AlternateContent`. Before, it skipped such charts in Excel's files.

- Each of the eight kinds round-trips through the engine (`every_chart_kind_survives_xlsx`, which fails before the change). A hand-written chartex drawing in Excel's layout is read back, and a test checks the written package (names, style and colour parts, content types).
- fmt, clippy (apart from the existing `date.rs` lint), the workspace tests, assets, layers and parity pass. The branch merges cleanly with #62, and it still builds with #62 merged.


The files open and paint in Excel for Mac (checked for waterfall, treemap and the other four kinds). Builds on #158 (combo and stock), whose commit is included here; review that one first.

title: de-DE language support: German interface, numbers and formulas
author: madara904
body:
GridCraft's interface can now be shown in **German**, including numbers, dates and formulas the way German Excel shows them (`1.234,56 €`, `10.10.2026`, `=SUMME(A1;2,5)`). This brings in the catalog-based i18n system the other Crafting Apps use (PdfCraft, PhotoCraft, WordCraft: `crates/ui-egui/src/i18n`) and adds German on top.

## How it works
- **English stays the source.** Strings in the code remain the lookup keys and are unchanged. A TSV catalog per language maps them to display text when the UI is drawn, and anything without an entry shows in English, so English users see exactly what they did before.
- **The `language` setting** is `auto` by default and follows the system through `sys-locale` (`GRIDCRAFT_LANGUAGE` overrides it). **View ▸ Language** picks one, `ui.language` does the same for scripts and agents, and the choice persists with the other UI preferences. No font files are added.
- **Translated at draw time:** ribbon tabs and widget helpers, menus, the generic dialog form (fields, choices, notes, titles), Format Cells, Find, Sort, panes, PivotTable fields, the status bar, sheet tabs, context menus, About, and command search (it matches English and German).
- **Unchanged for scripts and agents:** command ids, workbook contents, stored formulas, the CLI, MCP and control-channel results stay English and en-US.

## The German catalog
- **`de.tsv`, 1,063 entries.** Feature names are the terms German Excel users know: Start, Einfügen, Seitenlayout, Formeln, Daten, Überprüfen, Ansicht, Bedingte Formatierung, Als Tabelle formatieren, Zellenformatvorlagen, AutoSumme, Fenster fixieren, Sortieren und Filtern. CLAUDE.md allows feature names.
- **Clean room:** no string table or localisation file was copied. Messages and explanations are our own wording.
- **Scoped entries** (`Group › Label`, looked up with `i18n::t_at`) cover the words German Excel names two ways:
  - Font: Schriftart / Schrift (Format Cells tab)
  - Fill: Füllbereich / Ausfüllen
  - Size: Größe…

title: macOS: open documents from Finder, the Dock and `open -a` (#69)
author: LloydNicholson
body:
Fixes #69.

## Problem
Double-clicking a workbook in Finder, Open With, dropping a file on the Dock icon and `open -a GridCraft book.xlsx` show "GridCraft cannot open files in the "Excel Workbook" format". File > Open and drag-and-drop onto the window work.

## Cause
LaunchServices doesn't pass these paths on the command line. It sends the app a `kAEOpenDocuments` ('odoc') Apple event, and winit 0.30 doesn't handle it.

## Fix
This uses the same approach PdfCraft and PhotoCraft already ship: the audited [`fmv-macos-events`](https://crates.io/crates/fmv-macos-events) crate, pinned to `=0.1.0`.
- It registers an `NSAppleEventManager` handler before Finder's launch event and leaves winit's delegate alone.
- The Objective-C interop stays inside that crate, so the workspace keeps `unsafe_code = "forbid"`.
- `apps/gridcraft/src/apple_events.rs` drains the queue each frame. Each path goes through `SheetApp::open_path`, the same as File > Open. A quit event closes the window.
- The registration lives in `main()` until the event loop returns, so the event that launched the app is caught too.

#18 fixes the same issue a different way: it adds `application:openURLs:` to winit's delegate class with `class_addMethod`, in a new crate that needs `unsafe`. This PR is the alternative that keeps the code safe and matches the sibling apps. Merge whichever fits better.

## Testing
Tested on macOS (Apple silicon) with a full `packaging/macos/package.sh` build installed in /Applications:
- [x] `open -a GridCraft book.xlsx` with the app not running: the workbook opens, no error dialog.
- [x] `open -a GridCraft data.csv` while it's running: it opens as a second document.
- [x] An Apple-event quit (`osascript -e 'tell application "GridCraft" to quit'`) closes the app.
- [x] `cargo xtask ci`: all 7 steps pass (fmt, clippy, test, assets, layers, wasm, parity).

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: Linux: default to XWayland for file drag-and-drop on Wayland desktops
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
### Rationale & History

Under Wayland sessions, dragging and dropping spreadsheet files or media from desktop file managers onto GridCraft showed a "no" (prohibited) cursor and drops did not arrive.

This occurs because `eframe 0.36.2` depends on `winit 0.30.13`. In `winit 0.30`, Wayland drag-and-drop was not implemented ([winit#1881](https://github.com/rust-windowing/winit/issues/1881)). Native Wayland drag-and-drop was added for `winit 0.31` in [winit#4571](https://github.com/rust-windowing/winit/pull/4571) (merged July 2026, tagged in `0.31.0-beta.3`). However, updating to `winit 0.31` directly is blocked by breaking event loop API changes until upstream `eframe` adds support.

On X11 / XWayland, drag-and-drop is fully supported in `winit 0.30`. This pull request adopts the established pattern from `designcraft` and `deckcraft` by Brandon Thomas:
1. Adds `winit = { version = "0.30", default-features = false, features = ["x11"] }` under `cfg(all(unix, not(target_os = "macos")))`.
2. Adds an event loop builder hook before running the native event loop: when an X server is reachable (`DISPLAY` is set) and `GRIDCRAFT_WAYLAND` is not set, configures `EventLoopBuilderExtX11::with_x11()` to route through XWayland so file drops work out of the box on standard Wayland desktop sessions.
3. Allows users desiring pure native Wayland to opt out and preserve the native Wayland backend by setting `GRIDCRAFT_WAYLAND=1`.

### Verification
Verified local compilation and dependency resolution with `cargo check -p gridcraft` on Linux (0 errors, 0 warnings).

title: Open workbooks from Finder and Dock-icon reopen (macOS)
author: DDKatch
body:
Closes #166.

## Problem

GridCraft is the default app for `.xlsx`. The user double-clicks a workbook in Finder.

- macOS shows an alert: *"GridCraft cannot open files in the 'Excel Workbook' format."*
- The alert is modal. The app never creates its first window, so it looks frozen.
- Dock-icon reopen (clicking the Dock icon while the app runs with no windows) does nothing.

Both reproduce with `open -a GridCraft.app workbook.xlsx`. Full cause analysis in #166.

## Fix

Four commits:

1. `core, numfmt, functions: satisfy clippy 1.97 float range lints` — pre-existing gate failures, unrelated to the fix; needed to make `cargo xtask ci` green.
2. `macos-events: Apple Events shim for files opened from Finder and Dock reopen` — new crate `gridcraft-macos-events`:
   - adds `application:openURLs:`, `application:openFiles:`, `application:openFile:` and `applicationShouldHandleReopen:` to `NSObject`, process-local. winit's delegate inherits them, so launch-time and running-instance opens land in the crate's queue;
   - registers `NSAppleEventManager` handlers for `odoc` / `rapp` as a second path (AppleScript, and `open` targeting a running instance);
   - the app polls the queue each frame and opens the paths; Dock reopen opens the last workbook when no document is open.
3. `app: open workbooks from Finder and Dock-icon reopen (macOS)` — wiring in `apps/gridcraft`: install the shim before the event loop, poll it each frame, defer blank-workbook creation on macOS so a Finder-opened workbook is the only document.
4. `release: refuse unsigned or unnotarized macOS artifacts` — release gate: `import-cert.sh` exits 0 when `APPLE_CERTIFICATE` is missing, so a fork or a CI run with stale secrets ships an ad-hoc DMG while the job stays green — and every user sees the *"Apple could not verify"* Gatekeeper alert. New `packaging/macos/verify-release.sh` mounts each DMG, requires a Developer ID signature and a stapled notarization ticket on the DMG and a spctl-accepted binary in the CLI…

title: Rename sheet-qualified defined names with their sheet (#134)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #134.

The parser stores a sheet-qualified defined name such as `Data!MyName` as one `Expr::Name` string. `rename_sheet` only rewrote `Expr::Ref`, so after renaming `Data` to `Numbers`, cell references were updated but `Data!MyName` stayed and the formula stopped calculating.

`rename_sheet` now also rewrites an `Expr::Name` whose sheet prefix matches the old sheet (case-insensitive, like sheet references), and quotes the new sheet name when it needs quotes (`'New Name'!MyName`), using the same `quote_sheet` as references. Unqualified names and names qualified with other sheets do not change.

Test: `rename_sheet_updates_qualified_names` in `crates/formula/src/tests.rs`. It fails without the fix.

title: Clamp table style number to 1 so zero-numbered styles don't underflow (#130)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #130.

`parse_style_name` parsed `TableStyleLight0` / `TableStyleMedium0` as number 0, and `look()` then computes `(n - 1) / 7` in the Light and Medium branches. In a build with overflow checks that panics, so `table.convertToRange` (and anything else that styles table cells) failed with an internal error for these names, whether they came from `insert.table`, `table.style` or a saved workbook.

The fix clamps the parsed number to at least 1 in `parse_style_name`, since the gallery starts at 1. Every caller goes through this one function, so all entry paths are covered. A zero style now looks like style 1. The Dark branch never subtracted, and `accent_for` already used `saturating_sub`. The pivot-style parser in `pivot.rs` also uses `saturating_sub`, so it had no such bug.

The issue also allowed rejecting the name with an error. I kept the change small: unknown or non-numeric suffixes already fall back to a default style without an error, and a zero suffix now does the same.

Test: `tables::tests::zero_numbered_styles_do_not_underflow` checks that Light0/Medium0 parse to number 1 and that `look()` does not panic for Light0, Medium0 and Dark0. Without the fix the asserts fail (and `look()` panics in a debug test build).

title: Keep the untouched part of a data validation range when clearing or replacing part of it (#129)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #129.

`data.validation` (used by the CLI, MCP, the Data ribbon's Clear Validation and the rule dialog) only removed an old rule's range when the target fully contained it. A partial clear left the whole old range in place, and a partial replacement kept the old range first in the list, so lookups (which take the first rule covering the cell) still used the old limits in the overlap.

Both the `clear` path and the replace path now go through one helper, `remove_validation_cells`, which subtracts the target ranges from every existing rule's ranges (`subtract_range` splits a rectangle into up to four non-overlapping rectangles around the cut). Cells outside the target keep their old rule; rules left with no ranges are dropped, as before. Full-range clear and replace behave exactly as they did.

Covers both reported sequences:
- Clear B2 inside B1:B3: B2 accepts `999`, B1 and B3 stay restricted to 1..10.
- Apply 100..200 to B2:B4 over B1:B3: B2, B3 and B4 accept `150` and reject `5`; B1 keeps accepting `5` and rejecting `150`.

Test: `partial_validation_edits_keep_the_rest_of_the_old_rule` in `crates/engine/src/cmd/data.rs` runs both sequences through `Session::execute`; it fails on main (B2 still rejects `999`).

title: Keep comma when a semicolon or tab is missing from some CSV lines (#127)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #127.

`sniff_delimiter` scored each candidate by `(min count per line, total)`. When no candidate appeared on every line, all minima were 0 and the highest total won. A one-column export such as `alpha;beta` / `gamma` therefore came back split on `;` (or tab) as soon as it was re-imported.

Changes in `crates/xlsx/src/csv.rs`:
- A semicolon or tab is only chosen when it appears on every sampled line (`min > 0`); otherwise comma, the existing default, stays.
- Blank lines are skipped while sampling. Without this, a semicolon file with an empty line in the middle would now fall back to comma.

Tests (`delimiter_sniffing`): the issue's semicolon and tab round-trip inputs now sniff as comma (both fail on main), and `a;b` / blank / `c;d` still sniffs as semicolon. Existing sniffing cases are unchanged.

title: Deliver Export as PDF as a browser download (#141)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #141.

On the web build, `file.exportPdf` runs without a `path`, so the engine returns the PDF as base64 (`crates/engine/src/cmd/print.rs`, `export_pdf`). Nothing in the UI picked that result up, so the command palette's **Export as PDF** closed and nothing happened.

`SheetApp::run` now checks the result of `file.exportPdf`. If it has no `path` and the host provides `Services::download`, it decodes the base64 and hands the bytes to the browser as `<workbook title>.pdf`. This is the same route **Save As** already uses on the web (`file.saveBytes` -> `services.download`). The command palette, like every other UI command route, runs commands through `run_or_alert` -> `SheetApp::run`, so the fix covers it there.

Scope: web only. A native host has no `download` service, and an export with a `path` (native, CLI, automation) already writes the file, so those paths do not change.

Test: `export_as_pdf_is_delivered_as_a_download` in `crates/ui-egui/tests/file_menu.rs` runs `file.exportPdf` with a capturing `download` service. It checks that exactly one `.pdf` file starting with `%PDF-` is delivered. Without the fix, nothing is delivered and the test fails.

title: Shrink 3-D sheet spans when an end sheet is deleted (#140)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #140.

Deleting the first or last sheet of a 3-D span (`=SUM(Sheet1:Sheet3!A1)`) left the deleted name in the span, so the formula returned `#REF!`. `adjust::delete_sheet` only handled single-sheet references (`Reference::sheet_name` is `None` for a span).

Now, as in Excel ("Delete an endpoint"), the deleted end moves one sheet towards the other end:

- delete `Sheet1` -> `SUM(Sheet2:Sheet3!A1)` (12 in the issue's workbook)
- delete `Sheet3` -> `SUM(Sheet1:Sheet2!A1)` (8)
- delete `Sheet2` (interior) -> unchanged (10), as before
- a span left with one sheet becomes a plain reference (`Sheet1:Sheet2!A1` -> `Sheet2!A1`); a reversed span keeps its direction
- direct references to the deleted sheet still become `#REF!`

`delete_sheet` now takes the tab order from before the deletion; `home.deleteSheet` passes it for both cell formulas and defined names, so names that use a span are fixed too.

Tests: `formula::tests::delete_sheet_shrinks_3d_span` (first/last/interior/reversed/two-sheet spans) and `engine::tests::deleting_a_3d_span_end_sheet_keeps_the_rest`, which runs the issue's repro through `home.deleteSheet` and checks the values 12 / 8 / 10 and the `#REF!` direct-reference control.

title: Honor search in the desktop engine.commands handler so connected list_commands filters (#136)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #136.

MCP `list_commands` forwards `search` to the desktop `engine.commands` control method when connected (`--connect`), but that handler ignored it and always returned the full inventory. So `search: "border"` still included `home.bold`.

The handler now applies the same filter as the headless backend (`crates/mcp/src/headless.rs`): it keeps commands whose id, label or ribbon path (`menu`) contains the query, ASCII case-insensitive. The filter runs on the combined list, so the UI-only records (`ui.ribbonTab`, `view.darkMode`, ...) stay when they match. They have no `menu`, so for them only id and label count. Without `search` the full connected inventory is returned unchanged.

Only the desktop handler changes. The headless path already filtered correctly.

`docs/control-protocol.md` and the module docs now list the optional `search` param for `engine.commands`.

Test: `control::tests::search_filters_case_insensitively` checks the cases from the issue: `border` drops `home.bold`, `BORDER` gives the same result as `border`, `ribbon` keeps the UI-only `ui.ribbonTab`, a ribbon-path match (`font`), a query with no match gives an empty list, and no search keeps everything.

title: Report an error when file commands get no file in MCP and CLI (#135)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #135.

With no UI, `file.open` without `path`/`base64` and `file.saveAs` without `path` queued an open/save dialog, the headless MCP backend and the CLI dropped it, and the call returned `null` as a success. The `execute_command` description and AGENTS.md promise the opposite: "Programmatic calls never open dialogs: missing required params give an error."

## Change

- New `Session::execute_headless`: runs the command, drops queued UI requests, and when the command only queued an `open`/`saveAs` file dialog, returns `BadParams`, e.g. `invalid parameters for `file.open`: missing `path` or `base64`: programmatic calls never open dialogs`. The wording matches the engine's other missing-parameter errors (`missing `range``, `missing `what``...).
- The headless MCP backend (`crates/mcp/src/headless.rs`) and the CLI `exec` helper both use it, so `gridcraft-cli run --cmd file.open` now exits non-zero with that message.
- The same silent success happened on other paths that queue the same dialogs, so they are covered too: `file.save` on a workbook that has no file yet (new, or imported from ODS/XLSB) and `data.getData` / `data.fromTextCsv` with no `path` or `text`.
- The desktop app does not use `execute_headless`, so menu and shortcut Open/Save As still open their dialogs. The remote MCP backend forwards to the running app, so it is not affected either.

This follows the rule CADCraft applied in storytold/cadcraft#125 ("JSON calls never open file pickers"): programmatic file commands with no file report the missing path instead of asking for one.

## Test plan

- [x] New `file_commands_without_a_file_fail` in `crates/mcp/src/tests.rs`: `execute_command` for `file.open`, `file.saveAs`, `file.save` (on the blank Book1), `data.getData` and `data.fromTextCsv`, with no `params` and with `{}`, must return `isError: true` with the missing-parameter message. On `main` each returns `null` with `isError: false`, so the test fails there.
- [x] Existing engine tests that check th…

title: Write comment and hyperlink maps with A1 keys so JSON save works (#126)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #126.

`Sheet::comments` and `Sheet::hyperlinks` are `BTreeMap<CellRef, _>`, and `CellRef` serializes as a struct. JSON object keys must be strings, so `serde_json` refused any workbook with a note, comment or hyperlink (`key must be a string`). Every JSON entry point goes through `io::save_bytes`, so `convert … .json`, `--out x.json`, `file.saveBytes {"format":"json"}` and `file.saveAs` all failed.

Fix: a small serde helper (`crates/model/src/cellmap.rs`) writes those two map keys as A1 text (`"A1"`) and parses them back with `CellRef::parse` on load. A key that doesn't parse gives a normal deserialize error, not a panic. These are the only `CellRef`-keyed maps that get serialized (`spill` and `spill_ranges` are `#[serde(skip)]`). Old JSON files still open: before this change, a workbook could only be saved as JSON when both maps were empty (`{}`), and that reads the same way.

Tests:
- `cellmap::tests::comments_and_hyperlinks_survive_json` (model): a threaded comment with a reply and a hyperlink with a tooltip go through JSON and come back the same.
- `tests::notes_comments_and_links_survive_a_json_save` (engine): runs the commands from the issue (`review.newNote`, `review.newComment`, `insert.link`), saves with `io::save_bytes(.., "book.json")`, reopens with `io::open_bytes`, and checks that notes, comments, links and cell values match.

Both fail on `main` with `key must be a string` and pass with the fix.

title: Compare numbers at 15 significant digits like Excel (#57)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #57.

Excel and LibreOffice treat two numbers as equal when they agree to 15 significant digits. GridCraft compared raw `f64` values, so `=0.1+0.2=0.3` returned FALSE, and `MATCH(0.3,…,0)` and `COUNTIF(…,0.3)` missed cells that display `0.3`.

**Change**
- New `gridcraft_core::compare_numbers(a, b)`. It rounds both numbers to 15 significant digits and then compares them. Identical values return early without rounding. Non-finite values and zero are left unchanged.
- `compare()` uses it for number/number and number/blank. This covers every place that reaches numbers through `compare()`:
  - the `=` `<>` `<` `>` `<=` `>=` operators
  - approximate MATCH, VLOOKUP and XLOOKUP
  - conditional formatting
  - sort order
- `criteria.rs`: COUNTIF, SUMIF and the other `*IF(S)` functions compare numeric criteria with it.
- `lookup_equal` uses it for number/number. This is the exact-match path of MATCH, VLOOKUP and XLOOKUP.

The issue's five repro cases now match Excel: `TRUE`, `TRUE`, `eq`, `2` and `1`. Values that differ in the 15th significant digit stay different.

The issue's side note (ROUND to 15 or more digits keeps the noise) is a separate issue and is not changed here.

**Tests**
- `value.rs`:
  - `0.1+0.2 = 0.3` and `1.1*3 = 3.3` are equal.
  - `0.1+0.2` is not greater than `0.3`.
  - `1` vs `1.00000000000001` (differs in the 15th digit) stays Less.
- `criteria.rs`: `COUNTIF` with criterion `0.3` matches `0.1+0.2`, and exact lookup equality does too.

title: Release focus when the sheet tab rename ends (#145)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #145.

**Cause.** The sheet tab rename field called `request_focus()` on every frame. When you press Enter or click somewhere else, the `TextEdit` gives up focus, but the next line took it back straight away. Because of that, `lost_focus()` never became true. The new name was never saved, the field never closed, and the keyboard stayed in the sheet name.

**Fix.** The field now asks for focus only while it does not have it and did not lose it on this frame (`rename_needs_focus` in `crates/ui-egui/src/tabs.rs`). The commit / Escape handling that already existed now runs as intended. Both ways of starting a rename (double-click and the context menu "Rename") use the same field, so this fixes both. The bug is in shared egui code, so it was not only on macOS.

**Tests.**
- `crates/ui-egui/tests/sheet_tab_rename.rs` (egui_kittest, real input through the whole app):
  - `enter_saves_the_sheet_name_and_closes_the_field`: start a rename, press Enter, and check that the sheet has the new name and the field is closed. This test fails on main, because the field takes focus back and nothing is saved.
  - `clicking_a_cell_saves_the_sheet_name_and_closes_the_field`: the same check, but the rename ends with a click on a cell.
- A unit test for `rename_needs_focus`.

title: M12: Excel-style languages (12 languages, local formulas, regional formats)
author: quantmind-br
body:
## Summary

GridCraft in 12 languages, working the way Excel does:

- **Interface language**: ribbon, menus, dialogs, messages, native menus and app-created content (`Planilha1`, `Total Geral`, PivotTable captions).
- **Formula language** (the interface language by default, or en-US): function names, booleans, error values, structured-reference keywords, R1C1 letters and number-format letters (`=SE(A1>1,5;SOMA(B1:B3);0)`, `aaaa`, `JJJJ`).
- **Regional format**: decimal/group/list/array separators, dates, month and day names, AM/PM and currency (`{1\2;3\4}` in pt-BR, `{1.2;3.4}` in de-DE, `{1;2:3;4}` in ru-RU).

Storage stays canonical: `Formula.text`, XLSX, the journal and programmatic params keep English names, `,` arguments and `.` decimals, so a workbook opens identically in every language. Local text only crosses the engine boundary through `*Local` fields (`inputLocal`, `formulaLocal`, `valueLocal`, `numberFormatLocal`, `refersToLocal`).

Languages: en-US, pt-BR, pt-PT, es-ES, fr-FR, de-DE, it-IT, ru-RU, ja-JP, ko-KR, zh-CN, zh-TW. Japanese, Korean and Chinese keep English function names, as Excel does.

## What changed

| Area | Change |
|---|---|
| `crates/locale` (new, L0) | Language and region data in TOML, checked by `build.rs` (missing keys, duplicate local names, colliding separators, canonical en-US). CLDR-style negotiation of OS/browser tags (`pt_BR.UTF-8`, `pt-AO` → pt-PT, `zh-HK` → zh-TW, `C`/`POSIX` → en-US). |
| `crates/formula` | `tokenize_local` / `parse_local` / `print_local` per dialect. `catalog.rs` is the single function list with file prefixes and replaces the four hand-kept lists. `_xludf.` marks a canonical name typed in a localized dialect (`=SUM(1;2)` in pt-BR is `#NAME?`, as in Excel). |
| `core`, `numfmt`, `functions`, `calc` | Regional input parsing and text→number coercion, localized number-format codes and display (`[$-LCID]` honoured), TEXT/FIXED/DOLLAR, VALUE/DATEVALUE/NUMBERVALUE, `*IF(S)` and database criteria, CELL/INFO keyword…

title: Linux: the title bar carries the window controls, as in Excel
author: gyurix
body:
## What

On X11 the window manager draws its own title bar above the one the app already
has, so every window has two bars. Only the outer one carries minimize,
maximize and close, and it does not match the app it belongs to.

This turns the system frame off on Linux and FreeBSD and draws the controls in
the app's own title bar, which is where Word, Excel, PowerPoint and Acrobat put
them. The window still resizes, moves, maximizes and closes exactly as before.

## Why not leave the window manager's frame in place

It is not a matter of taste, in two places:

- **DeckCraft** draws the presentation full screen, and **PdfCraft** has a
  full-screen page view; in both, a system title bar would sit over the content.
- With client-side decorations the controls follow the app's own theme, so they
  stay legible in the dark theme instead of being a light bar on a dark window.

## How it was checked

Each app was built from this branch, installed as a `.deb` and driven with
`xdotool` on XFCE/xfwm4, 1920x1080:

| check | result |
|---|---|
| maximize / restore buttons | `_NET_WM_STATE` gains and loses `MAXIMIZED_HORZ`/`MAXIMIZED_VERT` |
| double-click on the title bar | same, in both directions |
| move by dragging the title bar | window moves |
| resize from all four edges | window resizes |
| resize from all four corners | window resizes diagonally |
| minimize, then reactivate | `_NET_WM_STATE_HIDDEN` set, then cleared |
| close | window closes, through the same unsaved-changes check |
| slideshow / full screen (DeckCraft, PdfCraft) | no controls drawn over the content |
| overlay screens (Backstage, palette) | controls stay reachable, drawn last |

## Compatibility

- macOS and Windows are untouched; both keep the system frame.
- `GRIDCRAFT_SYSTEM_TITLEBAR=1` keeps the window manager's title bar, for anyone who
  prefers it or whose window manager needs a frame to place the window.
- The three new tooltip strings (`Minimize`, `Maximize`, `Restore Down`) are
  added to eve…

title: Linux: the display theme asks the desktop, not winit
author: gyurix
body:
## What

`Display theme ▸ System` does not follow the system on Linux.

winit reports no system theme there: `ActiveEventLoop::system_theme()` is `None`
on every Linux desktop, in every version of winit. egui resolves
`ThemePreference::System` from exactly that value, so with the setting stored as
`systemTheme: true` the app fell back to light no matter what the desktop asked
for. macOS and Windows were unaffected; winit answers there.

## The fix

`desktop_theme` asks the XDG Desktop Portal's `Settings` interface for
`org.gnome.desktop.interface color-scheme`, on a thread of its own so no D-Bus
call is ever made from the frame loop. That schema name is asked first because
GNOME's portal and XFCE's both answer it; the older
`org.freedesktop.interface.color-scheme` is asked second, which is the one KDE's
portal answers. The first answer is delivered straight away and the frame loop
drains it each frame, so switching the desktop theme while GridCraft is running
is picked up within a few seconds.

egui offers no way to set `Options::system_theme` from outside, so where a
desktop answered, the app hands egui the concrete theme instead of `System`. That
changes only which `egui::ThemePreference` is stored internally — what is drawn
is identical on macOS and Windows, where winit answers and the same resolution
just happens a step earlier — and `ui.json` still records `systemTheme: true`, so
a saved file means exactly what it meant before.

`tests/system_theme.rs` asserted the internal `Options::theme_preference` rather
than the appearance; those two assertions now check the theme egui actually
resolved, which is what the rest of the test already checks.

## How it was checked

Built from this branch and run on XFCE with
`gsettings set org.gnome.desktop.interface color-scheme`:

| step | saved preference | drawn |
|---|---|---|
| fresh start, desktop dark | `systemTheme: true` | **dark** (was light) |
| desktop set to `prefer-light` | `systemTheme: true` | **light**, withi…

title: Linux: match the desktop scale instead of the panel's DPI
author: gyurix
body:
XRandR reports the panel's physical DPI while the desktop renders at 96, so winit scales every window up and the app looks zoomed for no reason. Pin WINIT_X11_SCALE_FACTOR to 1 in the desktop launcher so menu and panel launches match the desktop.

Same fix as the local WINIT_X11_SCALE_FACTOR=1 default; baked into the shipped launcher so installs work without system patches. Terminal launches can still export their own value.

title: Cell references: an invalid reference is an error instead of the active cell
author: mikl0s
body:
`cell_param` returned `None` for any cell argument it could not parse, so every command that falls back to the selection (`cell.set`, `view.freezePanes`, `formulas.trace*`, `insert.*` and others) silently used the active cell instead. It also dropped a sheet prefix, so "Other!B2" was applied to the active sheet.

Before:
- `cell.set {"cell":"ZZZZ0","input":"x"}` writes A1 and reports success.
- `cell.set {"cell":"Other!B2","input":"x"}` writes B2 on the active sheet.

Fix:
- `cell_param` returns `Result<Option<CellRef>>`. An absent or null value is still `None`, so the selection fallback is unchanged. An unparsable or non-string value is an error. A sheet prefix naming a sheet other than the one the command works on is an error.
- New `cell_param_on` is for commands that resolve their own sheet (cell.get, links, comments, notes, checkboxes, chart placement, paste): they accept a prefix naming that sheet. `cell.set` resolves its own target sheet and still writes to another existing sheet.

Tests: six new MCP tests: `set_cell_invalid_ref_is_error`, `cell_ref_boundaries_still_work`, `bad_ref_in_command_is_error`, `other_sheet_prefix_is_error`, `cross_sheet_cell_refs_resolve` and `text_to_columns_destination_follows_its_sheet`.
- Without the fix: `cargo test -p gridcraft-mcp --lib` runs 18 tests, 13 pass and 5 fail (the boundary test passes either way; it guards valid references).
- With the fix: 18 passed, 0 failed; `gridcraft-engine` 125 passed.
- `cargo xtask ci` passes on the patched tree.

Made with Opus 5.5 high.

title: Cell: cell.set without an input is an error
author: mikl0s
body:
`cell.set` treated a missing `input` as an empty string, so a call that forgot the input, or sent it under the wrong key, cleared the cell and reported success.

Before: `cell.set {"cell":"A1"}` clears A1 and returns success.

Fix: `cell.set` returns an error when neither `input` nor `value` is given, and leaves the cell alone. An explicit empty string still clears the cell.

Tests: new MCP test `cell_set_without_input_is_error` (a missing input is an error and the cell keeps its value; an explicit empty string still clears it).
- Without the fix: `cargo test -p gridcraft-mcp --lib` runs 13 tests, 12 pass and 1 fails.
- With the fix: 13 passed, 0 failed; `gridcraft-engine` 125 passed.
- `cargo xtask ci` passes on the patched tree.

Made with Opus 5.5 high.

title: Calc at Excel scale: topological recalc, lookup indexes, multi-threaded and background recalc, memory, shared formulas (#205)
author: arhammusheer
body:
Implements #205: recalculation that scales the way Excel's does. It brings lookups that no longer grow with the square of the data, multi-threaded recalculation, a desktop window that stays responsive during long recalculations, roughly half the memory, and fast opening of large XLSX files. It also fixes a wrong answer: on `main`, a long formula chain that reads against row order returns `#CIRC!`.

There are 8 commits, one per stage. Each passes `cargo xtask ci` on its own and has its own numbers in its message, so it reads best commit by commit.

## Results

Each figure is the median of 3 runs of `crates/engine/examples/perf.rs`, which this PR extends (every scenario checks its answers). The machine is an Apple M2 Pro (6 performance + 4 efficiency cores), release build, and each figure compares `main` at 90b3c41 with this branch. Sizes are 50,000 rows unless noted.

### Lookups and aggregates: algorithmic fixes

| Scenario | `main` | This PR | Speed-up |
|---|---|---|---|
| 10,000 exact VLOOKUPs over a 10,000-row table | 2,710 ms | 31 ms | **88×** |
| 10,000 XLOOKUPs | 3,244 ms | 35 ms | **92×** |
| 10,000 MATCHes | 2,109 ms | 29 ms | **73×** |
| Edit the table that 30,000 lookups read | 5,940 ms | 14 ms | **412×** |
| 100,000 VLOOKUPs over a 100,000-row table | 338 s | 0.50 s | **~670×** |
| 100,000 XLOOKUPs | 467 s | 0.55 s | **~850×** |
| 100,000 MATCHes | stopped after 900 s | 0.50 s | — |
| 1,000 × `SUM(A:A)` | 674 ms | 22 ms | **30×** |
| Edit A1 under 1,000 `SUM(A:A)` | 655 ms | 21 ms | **31×** |

### Recalculation

| Scenario | `main` | This PR | Speed-up |
|---|---|---|---|
| 20,000-cell chain, each cell reads the one below | **`#CIRC!` (wrong)** | 33 ms, correct | — |
| 20,000-cell chain, top to bottom | 45 ms | 27 ms | 1.7× |
| 10,000 formulas over a 1,000-cell array each | 2,062 ms | 327 ms | **6.3×** (all cores) |
| Edit A1 under those 10,000 heavy formulas | 2,088 ms | 319 ms | **6.6×** |
| Edit B1, everything below recalculates | 53 ms | 42 ms | 1.3×…

title: web: print straight to the system print dialog, not just export
author: Dejan-Port
body:
Resubmission of #143's print commit, rebased onto current main, split out from everything else per the maintainer's request there.

## What

The web build had no way to actually print — Ctrl+P (Cmd+P, declared on `file.print`'s shortcut) did nothing at all, and the ribbon's "Print…" menu item ran `file.print` and silently discarded the result. `file.print` already builds a PDF and returns it as base64 specifically "for the UI to hand to the system print dialog" per its own doc comment — this wires that up.

- ui-egui: new `Services::print` hook (web: hand PDF bytes to the browser's print flow directly, no download); `SheetApp::print_now` runs `file.print`, decodes the base64 result, and calls the hook.
- ui-egui: `Key::P` now dispatches to `print_now` (was unbound); the ribbon's "Print…" menu item calls `print_now` instead of discarding `file.print`'s result.
- gridcraft-web: implements the hook (Blob → object URL → hidden iframe → `iframe.contentWindow.print()` on load). The iframe and its blob URL are now cleaned up once the print dialog closes (listens for `afterprint`), so repeated prints don't leak them — per the review comment on #143.

Desktop builds are unaffected (no `Services::print` set there; `print_now` falls back to the existing alert-on-error behaviour with no UI action on success, same as before this change).

## Testing

`cargo test -p gridcraft-ui-egui` passes. Built and smoke-tested the web build: Ctrl+P and the ribbon's Print… both open the system print dialog, and the iframe/blob URL are gone from the DOM after the dialog closes.

title: fix: double-click the fill handle could hang on a sparse neighbour column
author: Dejan-Port
body:
## What

Double-clicking the fill handle fills down as far as the neighbouring column has data, by probing one row at a time until it finds an empty cell — capped at 1,000,000 rows so it couldn't literally run forever. But a million one-at-a-time cell lookups is itself long enough to feel like a hang, and the cap only kicks in that late: a single stray value far below the real data in the neighbouring column (not an unusual thing to have in a real spreadsheet someone's been using for a while) makes every double-click of the fill handle probe every empty row in between before it even reaches the value, let alone the cap.

## Fix

Lowered the cap to 10,000, which real double-click-fill usage never approaches (if you need to fill further than that you're using a formula or a drag, not a double-click) but which can't itself be felt as a hang.

## Testing

`cargo test -p gridcraft-ui-egui` passes (82 tests across the crate).
