title: Read the browser clock for NOW(), TODAY() and year-less dates on wasm (#202)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #202.

**Cause:** `now_serial()` in `crates/calc/src/recalc.rs` read the clock only off wasm (`std::time::SystemTime::now` traps on `wasm32-unknown-unknown`, see `clippy.toml`). In the browser it always returned the fixed fallback `46302.5`, which is 2026-10-07 12:00. `current_year()` in `crates/core/src/parse.rs` had the same pattern and always used 2026 for dates typed without a year.

**Fix:**
- New `gridcraft_core::date::unix_now_ms()` reads the clock: `SystemTime` on native (unchanged), `js_sys::Date::now()` on wasm. It returns `None` only when no clock is available.
- New `gridcraft_core::date::serial_from_unix_ms()` converts the result to a 1900-system serial. This is the same `25569 + days` formula as before.
- `now_serial()` and `current_year()` both use these functions. The fixed fallbacks stay only for the case where no clock is available.
- `js-sys` is a wasm-only dependency of `gridcraft-core`, declared the same way as in `apps/gridcraft-web` (`js-sys = "0.3"`). It is already in `Cargo.lock` (0.3.106), so no new crate is downloaded.

**Every place that reads the date goes through these two functions:** `NOW()` and `TODAY()` (`functions/src/date.rs`), conditional formatting "a date occurring" (`engine/src/cf.rs`), the print header and footer date and time (`engine/src/cmd/print.rs`), the ribbon's insert-today command (`ui-egui/src/ribbon.rs`), and m/d or d-mmm input without a year (`core/src/parse.rs`). No other date fallback remains in the repo.

Native behaviour does not change. The time stays UTC, as before.

**Test:** `date::tests::serial_from_unix_time` checks the conversion: the epoch gives 25569, and 2026-10-10T12:00Z gives 46305.5. It also checks that `unix_now_ms()` returns a current clock reading.

title: Do not draw the selection over the frozen pane when it lies only in the scrolling pane (#198)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #198.

With frozen rows or columns, all four panes are painted in one coordinate system and each pane only clips its own drawing. `paint_selection` ran once per pane and drew the whole selection every time, so a selection scrolled under the frozen columns/rows was painted on top of the frozen pane (the stray box in the issue screenshot).

What changed (`crates/ui-egui/src/grid.rs`, `chartview.rs`):

- **Selection** (the reported bug): each pane now draws only the parts of the selection that lie in its own rows/columns: the fill, the active cell, the current-range border, the fill handle, the fill and move drag previews, the formula-reference colours and the copy marquee. A selection that crosses the freeze line is still drawn in both panes.
- **Pointer, same cause:** the fill handle and the move border of a selection hidden under the frozen pane still reacted there (crosshair/move cursor, fill or move drag, double-click fill). They now react only in the panes where they are painted.
- **Other overlays with the same leak:** the data-validation dropdown arrow (and its click), the validation input message, and note popups are no longer shown for a cell scrolled entirely under the frozen rows/columns; the range outline of Trace Precedents/Dependents and the source-range outline of a selected chart are clipped to the panes that hold the range.

New helpers on `Geo`: `range_panes` (screen areas of the panes that hold a range) and `hidden_under_frozen` (cell scrolled entirely under the frozen rows/columns). Sheets without frozen panes behave as before.

Not changed: charts, pictures and shapes still float over the frozen panes, and Trace Precedents/Dependents arrows are drawn across them, as before. How objects and arrows anchored across the freeze line should behave is a separate decision.

Tests: four unit tests in `grid.rs` (`pane_tests`) cover the pane overlap check, cells scrolled under the frozen columns, clipping ranges to their panes, and the hidden fill hand…

title: Resize charts from the corner handle and the Size fields, keep typed chart and table names (#190)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #190. The issue reports two problems; both are fixed here.

**1. Dragging the sizing handle did nothing, with no resize cursor.**
A drag is only recognised after the pointer has moved past egui's threshold, and `interact` hit-tested the chart at that moved position. Dragging outward from the bottom-right corner had already left the chart, so the press missed it (or was more than 10 pt from the corner and became a move). The object press now uses `pointer.press_origin()`, the same point the header and cell drags in the same function already use. The selected object's corner now shows `ResizeNwSe` on hover and during the resize.

**2. The Format Chart Area Width/Height fields snapped back to 480 x 288.**
`format_chart` rebuilt `w`/`h` from the chart anchor every frame. egui's `DragValue` drops its edit text when the value it gets differs from the one it last parsed. So every keystroke was reverted, and a drag of the field committed the old size when you let go. The fields now keep a draft in egui memory while they are focused or dragged, commit it on release or focus loss, and drop it on Escape.

**Same bug elsewhere.** The Chart Title and axis-title fields in the same pane, and the Table Name field on the Table Design tab, had the same reload-every-frame pattern, so typed text disappeared. They now go through a small `widgets::committed_text` helper with the same draft approach. Escape cancels, as in sheet-tab rename (`tabs.rs`). The rest of the UI's text and number fields were checked: they write back to their dialog state every frame, so they were not affected.

`docs/chart-parity.md` no longer lists resize as broken.

Tests (real pointer and keyboard input through `egui_kittest`):
- `tests/chart_resize.rs`: corner drag resizes the chart and shows the resize cursor; typing `640` into Width, one key per frame, sets it; dragging the Width field grows the chart.
- `tests/committed_text_fields.rs`: typing a chart title and a table name commits them on Enter.

title: fix: Save toolbar button and saveChanges dialog discard an in-progress cell edit
author: Dejan-Port
body:
## Summary

Clicking the Save icon in the toolbar, or the **Save** button in the "save changes?" dialog, calls `file.save` directly without first committing a cell edit that's still in progress.

Repro: double-click a cell with existing content (or start typing a new value), then — instead of pressing Enter — click the Save toolbar icon with the mouse. The text sitting in `EditState` is never flushed into the document, so the saved file silently keeps the pre-edit value. No error, no indication anything was dropped.

The **File > Save** menu item already guards against this:

```rust
// File operations must include the cell the user is still editing.
if app.commit_edit(0, 0, false, false) {
    app.run_or_alert(id, json!({}));
}
```

(`crates/ui-egui/src/ribbon.rs`, `file_menu`). This PR applies the same guard to the two other places that trigger `file.save` without it: the toolbar Save icon, and the saveChanges dialog's Save button.

## Changes

- `crates/ui-egui/src/ribbon.rs`: toolbar Save icon now calls `app.commit_edit(0, 0, false, false)` before `file.save`, same as the File menu.
- `crates/ui-egui/src/dialogs.rs`: saveChanges dialog's Save button does the same.

`commit_edit` is a no-op returning `true` when there's no editor open, so this is safe on every save, not just mid-edit ones.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo check -p gridcraft-ui-egui`
- [x] Manual repro on a local build: double-click a filled cell, type a new value, click the Save toolbar icon (not Enter) — saved file now contains the new value.
- [ ] Maintainer confirmation on CI / existing UI test suite, if any covers toolbar interactions.

title: XLSX: bump quick-xml 0.38 -> 0.41 (RUSTSEC-2026-0195 namespace-declaration DoS)
author: pkibiego
body:
## What changed

`quick-xml` 0.38.4 -> 0.41.0 workspace-wide, plus the four API changes 0.41 requires. All of them are in `crates/xlsx`.

## Why

**RUSTSEC-2026-0195 is reachable from both the ODS and the XLSB reader.** Both parse untrusted package metadata and content through `quick_xml::NsReader`, and in 0.38.4 the namespace resolver pushes a binding for every `xmlns` / `xmlns:*` declaration on a start tag with no cap on how many there are. `NsReader::read_event` reaches that path, not only `read_resolved_event`.

None of our caps bound it. `MAX_PART` (512 MiB), `MAX_TOTAL` (1 GiB), `MAX_ENTRIES`, `MAX_CELLS`, `MAX_TEXT` and `MAX_DEPTH` bound part size, entry count, cells, text and nesting - never declarations per tag. The declarations are not text, so `MAX_TEXT` does not touch them either.

Measured with `gridcraft-cli info` on crafted `.ods` files, **before** this change:

| file on disk | declarations | peak RSS | exit |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 754 B (control) | 0 | 8.6 MB | 0 |
| 24 KB | 1,000,000 | 52.6 MB | 0 |
| 187 KB | 8,000,000 | 367.8 MB | 0 |
| 770 KB | 33,000,000 | **1.46 GB** | **0** |

About 45 bytes of resident memory per declaration, roughly 1,900x the file size, and no error at all. At `MAX_PART` a ~1 MB file reaches ~1.9 GB, and every part is held in memory while the package is read. A downloaded `.ods` or `.xlsb` was enough. Nothing panicked, so `Session::execute` never saw it and the never-crash net did not catch it - it is a silent allocation, not a crash.

**After** the bump, the same binary and the same four files:

| file on disk | peak RSS | exit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 754 B | 8.6 MB | 0, ok |
| 24 KB | 19 MB | 1 |
| 187 KB | 101.8 MB | 1 |
| 770 KB | 397 MB | 1 |

each with `start tag declares more than 256 namespace bindings`.

0.41.0 caps declarations per start tag at 256 (`DEFAULT_MAX_DECLARATIONS_PER_ELEMENT`, raisable through `NamespaceResolver::set_max_declarations_per_element`) and returns `NamespaceError::TooManyDeclarations…

title: selection.move: clamp extreme dr/dc to the sheet edge instead of overflowing
author: webdevtodayjason
body:
`selection.move` accepts `dr` and `dc` as any signed 64-bit number from the control channel, MCP or the CLI. `CellRef::offset` and `CellRef::offset_clamped` added them to the row and column with plain `+`, so a move like `{"dr": 9223372036854775807}` from B2 returned `Internal("selection.move", "attempt to add with overflow")`. With overflow checks off, as in release builds, the sum wrapped and the cursor landed on the opposite edge. Moving out of a merged cell had the same problem in `selection_move` itself, where a large `dr` also wrapped through `as u32`.

`offset` now uses checked addition and returns `None` when the sum overflows, as it already did for any off-sheet result. `offset_clamped` uses saturating addition before clamping, and the merged-cell branch goes through `offset_clamped`. Ordinary moves give the same results as before.

## How it was tested

- New `addr::tests::extreme_offsets` and `tests/extreme_selection_moves.rs` (both axes, mixed signs, a merged start cell, an ordinary move) fail on main with `attempt to add with overflow` and pass with the change.
- `cargo test -p gridcraft-core -p gridcraft-engine`: all pass.
- `cargo xtask ci`: all 7 steps pass (fmt, clippy, test, assets, layers, wasm, parity).

Possible follow-up, not in this PR: `=OFFSET(B2,1E300,0)` hits the same overflow in `crates/calc/src/eval.rs`. Happy to send that separately.

title: Accuracy: round an exact tie at the 16th significant digit toward zero
author: MacJedi42
body:
## What
Excel shows 15 significant digits. When a number is an exact tie at the 16th
(its exact decimal expansion is 15 digits, a 5, then only zeros), Excel rounds
it toward zero: `TEXT(1234567890123455,"0")` is `1234567890123450`. GridCraft
formatted with Rust's `{:.14e}`, which rounds that tie to even, so every tie with
an odd 15th digit came out one unit too high (`…460`).

## Change
`decimal_digits` (crates/numfmt/src/decimal.rs) now formats 16 digits, which is
correct unless the 16th digit is a 5, and only then checks the exact expansion
(a 30-digit screen, then the full one) and truncates a true tie. Non-ties,
including values just above or below a tie, round as before, and one format
serves almost every number.

## Evidence
All from black-box runs of Excel on synthetic workbooks; no Excel files, assets
or code are committed.
- Windows Excel 16.0.20430 `TEXT()` over a 174-row probe (ties of every
  15th-digit parity, negatives, fractional ties like 123456789012345.5, the
  neighbours just above/below a tie) and a 24-row probe of the carry case
  (`999999999999999.5` shows `999999999999999`, no carry up): every row agrees
  except those under a percent format and `General` over negatives (below).
- A number-format golden of Windows Excel `TEXT()` answers: 183,843 -> 184,900
  of 187,810 rows pass, and no row that passed before fails now.
- An independent review pass fuzzed ~10M doubles against exact decimal
  arithmetic (including 658k odd-parity ties) with no mismatches.

## Not covered here
- A `%` or trailing-comma format over such a value: GridCraft scales by 100 in
  binary before taking digits, Excel scales exactly (196 golden rows).
- `TEXT(x,"General")` of a negative value (a separate width-fit bug).

## Test plan
- `cargo xtask ci`: all 7 steps pass (fmt, clippy, test, assets, layers, wasm, parity).
- New tests: ties of every parity, negatives, fractional ties, the neighbours
  of a tie, the carry after fifteen 9s, and unchanged ordinary cases.
- Test …

title: Accuracy: Excel's snap to zero at a formula's root, in SUM, in names and in LAMBDA bodies
author: MacJedi42
body:
## What
Excel returns exactly 0 when an add or subtract of opposite-sign operands cancels
to less than 2^(e-49), `e` the binary exponent of the LEFT operand. GridCraft
returned the IEEE residue: `=1-1.0000000000000002` gave -2.2e-16 and
`=0.1+0.2-0.3` gave 5.5e-17, where Excel shows 0.

Excel does this only at specific places, not at every add or subtract:
- the bare root of a formula (`=A-B`, and the end of `=0+A-B`)
- the last addition of every `SUM`
- the body of a defined name, wherever the name is used
- the body of a LAMBDA, in every context
It never snaps inside parentheses, unary signs, `IF` branches or inner steps.

## Commits (each can be reviewed on its own)
1. **Root and SUM**: `core::arith::snap_add` / `sum_snapped`; `Evaluator::value_root`
   applies the snap at a cell formula's root; `SUM` snaps its last addition.
2. **Defined names and Evaluate Formula**: a name whose body root is an add or
   subtract snaps; Evaluate Formula snaps only the root step, so an inner step no
   longer disagrees with the cell. `value_root` charges its own depth (found in
   review: it bypasses `eval`'s counter, which opened a stack-overflow path through
   recursive names nested in cells).
3. **LAMBDA bodies**: `call_lambda_values`, the one place a LAMBDA body is evaluated
   for every route (named, inline, LET-bound, MAP, REDUCE, SCAN, MAKEARRAY, BYROW,
   BYCOL), uses the same root rule.

## Evidence
From black-box runs of Windows Excel 16.0.20430 on synthetic workbooks; no Excel
files, assets or code are committed.
- Formula golden (Excel-observed rows, 16,408): 488 failures -> 47, none of the
  remaining 47 involve the snap, and no row that passed before fails now.
- 297-row snap probe (11 magnitudes, 6-10 ulp thresholds, negative left operands,
  SUM shapes, the not-snapped forms): 174 -> 297 of 297 match bit for bit.
- 96-row name probe (8 body shapes x 12 usage positions): 72 -> 96 of 96.
- 126-row LAMBDA probe: 92 -> 126 of 126. Review probes also showed the same
…

title: Criteria: text patterns don't match blank cells
author: nihilist-narwhal
body: `COUNTIF(Z1:Z10,"*")` on empty cells gave 10 (Excel: 0), and `"<>*"` skipped blanks, which Excel counts. Text patterns now match text only. This applies to every *IF(S) function and the D-functions.

title: Conditional formatting: apply every matching rule; Cell Value rules as in Excel
author: nihilist-narwhal
body:
Only the first matching rule's format was used. Matching rules are now layered part by part, with higher priority winning, and Stop If True still ends the list.

Cell Value rules now treat blanks as 0 or empty text and never match errors, and a cell holding only spaces is no longer both blank and not blank. `home.conditionalFormat` accepts Excel's operator names (`lessThan`, …) and rejects unknown ones instead of reading them as "greater than".

title: engine: table auto-expansion on adjacent row and column edits (#258)
author: AlissonFA
body:

Implements Excel-parity automatic table expansion (`auto_expand_tables`) in `crates/engine`:

title: XLSX: write one cfvo per icon in icon-set rules (#235)
author: alexanderalber
body:
Fixes #235.

## Problem

An icon-set rule without stored thresholds was written as `<iconSet iconSet="3Arrows"></iconSet>`. `CT_IconSet` requires at least two `cfvo` children, and openpyxl discards the rule. Every rule created by `home.conditionalFormat` has no thresholds, so the built-in `sales` sample is affected too.

While looking at the reader I found a second, related bug. Files carry one `cfvo` per icon (the first is the lower bound, as in the existing round-trip test), but evaluation only used stored thresholds when there was one *fewer* than the icon count. Custom thresholds read from a file were therefore ignored and the defaults applied.

## Change

- `gridcraft-model`: new `icon_count` (moved from `engine::cf`, now re-exported there) and `default_icon_thresholds`, so writer and evaluation share the same defaults: percent `0/33/67`, `0/25/50/75`, `0/20/40/60/80`.
- Writer: always one `cfvo` per icon. It writes the stored thresholds when there is one per icon, prepends the lower bound when that is the only one missing, and falls back to the defaults otherwise.
- Evaluation: accepts both shapes (with and without the lower bound) and otherwise uses the same defaults.
- `icon_count` is clamped to 3..=5. Previously a set name like `0Foo` from a file gave `k = 0`, and `k - 1` underflowed.

**Behaviour change:** rules without thresholds were previously evaluated by *percentile*. They now use *percent* of the min..max span, which is what the written file says. My understanding is that Percent 33/67 is Excel's default for a new icon-set rule (the ECMA-376 example shows the same values). I did not verify that against a running Excel.

## Tests

- `xlsx::tests::roundtrip::icon_sets_always_write_one_cfvo_per_icon`: empty thresholds, missing lower bound and an unknown set name, plus a read-back check.
- `engine::tests::icon_set_thresholds_from_files_pick_the_icon`: default thresholds, and file-style thresholds (one per icon) deciding the icon.

title: Leave the active cell unshaded inside a selected range
author: arcanii
body:
## What was wrong

Select a range and every cell in it is shaded, the active cell included, so you can't see where typing will go. `paint_selection` means to leave it clear ("Fill all areas except the active cell"), but the line that should do it paints a fully transparent rectangle (`t.grid_bg.gamma_multiply(0.0)`), which changes nothing. A translucent fill couldn't be cleared by painting over it anyway.

## What changed

- The fill goes around the active cell. Each area of the selection is shaded as up to four rectangles (above, below and beside the cell) that never overlap. `grid::selection_fill` returns them and `paint_selection` paints them.
- A merged active cell is left clear as a whole. A lone active cell among several areas (Ctrl+click) isn't shaded, and neither is a single selected merged cell (it was shaded before).
- The joins between the rectangles fall on the lines that continue the cell's edges and don't show: with gridlines off at 100 %, 115 % and 137 % zoom, at 1x and 1.5x scale, two renders that differ only in where the active cell is differ only in those two cells.

Run locally on Windows with Rust 1.99: `cargo xtask ci`. fmt, clippy `-D warnings`, the tests (587), assets, layers and wasm pass. title: Glide the selection outline to a new selection; View ▸ Animations turns it off
author: arcanii
body:
Stacked on #265: the first two commits here are that pull request, and only the last commit is new. Please look at #265 first; I'll rebase this one once it lands.

## What it does

Excel's cell cursor doesn't jump. Press an arrow key or click a cell and the border slides to the new place; extend the selection and it grows. GridCraft's outline jumped. Now it glides.

- **What glides:** the outline of the selection's current area, with its fill and fill handle, whenever the selection changes (arrows, Enter, Tab, a click, a drag, Shift+arrows, the Name Box, any command). A new move takes over from wherever the outline is drawn, so a held arrow key reads as one continuous motion. A range grows or shrinks edge by edge.
- **What doesn't:** the same cells moving on screen (scrolling, zoom, a resized column or window) keep their outline glued to them. Another sheet or workbook, an outline that wasn't drawn the frame before, and moves that start or end off screen appear in place. An arrow key held at the edge of the window scrolls the sheet under an outline that stays where it is.
- **Only painting waits.** The selection itself, hit testing and the cell editor use the real cells at once.
- **Timing:** 0.12 s, decelerating (ease-out cubic), the same at any frame rate. This is an estimate from using Excel, not a measurement.
- **Turning it off:** View ▸ Animations, a checkbox under Display theme, since settings live in the View tab. `view.animations {on?}` and `ui.set {animations?}` do the same for agents. It is saved with the UI preferences and on by default. The label and its hint are in the five catalogs; the translations are mine and unreviewed.
- **Agents and screenshots:** the outline stays on its cells from a `ui.screenshot` request until the picture is delivered, and whenever egui's animations are off, which the headless harness does. Scripted pictures and the offscreen snapshot never catch it in flight.
- **Marching ants:** the dashes around a copied range now advance…

title: XLSX: write `@` as `_xlfn.SINGLE` in a dynamic-array formula (#64)
author: alexanderalber
body:
Refs #64. The export side of #64 is already fixed by #83; the issue is still open, and its read side is not addressed here (see below).

## Problem

The file format has no `@` operator, but a formula with an explicit implicit intersection was written with a literal `@`:

```xml
<c r="D3"><f>@A1:A3*2</f><v>10</v></c>
<c r="D2" cm="1"><f t="array" ref="D2">SUM(@A1:A3*B1:B3)</f><v>36</v></c>
```

Excel writes `@x` as `_xlfn.SINGLE(x)` in a dynamic-array formula (that is also how an `@` shows up in pre-dynamic-array Excel). As far as I know, Excel does not accept a literal `@` in `<f>`. I could not verify this, because there is no Excel on this machine.

## Change

- `fmla::expr_to_file`: `@x` becomes `_xlfn.SINGLE(x)`, next to the existing `x#` → `_xlfn.ANCHORARRAY(x)`.
- Parser: `SINGLE(x)` (with or without `_xlfn.`) reads back as `@x`, just as `ANCHORARRAY(A1)` already reads back as `A1#`.
- `array_formula::needs_array`: a formula containing `@` gets `cm="1"`, because `_xlfn.SINGLE` belongs to dynamic-array formulas.

After the change:

```xml
<c r="D3" cm="1"><f t="array" ref="D3">_xlfn.SINGLE(A1:A3)*2</f><v>10</v></c>
<c r="D2" cm="1"><f t="array" ref="D2">SUM(_xlfn.SINGLE(A1:A3)*B1:B3)</f><v>36</v></c>
```

### Changed expectations in the #83 test

`implicit_intersection_metadata_respects_function_argument_context` expected `SQRT(@A1:A3)` and `@A1:A3*2` to be written as ordinary formulas without `cm`. In legacy Excel the `@` there is redundant, so the alternative would be to drop it and write `<f>A1:A3*2</f>`. That is only lossless if the reader puts the `@` back on formulas without `cm`. Today it doesn't, so the formula would come back as `=A1:A3*2` and spill in GridCraft. Until the read side exists, these two cases now expect `cm`. Once the reader inserts `@` into legacy formulas, writing redundant `@`s as plain legacy formulas becomes possible and the two expectations can flip back.

## Not in this PR: the read side of #64

A formula without `cm` in an Excel-au…

title: Functions: ODDFPRICE, ODDFYIELD, ODDLPRICE, ODDLYIELD (#275)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #275

## What was added
The four odd-period bond functions, in `crates/functions/src/financial.rs` next to PRICE/YIELD. Financial is now 55 / 55.

- **ODDFPRICE**: the odd first period (short or long) is split into quasi-coupon periods counted back from `first_coupon`; price = redemption and regular coupons discounted over `N + Nq + DSC/NL` periods, plus the odd first coupon `100·rate/freq · Σ DCi/NLi` discounted over `Nq + DSC/NL`, minus accrued interest `100·rate/freq · Σ Ai/NLi`. With one quasi-period this is the documented odd-short formula (A, DFC, DSC, E, N).
- **ODDFYIELD**: bounded bisection on ODDFPRICE (price falls as yield rises), `#NUM!` when no bracket is found. Microsoft's page says Excel uses Newton; the root is the same.
- **ODDLPRICE / ODDLYIELD**: quasi-coupon periods counted forward from `last_interest`; `(red + C·ΣDCi/NLi) / (1 + ΣDSCi/NLi · yld/freq) − C·ΣAi/NLi` and its closed-form inverse.
- Day counts reuse the existing basis helpers (30/360 US and European, actual); NL is COUPDAYS' normal period length.
- Argument checks: dates truncated, date order (`maturity > first_coupon > settlement > issue`, `maturity > settlement > last_interest`), rate < 0, yld < 0, pr ≤ 0, redemption ≤ 0, frequency not 1/2/4, basis outside 0–4 → `#NUM!`; non-numeric → `#VALUE!`. Every quasi-period walk is capped (40,000 periods, more than the date range allows).

Source: the ODDFPRICE, ODDFYIELD, ODDLPRICE and ODDLYIELD pages on support.microsoft.com (syntax, remarks, variable definitions, worked examples). No GPL code was consulted.

## Tests
`financial::tests::odd_periods` and `odd_periods_survive_hostile_input`:
- Microsoft's worked examples, against the results printed there: ODDFPRICE 113.60 (ours 113.5977), ODDFYIELD 7.72% (ours 0.077246), ODDLPRICE 99.88 (ours 99.8783), ODDLYIELD 0.04519 (ours 0.045192).

title: UI: skip system fonts egui can't parse instead of panicking at startup (#226)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #226

## Root cause
egui's text layer (epaint 0.36) opens every face in `FontDefinitions` with `skrifa::FontRef::from_index` inside `Context::set_fonts` and panics if that fails (`fonts.rs:990`, "Error parsing \"sys-ui\" TTF/OTF font file: An offset was out of bounds"). `theme::try_load` handed any system font file that could be *read* to egui without checking that it *parses*, so one corrupt, truncated or non-sfnt file at a candidate path (`sys-ui`, `sys-hebrew`, …) crashed the app at startup.

## What changed (`crates/ui-egui/src/theme.rs`)
- `font_parses(bytes, index)`: the same call epaint makes (`skrifa::FontRef::from_index`, so the same parser and the same collection-index handling), plus "the face has a readable character map" — a truncated file opens but draws nothing, so it is refused too and the next candidate gets its turn.
- `try_load` skips a candidate that doesn't parse (with a `log::warn!`) and keeps looking, for the role fonts and the CJK/Thai/Hebrew fallback faces alike.
- `drop_unparseable_fonts` runs on the finished `FontDefinitions` before they reach egui: it removes any face that still doesn't parse and removes its key from every family. This is a last line of defence. `font_definitions_for_language` is the only place that builds the definitions passed to `set_fonts` (startup and language switch).
- `skrifa` is now a direct dependency of `gridcraft-ui-egui` (0.44, the version epaint already pulls in, so no second copy; lockfile only gains the edge).

## Tests
- `theme::tests::unparseable_font_files_are_rejected_not_fatal`: empty, garbage, truncated bytes and an out-of-range face index are refused; a bad `sys-hebrew` face injected into the definitions is dropped from `font_data` and every family; `set_fonts` + a frame with Hebrew text runs without panic.
- `theme::tests::try_load_skips_a_broken_candidate`: a broken file in front of a good one loses to the good one.

Commands run:
- `cargo test -p gridcraft-ui-egui --lib theme::` (6 passed)

title: Fill handle: Ctrl+drag swaps copying and extending a series (#264)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #264

## Root cause
The fill-handle release in `crates/ui-egui/src/grid.rs` sent `mode: "copy"` whenever Ctrl (Cmd on macOS) was held, so Ctrl+drag always copied. A plain drag of a lone number also copies (Excel does the same), so there was no way to drag a single number into a counting series.

## What changed
- `crate::fill::FillMode::Alternate` (`edit.autoFill` `mode: "alternate"`): the Ctrl+drag fill. It swaps the plain drag's choice per lane:
  - a lone number (no formula) counts up by 1 (down/right) or down by 1 (up/left);
  - anything a plain drag extends (two or more numbers, a date, a weekday/month or custom list entry, `Item 1`-style text) is copied;
  - plain text and formulas behave as before (copied; formulas still shift their relative references).
- The fill-handle drag sends `alternate` instead of `copy` when Ctrl/Cmd is held at release.
- `docs/ui-parity.md` fill-handle row, ROADMAP progress log row.

## Tests
- `tests::ctrl_drag_fill_swaps_copy_and_series` (engine): lone number down and up, two-number series, list entry, text with number, plain text, empty source.
- Commands run:
  - `cargo test -p gridcraft-engine fill`
  - `cargo fmt -p gridcraft-engine -p gridcraft-ui-egui -- --check`
  - `cargo clippy -p gridcraft-engine -p gridcraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings`

## Not done
- The Auto Fill Options button after a fill (Copy Cells / Fill Series / Fill Formatting Only …) and the right-drag fill menu.
- No visual cue (the small "+" next to the cursor) while Ctrl is held.

## Unverified assumptions (needs confirmation in Excel)
- On macOS the toggle key is Cmd here (the existing binding). Excel for Mac may use Option or Ctrl instead; not checked.

title: Functions: PERCENTOF and EUROCONVERT (#279)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #279

## What was added
- **PERCENTOF(data_subset, data_all)** (`crates/functions/src/math.rs`, Math & Trig) returns `SUM(data_subset) / SUM(data_all)`. Microsoft's page says the function is "logically equivalent" to that. Text, booleans and blanks inside ranges are skipped as SUM skips them, errors propagate, and a zero total returns `#DIV/0!`. XLSX writes it as `_xlfn.PERCENTOF` (`crates/xlsx/src/tables.rs`).
- **EUROCONVERT(number, source, target, [full_precision], [triangulation_precision])** (`crates/functions/src/financial.rs`) is in a new `Category::AddIn`, Excel's "Add-in and Automation" category.
  - Currencies: the 13 legacy currencies the function page lists (BEF, LUF, DEM, ESP, FRF, IEP, ITL, NLG, ATS, PTE, FIM, GRD, SIT) plus EUR, each with its calculation precision from that page.
  - Rates: the irrevocable rates from Council Regulation (EC) No 2866/98 as amended. GRD and SIT were added by later amendments. All 13 were checked against the ECB/EUR-Lex figures.
  - Behaviour: same source and target returns the number unchanged. Without `full_precision` the result rounds half away from zero to the target's calculation precision. `triangulation_precision` rounds the intermediate euro value to that many significant digits when the source is a member currency. A value below 3 returns `#VALUE!`, and so does an unknown code.

Sources: the PERCENTOF and EUROCONVERT pages on support.microsoft.com, and Council Regulation (EC) No 2866/98 (EUR-Lex / ECB press release of 31 Dec 1998) for the rates.

title: UI: Name Box Enter goes to the typed cell, not the one below (#247)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #247

## Root cause
The Name Box is a single-line `TextEdit` in the formula bar. Pressing Enter makes it lose focus, and the formula bar then runs `edit.goTo` (or `formulas.defineName`). The Enter key event stayed in the frame's input, though. The grid is drawn after the formula bar in the same frame, and it takes the focus back once nothing else holds it, so it read that same Enter as a grid Enter and called `move_after_enter`. The active cell landed one row below the target: typing `A1` + Enter selected A2.

## What changed
- `crates/ui-egui/src/formula_bar.rs`: when the Name Box commits on Enter, it removes the Enter key events from the frame's input, so later widgets in the frame never see them. Defining a name from the Name Box had the same bug (the selection moved down after the name was created), and this fixes it too.

## Tests
- `tests/interaction.rs::name_box_enter_goes_to_the_typed_cell_not_the_one_below`: start at C5, focus the Name Box, type `A1`, press Enter, and the active cell is A1. A second Enter, now in the grid, still moves down to A2. Without the fix the test fails (`left: row 1, right: row 0`).

Commands run:
- `cargo test -p gridcraft-ui-egui --test interaction name_box` (passes with the fix, fails without it)
- `cargo clippy -p gridcraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo fmt -p gridcraft-ui-egui -- --check`

title: Clipboard: pasted currency cells keep the number from the clipboard HTML (#257)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #257

## Root cause
Paste only used the clipboard's plain text, where each cell is what it *shows*: `Rp10,000.00`. Typed-input parsing is en-US and recognises only `$` as a currency symbol, so the field became text. Typing `Rp10,000.00` gives text for the same reason. Changing that parser would make typing differ from Excel's en-US behaviour, so this PR leaves it alone.

Spreadsheets also put an HTML table on the clipboard, and that table records the underlying number of each cell as an attribute: `x:num="10000"` (Excel's HTML) and `sdval="10000"` (LibreOffice Calc's HTML). GridCraft never read that flavour.

## What changed
- **Engine** (`crates/engine/src/clip_html.rs`, new): a small, panic-free reader for the first `<table>` in clipboard HTML. It reads only rows, cells, `colspan`, the cell text (with entities decoded) and the `x:num` / `sdval` attributes. Input is capped at 16 MB, `colspan` is capped at the sheet's column count, a `>` inside quoted attributes doesn't end a tag, and comments, `<style>` and `<script>` are skipped.
- **`edit.paste`** takes a new optional `html` param. A tab-separated field that would paste as **text** becomes the number recorded at the same row and column of the HTML table, but only if that HTML cell shows the same text (after whitespace and nbsp are normalised). HTML from another copy, or laid out differently, therefore changes nothing. Formulas, numbers that already parsed and cells formatted as Text (`@`) are left as they are.
- **Format:** when the cell is General, it gets a format inferred from the shown text (`Rp10,000.00` → `"Rp"#,##0.00`). The format is applied only if rendering the number with it gives back exactly the shown text. Otherwise the cell keeps the number with no format; that happens, for example, with comma-decimal or space-grouped text such as `10.000,00 €`.
- **UI:** a new `Services::paste_html` host hook, and `SheetApp::paste_external` used by the grid's paste event and the ribbon Paste button. The desk…

title: Clipboard: Insert Copied Cells and Insert Cut Cells (#21)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #21

## Root cause
There was no command for Excel's Insert Copied Cells / Insert Cut Cells, so the context menus only offered Insert (blank lines) and Paste. The secondary problem in the issue (pasting from the wrong row after inserting a blank row) was already fixed by #34: inserting or deleting cells ends copy mode.

## What changed
- **`home.insertCopiedCells`** `{at?, shift?: down|right}` (engine, `crates/engine/src/cmd/sheet.rs`). It makes room at `at` (default: the active cell), then pastes the clipboard there (everything, formulas shifted). The whole thing is **one undo step**, and a failure part-way restores the workbook.
  - Copied **whole rows / columns**: inserts that many whole rows above / columns left of `at`, then pastes into them.
  - A copied **block**: inserts cells of the block's size at `at` and shifts the cells there down (default) or right.
  - A **cut** of whole rows/columns (same workbook) moves them (**Insert Cut Cells**): insert at the destination, move (references to the moved cells follow), delete the vacated lines. Inserting the lines inside themselves is refused.
  - A cut **block** is refused with a clear message (see Not done). A cut from another workbook is treated as a copy, as paste already does.
  - Like the other insert commands, it ends copy mode afterwards.
- `Clipboard` keeps the range as copied (`selected`) in addition to the range trimmed to the used area, so the command can tell whole rows/columns from a block.
- **UI**: the cell context menu and the row/column header menus show *Insert Copied Cells* (whole lines, runs directly), *Insert Copied Cells…* (block → new *Insert Paste* dialog: shift right / shift down) or *Insert Cut Cells*, only while the clipboard holds a copy or cut of this app. The new labels are in all interface catalogs (ja, zh, ko, ru, pt).

title: Functions: GETPIVOTDATA (#284)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #284

## What changed
- **Model** (`crates/model/src/features.rs`): `PivotTable::data_cells`, a list of `PivotDataCell` entries, each holding the value-field caption and source column, the row/column items that locate it (field, label, value) and the value shown. It is `#[serde(skip)]`, so files never carry it.
- **Engine** (`crates/engine/src/pivot.rs`):
  - `compute` records every value cell it lays out: item cells, subtotals with fewer items, and grand totals with none.
  - `refresh` stores them on the PivotTable, and `clear_output` drops them.
  - The new `index_all` rebuilds them for every PivotTable when a workbook is opened (`DocState::new`), so GETPIVOTDATA works in files read from XLSX/JSON.
  - The index is capped at 1,000,000 value cells per report.
- **Calc** (`crates/calc/src/pivotdata.rs`): `GETPIVOTDATA(data_field, pivot_table, [field, item]...)` is an evaluator special form, because L1 `functions` can't see the workbook.
  - It finds the PivotTable whose last output intersects `pivot_table` (any cell of the report).
  - It then returns the value cell whose value field matches (caption "Sum of Sales" or source name "Sales") and whose items are exactly the given pairs.
  - Field and item names ignore case. A number matches an item by value (dates as serials) or by label.
  - Its result is recalculated on every pass, because a refresh changes the report without touching the formula's references.
- **Errors**, per Microsoft's GETPIVOTDATA page:
  - `#REF!` for a reference outside a PivotTable, an unknown value field, field or item, an unpaired field, the same field twice, or more than 126 pairs.
  - `#REF!` also for a report filter field named while the report doesn't show exactly that item. Naming a filter field is allowed when the filter shows just that item.
  - Error arguments propagate.

title: Functions: BAHTTEXT (#291)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #291

## What was added
`BAHTTEXT(number)` in `crates/functions/src/text.rs`, written from scratch (nothing taken from the closed #37).

- **Rounding:** the number rounds half away from zero to satang (2 decimals). Whole baht end in **ถ้วน**; satang are read as a number followed by **สตางค์**; an amount under one baht is read in satang only; zero is ศูนย์บาทถ้วน.
- **Number words:** digits ศูนย์–เก้า with the places สิบ, ร้อย, พัน, หมื่น, แสน.
  - A one in the tens place is **สิบ**; a two is **ยี่สิบ**.
  - A final one after higher digits in its six-digit group is **เอ็ด**: 11 สิบเอ็ด, 21 ยี่สิบเอ็ด, 101 หนึ่งร้อยเอ็ด.
  - Every six-digit group except the last is followed by **ล้าน**, so 10^12 is หนึ่งล้านล้าน.
- **Negatives:** a negative amount starts with **ลบ**.
- **Errors:** non-numeric text gives `#VALUE!`. A value whose rounding overflows gives `#NUM!`.

Source: Microsoft's BAHTTEXT page gives the syntax and one example (1234 → หนึ่งพันสองร้อยสามสิบสี่บาทถ้วน). Everything else comes from the standard Thai way of reading numbers and amounts.

title: Name Manager: New… and Edit… open the name dialog and return to the manager (#238)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #238

## Root cause
`dialogs::show` takes the open dialog out of `app.dialog`, draws it, and puts it back while it stays open. Clicking **New…** in the Name Manager called `open_dialog("defineName")`, which set `app.dialog` to the New Name dialog. A few lines later the Name Manager put itself back over it (`if open { app.dialog = Some(d) }`), so New… did nothing. Go To › Special… was hit by the same overwrite.

## What changed
- **Dialogs opened from dialogs** (`crates/ui-egui/src/dialogs.rs`): when a dialog's body opens another dialog, the new dialog takes over. The opener waits behind it (`Dialog::back`) and comes back when the new dialog closes. In Excel, OK or Cancel in New Name returns to the Name Manager. Go To is the one exception: it hands over to Go To Special for good, as in Excel.
- **Name Manager**: Excel's **New… / Edit… / Delete** buttons sit above a selectable list (Name, Value, Refers To, Scope), with a Close button. The list scrolls and shows "No names defined" when empty. Edit… opens the name dialog titled **Edit Name** and pre-filled with Name / Scope / Comment / Refers to.
- **`formulas.defineName`** takes optional `oldName` / `oldScope` to edit an existing name in place:
  - The old entry is replaced instead of a second name being added.
  - Renaming onto another existing name in the target scope is refused with "The name entered already exists. Enter a unique name."
  - A missing `oldName` is an error.
  - A renamed name is also renamed in cell formulas and in other names' definitions, on the sheets where the old name resolved to it. Without that, the formulas would turn into `#NAME?`.
- The `defineName` dialog now uses the params it is opened with: name, scope, comment, refersTo, oldName, oldScope.

title: Functions: TRIMRANGE (#296)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #296 (the function; the trim-reference operators are listed under "Not done")

## What was added
- `TRIMRANGE(range, [trim_rows], [trim_cols])` is an evaluator special form (`crates/calc/src/trimrange.rs`), because it returns a reference.
  - It drops blank outer rows and columns per Microsoft's codes: 0 none, 1 leading, 2 trailing, 3 both (the default for each).
  - A single-area reference stays a reference, so `ROW`, `ROWS`, `SUM`, spilling and dependency tracking work as for any range. Only the used part of large references such as `C:C` is read.
  - An array argument is trimmed into a smaller array. A scalar is returned unchanged.
- **Errors:** a trim code outside 0–3 gives `#VALUE!`, a multi-area reference gives `#VALUE!`, and nothing but blanks gives `#CALC!`.
- **Listing:** the function list (Insert Function / autocomplete) shows it under Lookup & Reference. XLSX writes it as `_xlfn.TRIMRANGE`, a Microsoft 365 function, added to the list in `crates/xlsx/src/tables.rs`.

Source: Microsoft's TRIMRANGE function page (syntax, the 0–3 codes and defaults, the trim-reference table).

## Tests
`calc::tests::trimrange`:
- each trim mode on a block with blank margins, whole-column `C:C`, the reference result (`MIN(ROW(...))`) and an array argument;
- the spilled result, and recalculation after an edit widens the block;
- bad code → `#VALUE!`, all blank → `#CALC!`, a union → `#VALUE!`.

`tables::tests::functions` checks `_xlfn.TRIMRANGE`.

title: XLSX: write threaded comments and persons parts, read note visibility (#300)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #300

## Root cause
The XLSX reader already understood threaded comments (`threadedComment` and `person` relationships), but the writer only produced the legacy `comments` part and its VML. After a save and reopen, every threaded comment came back as a plain note: replies were flattened into the text and the resolved state was lost. Separately, the reader never looked at the VML, so a note shown with Show/Hide Note came back hidden.

title: PivotTables: calculated fields (pivot.calculatedField) (#304)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #304

## What changed
- **Model:** `PivotTable::calculated_fields` holds `PivotCalcField { name, formula }`. A value field uses one by putting its name in `source_col`.
- **Engine evaluation** (`crates/engine/src/pivot_calc.rs` and `pivot.rs`). A calculated field's formula is evaluated on the **sums** of the fields it names, for each report cell, including subtotals and grand totals. It is not evaluated record by record. Microsoft documents this for Excel: "`=Sales * 1.2` multiplies the sum of the sales for each type and region by 1.2".
  - The grand total is the formula applied to the totals; for `=Sales/Units` that is 835/72, not the sum of the row ratios.
  - Implementation: the engine also accumulates sums of the referenced source columns, then evaluates the formula through the calc evaluator (a `LET` that binds each field to its sum). So worksheet functions work (`=IF(Units>0,Sales/Units,0)`, `=ROUND(...)`), and errors such as `#DIV/0!` show in the cells.
  - The value field's summary function is ignored for calculated fields: the formula always works on sums.
- **Formula syntax:** fields are written bare (`Sales`) or in single quotes (`'Unit Price'`), case-insensitive; a field named like a cell (`Q1`) is still a field. Cell references, table references and unknown names are refused with a message.
- **Nested fields:** calculated fields may use other calculated fields. Results are memoised per cell, the depth is bounded at 64, and a cycle is refused by the command (`#REF!` if one comes from a file). A PivotTable has at most 256 calculated fields, and a formula at most 8,192 characters.
- **Command** `pivot.calculatedField {pivot?, name, formula?, delete?, values?}`:
  - adds a field (and puts it in Values as "Sum of X" unless `values: false`), changes the formula of an existing one, or deletes it (also from Values);
  - refuses names of source fields, bad formulas and cycles, as one undo step;
  - without `name` (a menu-style call) it opens an "Insert Cal…

title: Review: Allow Edit Ranges with Excel-compatible password hashes (#307)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #307

Adds Review › Protect › Allow Edit Ranges: titled ranges that stay editable when the sheet is protected, optionally behind their own password. Catalog goes from 258 to 259 / 290.

## What changed
- **Model** (`gridcraft-model`):
  - `Sheet.edit_ranges: Vec<EditRange>`, where each range has a title, references, an optional `PasswordHash` and the `securityDescriptor` kept as read. It's `#[serde(default)]` and skipped when empty, so workbook JSON is unchanged.
  - New `password` module:
    - `PasswordHash::Legacy(u16)`: the ECMA-376 legacy 16-bit hash, checked against the published example (`"password"` → `83AF`).
    - `PasswordHash::Iterated { algorithm, hash, salt, spin_count }`: H0 = H(salt + UTF-16LE password), then Hn = H(Hn-1 + n as 32-bit LE), `spin_count` times.
  - `verify()` supports SHA-512, SHA-384 and SHA-256. It refuses with a clear error any other algorithm (SHA-1, MD5, …), a damaged hash or salt, an unreadable legacy hex value, or a spin count above 10,000,000 (so a hostile file can't make verification hang). Nothing is ever accepted without a real check.
  - New passwords get SHA-512 with spin count 100000 and a 16-byte salt derived from SHA-512 over the sheet, title, a counter, the document uid and the clock.
  - New dependency: `sha2` 0.11 (RustCrypto, MIT/Apache-2.0, `default-features = false`). `cargo check -p gridcraft-model --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` passes.
- **XLSX:**
  - Writes `<protectedRanges>` right after `sheetProtection`: `password` for legacy hashes, or `algorithmName`/`hashValue`/`saltValue`/`spinCount`, plus `securityDescriptor`.
  - Reads it back. Invalid references are dropped. A password that can't be read becomes a hash that never matches, so the range stays locked instead of opening.

author: vangel76

Fixes #311

## What changed
A PivotChart here is a regular chart (the existing chart model and renderer) with a link to its PivotTable. The engine rebuilds its series from the report every time the PivotTable is written. This is the "chart from the pivot's report that re-binds on refresh" approach; there is no separate PivotChart object model.

title: Windows: never load Vulkan by default; OpenGL fallback when DirectX 12 can't start (#120)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #120

## Root cause

The 0.4.0 build let wgpu create eframe's default instance (Vulkan + DirectX 12 + GL on Windows). Enumerating Vulkan adapters crashes inside Intel's Vulkan driver (`igvk64.dll`, access violation 0xc0000005) on some UHD Graphics drivers. The fault is in the driver, before any Rust error handling runs, so the process just disappears. The reporter's `WGPU_BACKEND=dx12` workaround avoids it because Vulkan is never loaded.

#22 (in 0.5.0, not in 0.4.0) already made the Windows instance DirectX 12 only, which removes the Vulkan path. That leaves two gaps this PR closes, so "DirectX 12 only" can't leave a PC with no window at all:

1. A PC whose GPU has no DirectX 12 driver gets only WARP (Microsoft's software renderer) from DirectX 12: the app opens but every frame is drawn on the CPU. Same as storytold/wordcraft#316.
2. If DirectX 12 fails to start (no adapter, device or surface), `eframe::run_native` returns an error and the app quits.

## What changed

`apps/gridcraft/src/graphics.rs` (Windows only at runtime; pure functions tested on every platform):

- **Probe before eframe starts** (no `WGPU_BACKEND` set): a short-lived DirectX 12-only wgpu instance lists the adapters and checks each against the limits eframe's device descriptor will request. `choose_backends(override, adapters)` then picks: a usable hardware GPU → DirectX 12 only (unchanged for everyone with a working driver, so AMD machines never get GL and the `atio6axx.dll` crash from #22 stays away); WARP only → OpenGL + DirectX 12 (wgpu ranks a GPU above a software adapter, WARP stays as a last resort for VMs/RDP); nothing usable → OpenGL. Same logic as storytold/wordcraft#325.
- **Retry once on a start failure:** `main.rs` keeps the `SheetApp` in a `Cell` until the app creator takes it. If `run_native` returns `eframe::Error::Wgpu` while the app was never created, it starts once more with `fallback_backends(override, first)` = the other of DirectX 12 / OpenGL. eframe keeps its winit …

title: macOS: end the process in on_exit so quitting doesn't crash (#117)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #117

## Root cause

The crash report in #117 is an uncaught Objective-C exception on the main thread, after the window is gone: `-[_NSTouchBarFinderObservation invalidate]` → `removeObserver:forKeyPath:` inside AppKit's display cycle (`NSDisplayCycleFlush`). AccessKit's macOS adapter (eframe's `accesskit` feature, enabled in `apps/gridcraft`) subclasses the window's content view and restores the original class when the window is torn down. AppKit's Touch Bar support registered a KVO observation on that view under the subclass, so removing it afterwards throws "not registered" and AppKit aborts (EXC_BREAKPOINT). eframe runs with `run_and_return`, so it drops the window while AppKit's run loop is still running, and the next display cycle hits it.

The same crash was found and fixed in storytold/vectorcraft#670 and storytold/photocraft#1624 (also zed-industries/zed#64819). Since #164, the Dock's Quit arrives as a `kAEQuitApplication` event that GridCraft turns into `ViewportCommand::Close`, i.e. the same window-teardown path.

## What changed

`apps/gridcraft/src/main.rs`: on macOS, `App::on_exit` calls `std::process::exit(0)` right after `save_prefs`, before eframe tears the window down. eframe calls `on_exit` on every way of quitting (Quit/⌘Q, Dock Quit, the red close button, `app.quit` on the control channel). Nothing after it is needed on a normal quit: preferences are saved, and the log file writer is unbuffered. eframe does the same itself (`save_and_destroy` + `process::exit(0)`) when `run_and_return` is off. `on_exit` exists only once the app was created, so a failed start still returns its error from `main`. Windows and Linux are unchanged.

## Tests

No unit test: the change exits the process and only acts on macOS. Commands run (Linux, where it compiles to nothing):
- `cargo clippy -p gridcraft --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo fmt -p gridcraft -- --check`

## Not done

- No macOS type-check from here (the `aarch64-apple-darwin` target isn't inst…

title: Functions: FORECAST.ETS, .CONFINT, .SEASONALITY and .STAT (#314)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #314

## What
Adds Excel's four exponential-smoothing forecast functions (Statistical: 111 / 111):

- `FORECAST.ETS(target_date, values, timeline, [seasonality], [data_completion], [aggregation])`
- `FORECAST.ETS.CONFINT(target_date, values, timeline, [confidence_level], [seasonality], [data_completion], [aggregation])`
- `FORECAST.ETS.SEASONALITY(values, timeline, [data_completion], [aggregation])`
- `FORECAST.ETS.STAT(values, timeline, statistic_type, [seasonality], [data_completion], [aggregation])`

New module `crates/functions/src/ets.rs`.

**Arguments, following Microsoft's function docs:** seasonality 1 (default) = detect, 0 = none, 2–8,760 = season length, anything else `#NUM!`. data_completion 1 (default) interpolates missing points, 0 fills zeros. Up to 30% of points may be missing, more gives `#NUM!`. Duplicate time stamps are aggregated (0/1 AVERAGE, 2 COUNT, 3 COUNTA, 4 MAX, 5 MEDIAN, 6 MIN, 7 SUM). The timeline is sorted implicitly. A timeline without a constant step gives `#NUM!`, values and timeline of different sizes give `#N/A`, and a target before the end of the timeline gives `#NUM!`. confidence_level must be strictly between 0 and 1, and statistic_type must be 1–8 (alpha, beta, gamma, MASE, SMAPE, MAE, RMSE, step size).

**Model:** ETS(A,A,A), additive error, trend and seasonality, after Hyndman, Koehler, Ord & Snyder, *Forecasting with Exponential Smoothing: The State Space Approach* (2008):
- Initial states use the book's heuristic (§2.6.1). Seasonal indices come from a classical decomposition (centred moving average) of the first seasons, and level/trend from a straight line through the first ten seasonally adjusted values.
- α, β, γ ∈ [0, 1] minimise the in-sample SSE of the one-step errors. The optimiser is a 5-point grid followed by a Nelder–Mead simplex clamped to the box, with at most 400 iterations.
- CONFINT is `z_{(1+c)/2} · σ · sqrt(1 + Σ_{j<h} (α + αβ·j + γ·[m | j])²)` (the book's Table 6.1, class 1). σ² = SSE / n. The sum is …

author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #170

## Root cause
On macOS the window has no system title bar (`with_fullsize_content_view`, `with_titlebar_shown(false)` in `apps/gridcraft/src/main.rs`). AppKit still draws the traffic lights, centred in its standard 28 pt title-bar band at the top of the window. body:
Fixes #322

**Stacked on #317** (FORECAST.ETS family). This branch contains #317's commit; review only the second commit (`Data: Forecast Sheet …`). Once #317 is merged I'll rebase this onto main.

## What
`data.forecastSheet` (Data › Forecast › Forecast Sheet) builds a forecast sheet the way Microsoft's "Create a forecast in Excel" page describes it:

- It inserts a new sheet before the active one and activates it. One undo step removes it again.
- The sheet holds a copy of the timeline and the values, sorted by time. A text first cell is the header ("Timeline"/"Values" otherwise). Next to them are three columns:
  - `Forecast(<values>)`: `=FORECAST.ETS(A18,$B$2:$B$17,$A$2:$A$17,<seasonality>,<fill>[,<aggregation>])`
  - `Lower/Upper Confidence Bound(<values>)`: `=C18∓FORECAST.ETS.CONFINT(…,<confidence>,…)`

- With `statistics: true` it adds a FORECAST.ETS.STAT table (Alpha, Beta, Gamma, MASE, SMAPE, MAE, RMSE).
- An Excel table covers the data, and a line chart (or a column chart with the bounds as lines) shows values, forecast and bounds.
- The future time stamps continue the timeline's step, using calendar months for monthly dates. To do this, `gridcraft-functions` now exports a small `Timeline` (step detection shared with FORECAST.ETS, including its 30%-missing rule).

**Params:**
- `timeline`/`values`: default is the first two columns of `range`, the selection or the current region.
- `end`: a number or date text. Alternatively `periods`: default is a third of the history, at least 1, at most 10,000.
- `confidenceInterval`, `confidence` (0.95 or 95), `seasonality` ("auto" / 0 / 2–8,760), `fillMissing` (interpolate/zeros), `aggregate` (average…sum), `statistics`, `chart` (line/column).

title: Data: Solver with Simplex LP, integer branch and bound and a nonlinear method (#326)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #326

## What
- New command `data.solver` (Data › Analysis › Solver) in `crates/engine/src/cmd/solver.rs`: objective cell (`goal`: max / min / value with `value`), variable cells (≤ 200 constants on the objective's sheet), constraints as strings (`"B5 <= 10"`, `"B2:B4 >= C2:C4"`, `"B2 int"`, `"B3 bin"`) or `{lhs, op, rhs}`, `nonNegative` (default on: variables without a lower bound get 0), `method` (`grg` default, `simplex`), `keep` (default true; false leaves the cells as they were), `saveModel`, `maxEvaluations`, `integerOptimality`. Returns `{status, message, objective, values, evaluations, changed}`. Without an objective it returns the saved model and the menu opens the dialog.
- Every evaluation sets the variable cells on a copy of the workbook and recalculates their dependents (the existing what-if `Trial`), so any formula model works; the document only changes when the solution is kept (one undo step).
- **Simplex LP**: linearises the model from n + 1 evaluations, checks linearity at one more point (`notLinear` otherwise), then solves with a dense two-phase simplex (Dantzig's rule, Bland's rule when stalled). Constant bounds on variable cells become box bounds. Integer/binary constraints: depth-first branch and bound (≤ 10,000 nodes).
- **"GRG Nonlinear"**: GridCraft's method is *not* GRG. It is an augmented Lagrangian (PHR) whose inner problems are solved by projected gradient descent with Barzilai–Borwein steps and an Armijo line search on central-difference gradients; bounds are kept by projection. It finds a local optimum of a smooth model from the current values. Integer constraints use a small branch and bound (≤ 200 nodes) on top.
- Statuses: optimal, converged, iterationLimit, infeasible, unbounded, notLinear. Infeasible/unbounded/not-linear results leave the cells unchanged.
- The model is saved as hidden sheet-scoped names (`solver_opt`, `solver_typ`, `solver_val`, `solver_adj`, `solver_lhsN`/`solver_relN`/`solver_rhsN`, `solver_num`, `solver_…

title: ci: refactor workflows to use storytold/craft-common-actions
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
### Summary
Refactors repetitive CI/CD workflows across GridCraft to call centralized reusable workflows and composite actions hosted in the organization repository [`storytold/craft-common-actions`](https://github.com/storytold/craft-common-actions).

### Design Decisions
- **Hosted in Organization Repository**: Workflows live under `storytold/craft-common-actions` (no personal fork/repository).
- **Intentionally Tracks `@main` (Not SHA Pinned)**: Callers deliberately track `@main` with an inline explanation comment so that org-wide CI improvements, security fixes, and build optimizations propagate across all 13+ craftapps automatically without requiring individual PR churn in every repository.
- **Explicit Secrets**: Only the exact required signing secrets are passed explicitly (`secrets: inherit` is avoided).
- **Node 24 Runtimes**: All composite and third-party actions inside `storytold/craft-common-actions` are updated to Node 24 (and pinned internally to immutable commit SHAs), eliminating Node 20 deprecation warnings.
- **Strict Verification**: Build utilities like `nfpm`, `actionlint`, and `trunk` are verified against SHA256 checksums.
- Preserves 100% of existing packaging, release matrix, and linting semantics for GridCraft.

## What it does

Excel's File button doesn't open a menu. It opens a view that fills the window, with a column of pages and actions on the left. GridCraft's File button opened a five-item dropdown. Now it opens a page like Excel's.

A browser has no system fonts to fall back on, so CJK text shows as boxes in the web build. title: Issue #341: resizing Ctrl-selected rows or columns resizes all of them
author: LloydNicholson
body:
Fixes #341.

## Problem
With columns B, D and F Ctrl-selected, dragging F's header boundary changed only F; the same with rows. Selecting a contiguous block or the whole sheet worked.

## Cause
`grid.rs`'s `ResizeCol` / `ResizeRow` drag handlers checked that the dragged line was inside a selected whole-column (whole-row) area, then resized only `sel.current()`, the last-selected area.

## Fix
- **UI** (`crates/ui-egui/src/grid.rs`): the drag now passes every whole-column (whole-row) area of the selection, e.g. `B:B,D:D,F:F`. Dragging a line that isn't selected still resizes only that line. Partial-cell areas in the selection (e.g. `A:A,C3`) don't widen their columns, so only fully selected lines change, as in Excel.
- **Engine** (`crates/engine/src/cmd/format.rs`): `home.columnWidth {cols}` and `home.rowHeight {rows}` accept a comma-separated list of areas (`"B:B,D:F"`), like `range` already does elsewhere. The whole drag stays one command per frame and one undo step. A bad entry in the list returns an error and changes nothing. Params docs updated.

## Testing
- New UI test `dragging_a_boundary_inside_a_multi_area_selection_resizes_every_selected_line` (`crates/ui-egui/tests/header_autofit.rs`) drives real egui pointer events. It covers dragging the last or an earlier area, a multi-line area, dragging an unselected line, and a full-line plus cell selection, for both columns and rows. It also checks for a single undo step and that undo restores every line. It fails on `main` and passes with the fix.
- New engine test `row_height_and_column_width_take_a_list_of_areas`.
- Real app, driven over the `--control` channel: `selection.set "B:B,D:D,F:F"`, then `ui.drag` on F's right boundary. The installed 0.5.0 app widened only F. title: Get rid of double range copy for aggregation operations over ranges
author: Fly-Style
body:
## Summary
Aggregations such as `SUM`, `COUNT` and `AVERAGE` now add up a range cell by cell instead of first copying the whole range into an array. This removes the 16M-cell limit for them and saves about 24 to 39 bytes of peak memory per range cell. The benchmark behind the numbers below is kept in this description, not in the changeset.

## Problem
On a dense 5000 x 5000 sheet (25M cells), `=SUM(A1:GJH5000)` returned `#NUM!`, while the status bar showed Sum, Count and Average for the same selection.

A formula's range is copied into an in-memory array before the function sees it. That copy is refused above `MAX_CELLS` (16M cells, `crates/calc/src/eval.rs:15`). `SUM` then copies the numbers a second time in `numbers()`. The status bar skips both copies because it reads the stored cells in place.

The cap bites only when the sheet's used range itself is above 16M cells: `area_value` first trims large ranges to the used range, so sparse sheets were not affected.

## What changed
**Evaluator, `crates/calc/src/eval.rs`**
- `Host` gets a default method `visit_range()` that returns `false`, so other hosts behave as before.
- `builtin` hands `SUM`, `COUNT` and `AVERAGE` to the new `Evaluator::aggregate`.
- A small accumulator does the work: `Agg` names the function and `Acc` carries a sum and a count. Adding another aggregate means a new `Agg` variant and, if needed, another field in `Acc`.
- A multi-cell block is folded through `visit_range`. Single cells, blocks the host declines, and non-reference arguments are added by calling the real `SUM` and `COUNT` on them (`AVERAGE` of an argument is its `SUM` over its `COUNT`), so coercion and error rules stay in one place.
- Inside a range, `SUM` and `AVERAGE` stop at the first error. `COUNT` skips errors, as the real functions do.
- **Evaluation order.** Arguments are evaluated and read one at a time, in order, exactly like the array path, and the arguments after an error are still evaluated. This matters for volatile formul…

title: Issue #348: copying multiple selections works when the areas line up, and explains when it can't
author: LloydNicholson
body:
Fixes #348.

## Problem
With several ranges selected, Ctrl+C did nothing and showed no message, so Ctrl+V had nothing to paste.

## Cause
- `edit.copy` / `edit.cut` (`crates/engine/src/cmd/edit.rs`) returned "This action won't work on multiple selections." for any selection with more than one area.
- `SheetApp::copy_to_clipboard` (`crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs`), which Ctrl+C, the ribbon and the context menus use, dropped the error with `let Ok(..) else { return }`.

## Fix
This follows Excel's rule. A multi-area copy works when every area covers the same rows or every area covers the same columns. Excel then slides the areas together into one rectangle.
- **Engine:** when the areas line up and don't overlap, `edit.copy` slides them together in the clipboard's workbook snapshot. Side-by-side areas go left to right and stacked areas go top to bottom, whatever order they were selected in, and the block sits at the first area's place.
  - Paste, Paste Special and tiling then work unchanged.
  - Formulas travel as their values, as in Excel. Styles, comments, cell pictures, merges inside an area, and column widths (side by side) or row heights and hidden rows (stacked) come along.
  - Whole rows and columns are trimmed to the used range, like a single-area copy.
- **Still refused**, with "This action won't work on multiple selections.":
  - areas that don't line up, or that overlap;
  - Cut of several areas (Excel refuses this too);
  - Paste Link of a multi-area copy (`edit.pasteSpecial {link: true}`), since the links would point at the packed block.

  A refused copy leaves the earlier clipboard as it was.
- `Clipboard` has a new `areas` field holding the areas as selected. The marching ants go around each copied area instead of the packed block.
- **UI:** `copy_to_clipboard` shows the command's error the same way `run_or_alert` does (shared through a small `alert` helper). Copy and Cut now show Excel's message instead of doing nothing.

title: Journal: sheet protection passwords aren't recorded in plain text
author: LloydNicholson
body:
Related: #347, #351.

## Problem
`review.protectSheet` and `review.unprotectSheet` were journaled with their params as given, `password` included. So the sheet password showed in plain text in:
- the Action Journal dialog;
- `engine.journal` (control channel and headless MCP);
- **the saved workbook**, when Protect Sheet was run during Automate › Record Actions. A recorded script is built from the journal and stored in the hidden defined name `_sc_scripts`, which is written to the XLSX. The file then holds the protected sheet's password in plain text next to it.

#351 masks the password in the dialogs but leaves the journal alone. Other places checked: AutoSave only writes the workbook (so it's covered by the script fix above), nothing logs command params, and undo history keeps only command labels. On `main`, the only commands that take a secret are these two.

## Fix
`Session::execute` journals `cmd::journal_params(&params)`: the params without secret ones. A param is secret when it's named `password` or its name ends in `Password` (e.g. a future `newPassword`). The commands still run with the full params. The check goes by param name, not a per-command list, so a new command with a password param is covered without extra steps. `CommandSpec` is unchanged.

### Replay trade-off
#308 avoids the problem for `review.allowEditRanges` by not journaling the command at all (`journal: false`). For Protect/Unprotect Sheet that would drop the step from the journal and from recorded scripts, so a replay would leave the sheet unprotected and later steps would run against a different state.

Here the step stays in the journal, without its password:
- A replayed Protect Sheet protects the sheet with the same options (format cells, insert rows, …) but no password.
- The matching Unprotect Sheet, also recorded without its password, still succeeds on that sheet. So replaying a journal or running a recorded script gives the same sequence of protection states.
- What's lost: the rep…

title: Edit date cells as dates, not serial numbers (#362)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #362.

Editing a cell that holds a date (F2, double-click, the formula bar) showed the raw serial number (`46085`) instead of the date. `Cell::input_text` has no access to the workbook, so it can't see the cell's number format.

What changed:

- New `display::edit_text(wb, sheet, cell)` in the engine. For a constant number in a date or time format it returns the text the grid shows, e.g. `3/4/2026` or `2026-03-04`, so the date is edited in the same form and with the same separators.
- If that text would not read back as the same value (e.g. `dddd, mmmm d`, or `h AM/PM` that drops the minutes), it uses an ISO form that does read back: `yyyy-mm-dd`, `yyyy-mm-dd hh:mm:ss` for a date with a time, or `hh:mm:ss` for a time alone. If even that doesn't read back, it keeps the serial, so committing an unchanged edit never alters the value.
- Formulas, text, and numbers in non-date formats are unchanged.
- It is used everywhere the editor gets its starting text: the cell editor (`begin_edit`), the formula bar, and Ctrl+' (copy the cell above into the editor), which had the same problem.

Test: `editing_a_date_cell_shows_a_date_not_the_serial` covers a date in its default format, a format that can't be typed back (falls back to ISO), a time alone in `h AM/PM` (falls back to `09:36:00`), and a plain number (unchanged).

title: Ctrl+click on an already selected header or cell deselects it (#359)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #359.

Ctrl+click on a column or row header always appended the clicked area to the selection, even when it was already selected. Clicking the same header again stacked a duplicate area, so the selection overlay got darker with every click and the column never deselected.

Ctrl+click on a single cell had the same bug (it also pushed a duplicate on every click), so it now uses the same path.

Changes in `crates/ui-egui/src/grid.rs`:
- New `toggled_ranges` helper: with Ctrl, an area that is already selected is removed, and an area that is not is added once. The only remaining area is never removed, so the selection never ends up empty.
- `select_ranges` (column and row header clicks) uses it. When the clicked area is removed, the active cell is not placed in it; `selection.set` puts it at the start of the last remaining area.
- Ctrl+click on a cell now goes through `select_ranges` instead of pushing the cell itself.
- Plain clicks, Shift+clicks and header drags behave as before.

Test: `ctrl_click_on_a_selected_header_deselects_it` covers removing a selected column, adding a new one, keeping the only remaining area, removing a selected cell from a mixed selection, and a plain click replacing the selection.

title: Functions: lookups keep an empty target cell blank (#374)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #374

## Root cause
`crates/functions/src/lookup.rs` passed every looked-up value through `cell_result`, which turned `Value::Empty` into `Number(0)`. So the function result was already 0 before `ISBLANK`, `&` or `CONCATENATE` saw it. `INDEX` doesn't do that, which is why it behaved correctly.

## What changed
- VLOOKUP, HLOOKUP, LOOKUP (vector and array forms) and single-cell XLOOKUP results return the empty value unchanged. The final-result coercion in `calc/src/recalc.rs` (Empty → 0) still makes a bare `=VLOOKUP(...)` display 0, as in Excel.
- Arithmetic is unaffected (`VLOOKUP(...)+1` still treats the blank as 0, tested).
- `formulas.evaluate` / `gridcraft-cli eval` don't apply the final-result coercion (same as `=INDEX(...)` or `=A1` of an empty cell today), so a bare lookup of an empty cell now prints blank there instead of 0.

## Tests
- `calc::tests::lookup_of_an_empty_cell_stays_blank`: the reporter's D1–D6 cases plus HLOOKUP, a bare lookup that still shows 0, and `+1` arithmetic.
- `functions` VLOOKUP unit test updated (empty target → `Value::Empty`).
- `cargo test -p gridcraft-calc`, `cargo test -p gridcraft-functions`, `cargo clippy -p gridcraft-calc -p gridcraft-functions --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`.

## Not done
- PR #208 (lookup indexes) touches the lookup path; if it lands first it may need the same change.

## Unverified
- Expected values are taken from the issue's Excel for Mac 16.78 observations. HLOOKUP was not in the report; I assumed it behaves like VLOOKUP (needs confirmation in Excel).

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: Grid: merged ranges draw their right and bottom borders (#376)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #376

## Root cause
The grid painted a merged area with the borders of its anchor (top-left) cell only. Excel stores a merged range's outline on the cells along each edge: the right border on the last column's cells, the bottom border on the last row's cells. The anchor carries only `left` and `top`, so a boxed merge rendered as an open "Γ".

## What changed
- `crates/ui-egui/src/grid.rs`: a merged area's outline is drawn edge cell by edge cell (`merged_edges`): top/left from the first row/column, bottom/right from the last row/column, one segment per visible cell, limited to the visible rows and columns (whole-column merges stay cheap). Table-style and conditional-format borders still apply because each edge cell goes through the same `look()`. Diagonals still come from the anchor.
- The PDF/print path already read the right/bottom edge from the edge cells, so the screen now matches it.
- ROADMAP progress log row.

## Tests
- `crates/ui-egui/tests/borders.rs::merged_range_draws_the_outline_from_its_edge_cells`: Thick Outside Borders on B2:E5, merge, then checks the painted segments form all four sides (4 per side).
- Opened the issue's openpyxl workbook in the offscreen snapshot: closed thick box around B2:E5.

Commands: `cargo test -p gridcraft-ui-egui --test borders`, `cargo clippy -p gridcraft-ui-egui --lib --tests -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt -p gridcraft-ui-egui -- --check`.

## Not done
- If a file puts the right/bottom border only on the anchor cell (not what Excel writes), that edge is not drawn, as in Excel's model where it would lie inside the merge (needs confirmation in Excel).
- Dashed styles restart their pattern per cell segment.

title: Grid: render Shrink to fit (#375)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #375

## Root cause
`shrinkToFit` was already read from and written to XLSX (`Alignment::shrink`) and honoured by the PDF/print renderer, but the on-screen grid ignored it: too-wide text overflowed or was clipped, and numbers were replaced with `####`.

## What changed
- `crates/ui-egui/src/grid.rs`: for single-line, unrotated cells with Shrink to fit (not Fill alignment / repeat-fill formats), content wider than the cell's room (cell or merged area, minus padding and indent) is laid out in a proportionally smaller font (`shrink_font`). Shrunk content no longer spills, is no longer clipped, and numbers are not turned into `####`.
- XLSX attribute unchanged (already round-trips; covered by the existing round-trip test).
- ROADMAP progress log row.

## Tests
- New `crates/ui-egui/tests/shrink_to_fit.rs`: shrunk text is drawn smaller than an unshrunk twin and fits column A; a `#,##0` number with Shrink to fit shows its digits in a smaller font while its unshrunk twin shows `####`.
- Offscreen snapshot of the issue's `shrink.xlsx`: A1 smaller inside A, A2 spills, A4:D4 sentence fully visible and centred, B6 shows `0:00:00`.

Commands: `cargo test -p gridcraft-ui-egui --test shrink_to_fit`, `cargo clippy -p gridcraft-ui-egui --lib --test shrink_to_fit -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt -p gridcraft-ui-egui -- --check`.

## Not done / unverified
- General-format numbers still pick their digit count from the column width before shrinking (Excel's exact interplay of General rounding and shrink needs confirmation in Excel).
- Wrapped or rotated cells ignore Shrink to fit (Excel disables shrink when wrap is on).
- A 3% slack is applied to the computed size to absorb glyph-advance rounding, so shrunk text can be marginally smaller than Excel's.

title: Windows: compile DirectX 12 shaders with FXC, no DXC runtime needed (#339, #354)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #339, fixes #354

## Root cause
wgpu 30's default DirectX 12 shader compiler, `Dx12Compiler::Auto`, loads the first `dxcompiler.dll` the DLL search path finds. GridCraft ships none, so that is another program's copy (Windows SDK, an Edge/WebView folder, anything on `PATH`). Without a matching `dxil.dll` next to it, DXC emits `warning: DXIL signing library (dxil.dll,libdxil.so) not found`. wgpu-hal treats any non-empty DXC error blob as a compile error, so its `indirect_validation` compute pipeline fails, the device is lost and eframe exits with `Parent device is lost` before the first frame (the log in #339). #354 describes the same failure on Windows 11 / DX12 and points at the same code (`graphics.rs` DX12 default, `graphics::configure` in `main.rs`).

Shipping `dxil.dll` alone would not help: #339 shows a mismatched pair still fails, and a stray `dxcompiler.dll` on `PATH` would still be the one loaded. Shipping a matched pair would add native Microsoft binaries to the MSI/zip. Same analysis and fix as storytold/lightcraft#484 (#471 there), adapted here.

## What changed
- `apps/gridcraft/src/graphics.rs`: new `dx12_compiler()`: `WGPU_DX12_COMPILER` if set (for troubleshooting: `dxc`, `staticdxc`, `auto`, `fxc`), else **FXC** (`d3dcompiler_47.dll`, part of Windows, no extra DLL). `configure_backends` applies it to the wgpu instance eframe creates, so both the first start and the DirectX 12 / OpenGL retry from #315 use it.
- The retry from #315 (already on main) also catches this error (`eframe::Error::Wgpu` before the app is created) and falls back to OpenGL. With FXC the DirectX 12 start shouldn't fail this way in the first place.
- README (Windows troubleshooting), `docs/hardware-parity.md`, one ROADMAP progress row.

## Tests
- New `graphics::tests::dx12_compiles_shaders_with_fxc_unless_asked`: FXC by default, an env choice wins, eframe's own default is `Auto` and the configured instance uses FXC.
- `cargo test -p gridcraft --bin gridcraft graphics` (5 pa…

author: vangel76
body:

`sheetView topLeftCell` was parsed into `Sheet::view_top_left`, but the grid's scroll state (`SheetApp::views`) always started at zero, so every sheet opened at A1. The current scroll was also never handed back to the model, so a save wrote whatever the file had been opened with.
