title: Review: Protect Sheet passwords use Excel-compatible hashes, kept in XLSX (#346)
author: vangel76
body:
Refs #346. **Stacked on #384**, which adds the shared hash/XLSX helpers; the first commit here is #384's. Review only the commits after it, or wait for #384 to land.

## Root cause
- Protect Sheet stored its password as an internal FNV hash (`SheetProtection.password_hash: Option<u64>`), and the XLSX writer never wrote it, so a saved protected sheet lost its password.
- On import, an Excel sheet password (`sheetProtection password=` / `hashValue=`) was dropped with a warning, so anyone could unprotect such a sheet.

## What changed
- **Model:** `SheetProtection.password: Option<PasswordHash>`, the Excel-compatible hash from #308. The old `u64` stays as `legacy_password_hash` (serde name `password_hash`), so GridCraft JSON workbooks saved before still load and their password still verifies. It is never written for new passwords.
- **Engine:** Protect Sheet hashes with salted SHA-512 (spin count 100000). Unprotect Sheet verifies it; a wrong or missing password, or a hash that can't be checked, is refused. Protect Sheet on a sheet that already has a password is refused (unprotect first), so re-protecting can't drop the password. The sheet-tab menu offers Unprotect Sheet… on a protected sheet, like the ribbon.

title: Draw the outline band for grouped rows and columns (#373)
author: itrycodinganditsbad
body:
Fixes #373

Grouping rows or columns set their outline level, but the grid never drew it. There was no band, no bracket, no − / + and no level buttons, and Show Detail / Hide Detail couldn't be reached from the UI.

What changed:

- Grid: an outline band sits left of the row headers and above the column headers, sized by the deepest level. It's hidden when the sheet has no outline. Each expanded group gets a bracket, and its summary row or column (below / right of the detail) gets a − / + button. The level buttons 1…n+1 sit in the corner. Clicking − / + runs `data.hideDetail` / `data.showDetail` with the group's lines and level. A level button runs a new `data.showLevels {rows?, cols?}` command. All of them undo. Frozen panes and right-to-left sheets are handled.
- Engine: `engine::outline` works out the groups. Hide Detail now marks the summary line `collapsed`, so the + is saved to XLSX. Show Detail keeps inner groups collapsed if the user collapsed them separately. Hide Detail on a summary row collapses the group above it. Group / Ungroup take `by: rows|cols`. The specs list the Windows shortcuts, Alt+Shift+Right / Left, so the command list no longer advertises Cmd+Shift+K as if it worked on Windows.
- Show Detail and Hide Detail are on the Data tab (Outline group) and in the native Data menu, with translations.
- `keymap::lookup` now reads arrows, Page Up/Down, Home, End, Insert and Delete by their logical key. With Num Lock off, the numpad versions of these keys used to show up as Num6 / Num3 etc.

title: Web & UI: local system font loading via Local Font Access API and ribbon integration
author: GhostMitra
body:
### Summary
Rework of local system font loading built on top of PR #9's bound-family architecture:

1. **Explicit Action Only**: Completely removed all capture-phase gesture listeners on `window`/`document`/`canvas`. Local font access (`queryLocalFonts()`) is requested exclusively when the user explicitly clicks the **"Load System Fonts…"** button in the ribbon font picker.
2. **Bounded Memory & On-Demand Fetching**: During the initial scan, only font metadata (`Face::new_web`) is indexed into the font catalog. Binary font blobs are fetched asynchronously via `font.blob()` and `arrayBuffer()` **only** for families actively used in the open workbook (`SheetApp::used_fonts()`).
3. **No Panic Risk / Bound-Family Registry**: Integrated with the bound-family registry (`fonts::is_bound`, `fonts::set_bound`, `theme::font_definitions_with`). In-memory font bytes are stored in `store_face_bytes` and bound via `bind_faces`. Any unbound font safely falls back to standard `CELL`/`SERIF`/`MONO` without panicking.
4. **UI Truncation**: Applied `truncate_with_ellipsis` to prevent font picker dropdown text overflow.

### Verification

title: File: desktop Print opens the system PDF viewer, Save As offers PDF/CSV/HTML (#370, #343)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #370
Fixes #343

## Root cause
- **Print on the desktop:** since #209, every UI print path (Ctrl+P, title bar More › Print, macOS File › Print, the Print button on File › Print) runs `print_now`, which hands the PDF to `Services::print`. Only the web build sets that hook, so on Windows/Linux/macOS the PDF was built and dropped: nothing happened.
- **Properties (macOS menu):** File › Properties… ran `file.properties` with no fields, which changes nothing and shows nothing.
- **Save As formats:** the desktop save picker always proposed `Book.xlsx` and listed no PDF type. `file.save`/`file.saveAs` with a `.pdf` path fell through to the XLSX writer: the file held XLSX bytes and became the workbook's file.

## What changed
- `apps/gridcraft`: implements `Services::print`. The PDF is written to the temporary folder under a fresh name and opened with the system's default PDF viewer (`open` / `explorer` / `xdg-open`), whose Print command opens the printer dialog. The save picker now uses the suggested name's type (`.pdf`, `.csv`, `.html`, `.xlsx`) and lists that filter first, so Export › Create PDF no longer proposes `Book.xlsx`.
- macOS menu: Properties… opens File › Info (title, subject, author…).
- Engine: `file.save` / `file.saveAs` with a `.pdf` path delegate to `file.exportPdf`. The workbook keeps its own file and dirty state (like CSV/HTML). Spec text updated.
- File › Save As: new **Save as type** chooser (Excel Workbook, CSV UTF-8, Web Page, PDF). xlsx goes through the Save dialog as before; the others go through the existing export path (save picker on the desktop, download on the web). Strings are in all 8 catalogs.

## Tests

title: Keyboard: Shift+Space and Ctrl+Space select without starting an edit (#338)
author: vangel76
body:
Refs #338

**Root cause**
- Shift+Space selected the row, but the OS also sends `Text(" ")`; the grid treated it as typing and called `begin_edit(" ")`.
- Ctrl+Space was bound to `m.command` only, which on macOS is Cmd (Spotlight). Excel for Mac uses Control+Space.

**Changes**
- `grid.rs`: Text events are ignored in the same frame as a pressed key with Ctrl/Cmd (no Alt, so AltGr text still works) or Shift+Space.
- `keymap.rs`: Space bindings moved into `lookup`: Shift+Space = row; Ctrl+Space (Windows/Linux) and Control+Space (Mac) = column; Cmd+Space is left unbound.
- Docs: ui-parity revision row, one ROADMAP row.

**Tests / commands**
- `keyboard_shortcuts`: Key(Space)+Text(" ") with Shift selects the row, with Ctrl selects the column, neither starts an edit; plain typing still edits; per-platform `lookup` test (incl. Cmd+Space unbound).
- `cargo test -p gridcraft-ui-egui --test keyboard_shortcuts`, `cargo clippy -p gridcraft-ui-egui --lib --test keyboard_shortcuts -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt -p gridcraft-ui-egui -- --check`.

**Not done**
- The "other shortcuts not working" part of #338 depends on the reporter's answer. Windows-only checks of the OS-level text events are not done.

**Unverified**
- Mac untested (Control+Space per Microsoft's published Mac list, from memory of the list, not re-checked on a Mac). Real OS event order (Key before Text) is assumed; the fix checks the whole frame so order does not matter.

title: XLOOKUP: return a reference when the result range is one
author: nihilist-narwhal
body:
XLOOKUP returned only values, so `SUM(B1:XLOOKUP("c",A1:A4,B1:B4))` and `CELL("address",XLOOKUP(…))` gave `#VALUE!`. With one lookup value over single-area ranges of matching length, the evaluator now returns the matching row or column of the result range, found with the library XMATCH; other cases go to the library XLOOKUP as before.

Returning the reference also keeps an empty target blank for XLOOKUP (`ISBLANK` TRUE, no `0` in concatenation), which overlaps #379 for that one function; whichever lands second keeps both.

title: Data validation: relative formulas, checked with the value being entered
author: nihilist-narwhal
body: A Custom rule `=A1>10` on A1:A9 rejected 20 typed into A1, because it ran against the old value, and typing into A5 also checked A1. Rule formulas are now relative to the range's first cell, as conditional formatting already is, and see the value being entered. The same goes for the formula bounds of the other types: `<= B1` on C1:C9 now compares C2 with B2.

title: Defined names: relative references follow the cell that uses the name
author: nihilist-narwhal
body:
A name without `$` was evaluated as if absolute: `LeftCell` defined from B2 as `=Sheet1!A2` gave A2 wherever it was used. Excel stores such references relative to A1, as `Sheet1!XFD1` (wrapping at the sheet's edges), and moves them by the using cell's offset; in Excel for Mac, `=LeftCell` in C10 gives B10, and on Sheet2 it still reads Sheet1. `formulas.defineName` now takes relative references as seen from the active cell, as the Name Manager does, and stores them relative to A1.

#208 resets its evaluator `shift` inside names, so whichever lands second needs to combine the two.

title: XLSX: write the _xlfn. prefix for GROUPBY, PIVOTBY, ENCODEURL and the REGEX functions
author: nihilist-narwhal
body: GROUPBY, PIVOTBY, ENCODEURL, REGEXTEST, REGEXEXTRACT and REGEXREPLACE were missing from `FUTURE_FUNCTIONS`, so they were saved without the prefix newer functions carry in files and Excel does not recognise them. Found by saving a call to each function and listing the names written unprefixed.

title: INDEX: arrays of row and column numbers pick a value each
author: nihilist-narwhal
body: `INDEX(A1:C3,{1;3},{1,3})` gave one value, and `SUM(INDEX(A1:C3,{1,2,3},2))` summed one cell. Arrays of positions now return the value at each position, broadcast like other lifted arguments. A 0 inside such an array gives `#CALC!` in that cell.

title: Drawing: text box formatting — run size/bold/font/outline, alignment, anchor, no outline (#377)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #377

## Root cause
The shape model only had `fill`, `line` and plain `text`. The reader dropped `a:rPr`, `a:pPr algn`, `a:bodyPr anchor` and `spPr/a:ln/a:noFill`. As a result, text boxes were drawn at a fixed 14 px in black, in the top-left corner, with a grey border whenever the line colour was unset.

## What changed
- `crates/model`: `Shape::format: ShapeFormat` (`#[serde(default)]`, so old JSON still loads). It holds `no_line`, `font_size` (pt), `bold`, `italic`, `font`, `text_color`, `text_outline` (colour, width in pt), `align` and `anchor`. Alignment and anchor are `Option`: `None` keeps each shape kind's default (text boxes: left/top; other shapes: centred).
- `crates/xlsx/src/drawing.rs`:
  - Reads the shape-outline `noFill` from `spPr/a:ln` and the run properties from `a:rPr`, each looked up under its own parent.
  - `sz` is in hundredths of a point. The outline `w` is in EMU.
  - Theme typefaces (`+mn-lt`) are ignored.
  - On save it writes them back in schema order: `bodyPr anchor`, `pPr algn`, `rPr sz/b/i` with `a:ln`, `a:solidFill`, `a:latin`, and `<a:ln><a:noFill/></a:ln>`.
- `crates/ui-egui/src/chartview.rs`: shape text is laid out with its size, typeface (through the cell font families), bold/italic, colour, alignment and vertical anchor, and clipped to the box. A shape with no outline draws no border.
- `crates/engine/src/cmd/print.rs`: PDF export uses the same size, font, colour, alignment and anchor, and the no-outline flag.
- ROADMAP progress log row.

## Tests
- `crates/xlsx/src/tests/fixtures.rs::text_box_formatting_is_read_and_written`: the issue's drawing XML is read (54 pt, bold, Arial Black, white text with a 1.5 pt black outline, centred, middle, no outline) and survives a write/read round trip.

title: UI fonts: formula bar falls back to the cell font, so Hebrew isn't boxes (#349)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #349

## Root cause
Cells and interface text use different font chains. Cells use `sys-cell` (Arial on the reporter's Mac, which includes Hebrew), then egui's defaults, then the script fallback faces. The formula bar, name box and dialogs use `sys-ui` (SF on macOS, no Hebrew), then egui's defaults, then the same script faces.

On the reporter's Mac no Hebrew fallback face was found: `hebrew()` looks for `Supplemental/Arial Hebrew.ttf` and `Lucida Grande.ttc`. So the cell drew the text and the formula bar drew egui's replacement boxes.

## What changed
- `crates/ui-egui/src/theme.rs`: the interface families (UI, UI bold, the default proportional family, serif, mono) now carry the cell face right before the script fallback faces. Anything a cell can draw, the interface can draw too. Latin text still uses the UI font, because the cell face only catches glyphs the UI font lacks.
- The macOS Hebrew candidates now also include `/System/Library/Fonts/ArialHB.ttc`, `SFHebrew.ttf` and `LucidaGrande.ttc`. The old paths are kept.
- ROADMAP progress log row.

## Tests
- `theme::tests::interface_families_fall_back_to_the_cell_font`: a structural test that does not depend on which fonts the machine has. Each interface chain must contain the cell face, ahead of the script faces. The existing `fallback_faces_are_appended_to_every_family` still holds: the script faces remain the tail of every chain.

Commands: `cargo test -p gridcraft-ui-egui --lib theme::`, `cargo clippy -p gridcraft-ui-egui --lib --tests -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt -p gridcraft-ui-egui -- --check`.

title: Headers and footers: first-page and even-page variants, Insert › Header & Footer edits in place (#344)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #344

## Root cause
- The Header & Footer button under **Insert** opened a dialog where you type codes (`&L…&C…&R`). That is easy to miss and isn't how Excel works. In-place editing in Page Layout view only arrived with #334 (after 0.5.0).

- PDF / print: the sheet's first page, even pages and the rest each print their own pair.
- Page Layout view: each page shows its own pair. Clicking edits that pair. The header and footer presets write to it. The Header & Footer tab has **Different First Page** and **Different Odd & Even Pages** check boxes.
- `pageLayout.headerFooter` accepts `differentFirst`, `differentOddEven`, `firstHeader`, `firstFooter`, `evenHeader` and `evenFooter`, plus `page: odd|even|first` for one-section edits, and returns them.

title: macOS: build the DMG with hdiutil create so the app passes codesign --strict
author: itrycodinganditsbad
body:
Fixes #246.

`hdiutil makehybrid -hfs` puts a `com.apple.FinderInfo` on every file it writes into the image. The app is signed before that, so GridCraft.app inside the released DMG, and any `ditto` copy of it, fails `codesign --verify --deep --strict` with "resource fork, Finder information, or similar detritus not allowed". The script only re-checked the DMG's own signature after imaging, so this went unnoticed.

This is the fix PdfCraft and LightCraft already shipped (https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/pull/823, https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/pull/959), ported to `packaging/macos/package.sh`:

- The image is built with `hdiutil create -srcfolder … -fs HFS+ -format UDZO` instead of `makehybrid` + `convert`. `create` attaches a device while it copies and can hit "Resource busy" on CI runners, so it gets up to five tries with growing pauses.
- `xattr -cr` on the bundle before signing, so nothing picked up during the build ends up under the signature.
- After the DMG is signed, the script mounts it read-only and runs `codesign --verify --deep --strict` on the app inside and on a `ditto` copy of it, plus `spctl --assess` on the copy when notarizing. Any failure stops the release and prints the app's xattrs.
- The volume name stays `GridCraft` and `.DS_Store` / `.background` are copied as before, so the window layout is unchanged.
- `packaging/macos/dmg/README.md` no longer says the DMG is built with `makehybrid`.

Testing: I don't have a Mac, so this was not run. I checked the script with `bash -n` and shellcheck 0.11 (clean) and compared it line by line with the PdfCraft change, which was verified on macOS (the new gate passes, and fails with the old `makehybrid` lines put back). The release workflow's macOS job is what will actually exercise it; the new check after imaging makes that job fail loudly if something is off.

title: Refuse formulas with the wrong argument count on entry (#363)
author: shrshk
body:
Fixes #363.

## Problem

`=DATEDIF(start, end)` was stored and showed `#VALUE!`. DATEDIF has no default unit; it needs three
arguments. The same happens for every built-in: `=SUM()`, `=DATE(2024,1)` and `=LEFT("a",1,2,3)`
are all accepted and evaluate to `#VALUE!`, with nothing telling the user what was wrong. The
reporter couldn't find out which unit values exist.

## Change

- `engine` (`input_to_cell`): after parsing, walk the formula. A call to a registered function with
  fewer than `min_args` or more than `max_args` arguments is refused with
  `<NAME> has too few|many arguments. Use <signature>`, e.g.
  `DATEDIF has too few arguments. Use DATEDIF(start_date, end_date, unit)`. The cell is unchanged.
- Functions the registry holds are checked, including IF, IFS, IFERROR, IFNA, CHOOSE, SWITCH and
  INDEX. Special forms the evaluator handles without a registry entry (LET, LAMBDA, OFFSET,
  INDIRECT, SUBTOTAL, AGGREGATE, TEXT, ROW, COLUMN, the LAMBDA helpers and a few more), defined
  LAMBDA names and unknown functions (`#NAME?`) are skipped and keep showing `#VALUE!` for a
  wrong count, as before.
- One behaviour change beyond `#VALUE!`: the evaluator accepted `=IF(TRUE)` (one argument) and
  showed `TRUE`, while the registry gives IF a minimum of 2. Entry now refuses it, as Excel does
  (see below). IF's signature still shows `[value_if_true]` as optional; I left that text alone.
- Paste and Find & Replace already turn input that fails entry into text; a wrong count follows
  that same path. Files are not affected (entry only).
- Text to Columns drops a split part that fails entry (`data.rs`, `unwrap_or(None)`), as it already
  does for a syntax error: `x;=DATEDIF(1,2)` splits into `x` and an empty cell, where it used to
  store the formula showing `#VALUE!`. Keeping such a part as text, like paste, would change the
  syntax-error case too, so I left it.
- DATEDIF's description keeps its sentence and adds the units: `Y, M, D, MD, YM or YD`.
- `ui`: the argument …

title: CLI: check subcommand - cached-value calc oracle and XLSX round-trip fidelity on any corpus
author: neilcawse
body:
## What changed
New `gridcraft-cli check <file-or-dir>... [--json] [--tolerance 1e-9] [--max-report 20]` (`apps/gridcraft-cli/src/check.rs`). It measures calculation correctness and file fidelity on any set of `.xlsx`/`.xlsm` files and writes nothing next to them.

- **Calc oracle.** Excel stores its own result next to every formula. `check` reads each file and keeps those cached values, recalculates every formula with GridCraft, and compares the two. Numbers must agree within a relative tolerance (absolute when the magnitude is below 1). Errors must be the same kind. Text and logicals must match exactly.
  - Cells with no cached value (including `fullCalcOnLoad` files from libraries that don't calculate, such as xlsxwriter) are counted as *no oracle*. Volatile formulas, and everything downstream of them in the dependency graph, are counted as *volatile*. Neither is compared.
  - Each mismatch lists the cell, formula, expected and actual values, and the functions it calls. Mismatches are also summed by function, where *primary* means none of the cell's precedents mismatch, so that function is the likely culprit. They are also summed by type signature (e.g. `number → #SPILL!`), which tends to group one root cause.
- **Round trip.** The recalculated workbook is saved with GridCraft's XLSX writer, then read back. The package is validated against the things Excel would "repair": missing content types, dangling relationship targets, duplicate relationship ids. Then sheets, values, formulas, per-cell number formats, merges, names, tables, conditional formats, validations, charts, comments, hyperlinks and pivots are compared with the original.
- `--json` gives a machine-readable report for CI or scripts. Usage is documented in `docs/cli.md`.

## Why
The parity docs count which functions exist, not whether they return what Excel returns. This gives a repeatable number from real Excel-saved files without needing Excel installed. It's clean-room: it only uses values Excel alr…

title: XLSX: legacy formulas (no dynamic-array `cm`) open with Excel's implicit `@` and calculate like Excel
author: neilcawse
body:
Follow-up to #64 / #267. #267 writes `@` as `_xlfn.SINGLE` in a dynamic-array formula, and its test notes that dropping the `@` instead "would need the reader to put it back on legacy formulas". This PR adds that reader side. The write side of #64 is already on main, so this PR does not close it.

## What changed
- **Read.** A cell formula saved without dynamic-array metadata (no `cm` attribute) and not entered as a Ctrl+Shift+Enter array is a legacy formula. Excel evaluates it with implicit intersection, and dynamic-array Excel shows it with `@` inserted at those places. GridCraft now does the same. After names and tables are read, `array_formula::apply_legacy` inserts `@` wherever a reference that may cover several cells meets a single-value parameter, an operator, or the cell result. Examples: `TANH(A1:A3)` → `TANH(@A1:A3)`, `MYUDF(A1:A3)` → `@MYUDF(A1:A3)`. `SUM(A1:A3)` and `SUMPRODUCT(A1:A3*B1:B3)` are left alone. The calc engine then gives the legacy result with no second evaluator. Dynamic-array formulas (`cm`) and CSE arrays are read as written.
- **Write.** `array_formula::export` replaces `needs_array` and has three outcomes:
  - unchanged;
  - dynamic (`cm` + single-cell array ref, as before);
  - legacy: every `@` in the formula is one legacy Excel would imply, so the formula is written without them and without `cm`.

  So a legacy formula read from a file saves back as it was read. Any other `@` is still written as `_xlfn.SINGLE` in a dynamic-array formula (`@(A1:A3*2)`, `SQRT(@A1)`, `@SUM(A1:A3)`).
- **Formula parser.** `_xlfn.SINGLE(A1:A3*2)` reads as `@(A1:A3*2)` (parenthesised), not as `@A1:A3*2`. `fmla.rs` writes `@(x)` back as `_xlfn.SINGLE(x)`.
- **Layering.** The classification needs to know which names are built-in functions and which parameters take a single value, and that knowledge lives in `gridcraft-functions`. Format crates may not depend on that crate, so `gridcraft-xlsx` gains `FunctionInfo` (two `fn` pointers) supplied by the caller:

title: Numfmt: fraction literals and zero fractions, `?` pads thousands separator, TEXT booleans through text section
author: neilcawse
body:
## What changed
Fixes in `crates/numfmt`, shared by `TEXT()` and cell display, found by comparing against Excel-cached `TEXT()` results in number- and text-format test workbooks (352 TEXT cells: 226 mismatched before, 0 after).

- Fraction sections with literal text: `parse.rs` now treats a section as a fraction when literal text sits between the bar and the denominator (`#/ #`, `# ?=/=?`). `render.rs` splits a fraction section into `[whole] [sep] num [lit] / [lit] den` and keeps the literals between the parts (`|#\:#=/=#|` with 23.75 gives `|23:3=/=4|`).
- When the whole part shows no digit, its separator disappears, or becomes spaces when the whole part or the numerator has a `?` (`|#\:#/#|` with 0.75 gives `|3/4|`).
- Zero fractions: when the fractional part is zero and the numerator has no `0` placeholder, the separator, numerator, bar and denominator are hidden (spaces if any part has a `?`) and the whole part shows at least `0`. With a `0` in the numerator it shows `0/1` (`|#\:0=/=#|` with 0 gives `|0=/=1|`).
- Literal text before the bar keeps the improper fraction (`|#_#/#|` with 3.75 gives `|15 /4|`).
- `0` denominator placeholders zero pad on the left (`/000` gives `/004`).
- A blank `?` placeholder also pads the thousands separator it would have carried with a space (`?,?????????` with 1234567 gives `    1,234,567`).
- `TEXT()` with a boolean now runs `TRUE`/`FALSE` through the text section instead of returning it as is (`TEXT(TRUE,";;;\@@\@")` = `@TRUE@`). Number formats without a text section still return `TRUE`/`FALSE`.

## Tests
New tests in `crates/numfmt/src/tests.rs`:
- `fractions_with_literals`: 45 cases (literals around the bar, hidden whole part, zero fractions, `0` in the numerator, zero-padded denominators, literal before the bar).
- `question_mark_pads_thousands_separator`: 7 cases.
- `text_fn`: 9 boolean cases through the text section.

Expected values are Excel results as cached in the test workbooks.

title: Functions: MODE/VALUE/SUMPRODUCT text args, ADDRESS [Book]Sheet, Excel-style lookup bisection, SUBTOTAL skips filtered rows
author: neilcawse
body:
## What changed
Function fixes found by comparing GridCraft against Excel-cached formula results in test workbooks. One PR because they came out of the same comparison run; the parts are independent and grouped below.

### MODE / MODE.SNGL / MODE.MULT (`crates/functions/src/stat.rs`)
- New `mode_numbers`: inside multi-cell ranges and arrays only numbers count (as before), but direct text (even numeric text like `"1"`) and a single-cell reference to text or a blank cell give `#VALUE!`. Arguments are read left to right, so the first error wins (`MODE(1,1,#DIV/0!,"1")` is `#DIV/0!`, `MODE("1",1,#DIV/0!)` is `#VALUE!`).

### VALUE (`crates/functions/src/text.rs`)
- `VALUE("")` and whitespace-only text are now `#VALUE!` (they returned 0). A blank cell still reads as 0.

### SUMPRODUCT (`crates/functions/src/math.rs`)
- Text in a scalar argument (a literal or a single-cell reference) is `#VALUE!`. Text inside arrays and multi-cell ranges still counts as 0.

### ADDRESS (`crates/functions/src/lookup.rs`)
- A `[Book]Sheet` sheet_text is judged by its parts, so `ADDRESS(2,3,3,TRUE,"[Book1]Sheet1")` gives `[Book1]Sheet1!$C2` instead of `'[Book1]Sheet1'!$C2`. Names with spaces are still quoted (`'[My Book]Sheet1'!$A$1`, `'EXCEL SHEET'!R2C3`).

### Approximate match: VLOOKUP / HLOOKUP / LOOKUP / MATCH (`crates/functions/src/lookup.rs`)
- `bsearch_last` now bisects the whole vector the way Excel does, instead of first filtering to entries of the needle's type and searching those. A probe of a different type moves to the nearest same-type entry below it in the window (or the window moves up past it). An equal probe ends the search, then the run of equal entries after it is taken, so sorted duplicates give the last one. On unsorted, mixed-type data the answer now matches Excel's (e.g. `VLOOKUP(534, {"INTEGRAL";0;1;2;534;9999999999;-9999999999}, …)` finds 534). No allocation; linear work in the worst case, including long runs of trailing blanks.

title: Formulas: trim-reference operators (A1:.E10, A1.:E10, A1.:.E10); read unbracketed [[#This Row],Col]
author: neilcawse
body:
Follow-up to #297 (TRIMRANGE), which listed the trim-reference operators under "Not done".

## What changed
- **Trim references.** The lexer now produces a `Trim` token for `:.` (trailing), `.:` (leading) and `.:.` (both) when it sits between two range ends. That covers cells (`A1:.E10`), whole columns (`A:.A`, `$A.:.$C`), whole rows (`1:.5`, `$1.:$5`) and sheet-qualified ranges (`Sheet2!$A$1:.B9`, `'Q1 2026'!A1:.B2`). Decimals (`1.5+.5`), dotted names (`my.name`) and dotted sheet names (`Q1.2026!A1:B2`) keep their old meaning. Malformed forms (`A1.:`, `.:A1`, `A1:.:B2`) are parse errors.
- The parser builds `Expr::Unary(UnOp::Trim(TrimMode), range)`; `TrimMode` is exported from `gridcraft-formula`. The printer writes the operator back in A1 and R1C1 (`SUM(RC:.R[1]C[1])`). Insert/delete adjustment, relative shifting and `references()` go through the inner range, as for `:`.
- **Evaluation.** `crates/calc/src/trimrange.rs` gains `trim_ref`, which evaluates the range and runs it through the same trimming code as `TRIMRANGE(range, code, code)` (1 leading, 2 trailing, 3 both). The result spills and follows edits to the full range. An all-blank range gives `#CALC!`, as TRIMRANGE does.
- **XLSX.** On save, a trim reference is written as `_xlfn.TRIMRANGE(range,code,code)`. Public docs do not say how Excel spells the operator in files. On read, both that form and the `_xlfn._TRO_ALL` / `_TRO_LEADING` / `_TRO_TRAILING(range)` call forms parse back to the operator. A `_TRO_*` call on something other than a range prints as the equivalent `TRIMRANGE(x,n,n)`. `array_formula.rs` treats the operator as a reference operator, like `#`.
- **Unbracketed `[[#This Row],Col]`.** Some writers (xlsxwriter, for example) write `[@Units]` as `[[#This Row],Units]`, with the column name unbracketed. That form now parses, with or without a table name, and prints canonically as `[@Units]` / `Sales[@Units]`. title: Calc: iterative calculation for circular references (Maximum Iterations, Maximum Change)
author: neilcawse
body:
## What changed

Enable Iterative Calculation was already read from and written to XLSX (`<calcPr iterate iterateCount iterateDelta>`) and settable through `formulas.calculationOptions`, but the calc engine ignored it: circular references always gave `#CIRC!`. With it on, they now iterate.

- `crates/calc/src/recalc.rs`: with `wb.calc.iterative` on, a formula read while it is being evaluated gives its previous value (from the last iteration, else the value it shows; blank and a stale `#CIRC!` count as 0) instead of `#CIRC!`. The pass records which formulas sit on a loop and which results read a previous value, directly or through other formulas or spilled arrays. After the first pass, those formulas are evaluated again in the same order (each pass reads what it has already produced, Gauss-Seidel style) until no formula on a loop changes by Maximum Change or more, or Maximum Iterations passes are reached. Text, logical and error values count as changed unless equal. Total work is capped at 10,000,000 formula evaluations per recalculation, whatever Maximum Iterations says. With iteration off, behaviour is unchanged (`#CIRC!`).
- The `PassHost` struct literal, which was repeated in three places (recalc, `evaluate_expr`, the `visit_range` test probe), is now `PassHost::new`.
- `crates/model/src/workbook.rs`: `CalcSettings` gains `DEFAULT_ITERATIONS` (100), `DEFAULT_CHANGE` (0.001), `MAX_ITERATIONS` (32,767), `set_max_iterations` (clamps to 1..=32,767) and `set_max_change` (magnitude; ignores NaN/infinite). The XLSX reader and the command use them.
- `formulas.calculationOptions` (`crates/engine/src/cmd/formulas.rs`): changing `iterative`, `maxIterations` or `maxChange` outside manual mode now recalculates the workbook. The result returns all four settings, and the parameter description documents ranges and defaults.

title: File formats: CSV/TSV export writes displayed values; templates and .xlsm saved with their own content types
author: neilcawse
body:
## What changed
- Save As CSV/TSV now writes each cell as it is displayed: number formats applied (dates, currency, percent, fractions, thousands separators, `@` text), formula results, errors and booleans as shown. It never writes column-width `#####` and never applies the grid's General narrowing, so the field holds the whole value. This follows Microsoft's description of Save As CSV/Text ("the text and values as they are displayed in cells", all characters kept). Before this change the export wrote raw values (`46023` instead of `2026-01-01`).
  - `engine::display::value_text` is split out of `cell_text`: it formats the value without the show-formulas branch. A sheet with Show Formulas on still exports values.

The new `XlsxKind::from_path` picks the kind from the extension (case-insensitive; unknown or missing extensions give `.xlsx`). `write_xlsx_as(wb, kind)` writes it.
- The VBA project kept by #6 now follows the kind: the writer adds `xl/vbaProject.bin` only for `.xlsm` and `.xltm` (`XlsxKind::is_macro_enabled`), so `save_bytes` no longer clones the workbook to strip it, and a macro-enabled template keeps its macros. `write_xlsx(wb)` behaves as before: `.xlsm` when the workbook holds a VBA project, `.xlsx` otherwise. title: XLSX: strip _xlpm. from LET/LAMBDA parameters on read, keep line breaks in table columns, allow leading backslash in table names
author: neilcawse
body:
## What changed
Three XLSX round-trip losses, all in `crates/xlsx`:

- **`_xlpm.` LET/LAMBDA parameters.** Excel stores LET/LAMBDA parameter names as `_xlpm.name` in the file. The writer already adds the prefix, but `read_formula` (`sheet_read.rs`) used the raw `<f>` text, so a saved `LET(x,1,x+1)` came back as `_xlfn.LET(_xlpm.x,1,_xlpm.x+1)`. Cell, shared and array formulas now go through `fmla::from_file`, the conversion CF, data validation and names already use. When the formula parses, the stored text is the parser/printer form with `_xlfn.`/`_xlpm.` removed. When it doesn't parse, the text is kept as written. One side effect: cell formula text read from a file is now in printer form (for example, spacing may change) rather than byte-for-byte as stored.
- **Line breaks in table column names.** `table_columns` (`sheet_write.rs`) replaced `\r`/`\n` with spaces in column names. Excel allows a line break in a table header, and the header cell still had the break, so the column name and its header cell disagreed after a save. The name is now written unchanged (XML escaping already handles it).
- **Leading backslash in table names.** `table_name` turned a leading `\` into `_` (or fell back to `TableN`). Excel's rules for names in formulas allow a name to start with a letter, `_` or `\`, so `\_Prime.1` is now kept. Structured references such as `COUNTA(\_Prime.1[Name])` already parsed.

## Tests
- `tests::roundtrip::let_lambda_parameters_drop_xlpm_on_read`: LET, an immediately called LAMBDA and an array MAP/LAMBDA formula are written with `_xlpm.` in the sheet XML and read back with bare parameter names.
- `tests::roundtrip::table_newline_column_and_backslash_name_survive`: a table named `\_Prime.1` with a `Handle\nBars` column keeps both after a round trip, along with the header cell value and a structured reference formula to it.

title: Charts: read, write and draw trendlines
author: neilcawse
body:
## What changed

- **Model** (`crates/model/src/features.rs`): `Series.trendlines: Vec<Trendline>` (`#[serde(default)]`, so older saved state still loads). A `Trendline` holds the kind (linear, exponential, logarithmic, polynomial order 2–6, power, moving average period 2–255), an optional name, forward/backward forecast, an optional set intercept, show-equation and show-R² flags, and line colour, width and dash.

A forecast widens the category or x axis, and the line is clipped to the plot area. Equation and R² labels are drawn in the plot, and the legend gets entries such as "Linear (Sales)". Degenerate data (too few points, constant x, singular system) draws no trendline and does not panic. Each series draws at most `MAX_TRENDLINES` trendlines.

title: Fix AutoFit width for table and AutoFilter dropdowns
author: derechopiano
body:
AutoFit currently measures column header text without accounting for the width of its filter dropdown button. As a result, longer headings such as `Quarterly Revenue` can be partially obscured by the dropdown, particularly when the cells below contain only short values (e.g. `1`).

Reserve dropdown space on visible filter header cells before comparing their widths with body cells. Share that geometry with header text layout and button hit-testing. This covers both tables and ordinary AutoFilters without double-counting overlapping buttons.

The allowance follows observations of Windows Excel 16.0 build 20326: 12.5 points at 100–200% zoom, 25 points at 50%, independent of header row height. Existing approximate font measurement remains unchanged.

Validation:
- Regression tests cover filter/header flags, ordinary and overlapping filters, longer body values, unaffected columns, zoom, row heights, and undo.
- UI tests exercise both the command and real header double-clicks at 50%, 100%, and 200% zoom.
- Native desktop launch and before/after renders were verified with a synthetic workbook.
- `cargo xtask ci`: all seven gates passed; 843 tests passed, 1 ignored. On Windows, the generated parity document was temporarily normalized to LF for its content check; the original checkout was restored without a content change.

title: Open password-encrypted workbooks (Agile and Standard encryption) (#11)
author: LloydNicholson
body:
Follows up #11 (closed by #17, which recognised encrypted workbooks and refused them). Requested by @LloydNicholson.

GridCraft now opens password-protected `.xlsx` workbooks: it asks for the password, decrypts the file and shows the workbook. This PR only opens them. Saving with a password is still to do.

## What changed
- **xlsx: new `crypto` module.** `decrypt(bytes, password)` reads Agile encryption (Excel 2010 onward: AES-128/192/256 in CBC mode, SHA-1/256/384/512) and Standard encryption (Excel 2007: AES with SHA-1) on top of the existing CFB reader. It is clean-room from the public [MS-OFFCRYPTO] spec. `check_encryption(bytes)` tells, without a password, whether any password could open the file. Files no password can open get their real message straight away: RC4, Extensible, certificate-only, rights-management (IRM) and damaged files.
- **Hostile input:**
  - The spin count is capped at 10,000,000.
  - The stated package size is checked against the ciphertext before anything is allocated.
  - Key, block and salt sizes are validated.
  - Every read goes through `get()`.
  - No new non-test code can panic.
- **New dependencies:** RustCrypto `aes` 0.9 and `sha1` 0.11 (pure Rust, MIT OR Apache-2.0, wasm-safe, default features off). xlsx also adds `sha2`, which was already in the workspace.
- **engine:**
  - `io::open_bytes_with_password`, plus the markers `PASSWORD_REQUIRED`, `WRONG_PASSWORD` and `DECRYPTED_NOTICE`.
  - `file.open` takes an optional `password`. Without one, an encrypted workbook returns an error and never opens a dialog.
  - A decrypted workbook gets **no save path**, so Save asks where to save it and never replaces the encrypted original with an unprotected copy.
  - The password stays out of the journal (it was already a secret param) and is never quoted in an error.
- **ui-egui:**
  - A new `openPassword` dialog, with a masked field and the existing Show password toggle.
  - It opens for File › Open, drops, Finder, the web picker and files n…

title: Scatter charts of two unlabelled columns plot the first as X for one series (#428)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #428.

A scatter chart of two plain numeric columns came out as two series, each plotted against its point index, instead of one series with the first column as X and the second as Y.

`series_from_range` only treats the first column as categories when it holds text (or sits under a blank corner cell), which suits column/line charts but not scatter, where the first numeric column is the X values. The new `scatter_x_from_first` helper in `cmd/insert.rs` does what Excel does for scatter: when the block has no category labels, the first series becomes the X values (`categories`) of the remaining ones. Three columns give two series sharing the first column as X; a block laid out in rows uses its first row.

It runs on every path that builds a scatter chart's series from a range:
- `insert.chart` (and the Recommended Charts preview, which goes through `build_chart`),
- `chart.selectData` with a new `range`,
- `chart.switchRowColumn`.

Other chart kinds, and blocks that already have a text label column, are unchanged.

Test: `scatter_of_two_columns_is_one_series_with_the_first_as_x` inserts a scatter chart from `X`/`Y` columns and checks it gets one series, values `B2:B4` and X `A2:A4`. It then checks the same result after Select Data, and after Switch Row/Column on a block laid out in rows. Without the fix, `insert.chart` gives two series.

title: Rotated text follows the cell's alignment
author: itrycodinganditsbad
body:
Fixes #435

Rotated text (for example "up", 90°) was drawn at a fixed anchor: bottom-left for upward text, top-left for downward text. The cell's horizontal and vertical alignment were ignored, so upright text with Middle Align in a tall merged block stayed at the bottom.

The fix adds `rotated_text_pos` in `grid.rs`. It works out the bounding box of the rotated galley, places that box in the cell the same way flat text is placed (Left/Center/Right, Top/Center/Bottom, with pad and indent), and then derives the `TextShape` position from it, since egui rotates around the galley's top-left corner.

Default alignment (General, Bottom) keeps the old placement for ±90° text. Upward text sits at the bottom-left and downward text starts at the top-left, same as before. There is no separate "unset" vertical alignment, so for downward text Bottom still means top. Upward text at other angles (like 45°) with Bottom alignment now sits fully inside the cell. Before, the lower part hung below the bottom border and got clipped.

Tests: unit tests for 90°, -90°, 45° and -45° with every Top/Center/Bottom and Left/Center/Right combination. Each one rotates the galley corners around the returned position and checks the box is in the cell and lines up with the requested edge or the centre. A separate test pins the old default placement, and another covers the issue's case (90°, tall merged block, Middle and Center). The alignment tests failed against the old anchoring. I also checked offscreen snapshots of the issue repro before and after: the text is now centred in A1:A4, and default-aligned up and down text hasn't moved.

title: Release workflow: pass the Azure signing secrets
author: echelon
body:
Since this repo's `release.yml` moved to `storytold/craft-common-actions`, it has passed the Apple and `WINDOWS_CERTIFICATE*` secrets to the shared workflow, but not the six `AZURE_*` secrets that Azure Trusted Signing uses.

The shared workflow's signing jobs run in this repo's `release` environment and read the values from there, but only for names the caller lists. So the next release would have built **unsigned** Windows MSIs and portable zips, with only a warning. craft-launcher 0.3.1 did exactly this, and storytold/craft-launcher#174 fixed it with this same change.

This adds the six names. All twelve secrets are already set in this repo's `release` environment. storytold/craft-common-actions#3 makes release builds fail outright if signing secrets are missing, and fixes the riscv64 `--formats` call. This PR should land first.

`actionlint` passes.
